```sql
  -- caller's profile points at a firm they do not own. Returned rather than
  -- raised so the answer is a value the client can report; nothing is written.
  if exists (
    select 1
      from public.profiles p
     where p.id = v_user_id
       and p.firm_id is not null
       and (not v_has_firm or p.firm_id is distinct from v_firm.id)
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'member_of_another_firm');
  end if;

  if not v_has_firm then
    -- The transition to firm mode is the premium-gated step (Phase 1 item 2).
    if not public.is_premium(v_user_id) then
      return jsonb_build_object('status', 'premium_required');
    end if;

    -- `created_at` is a server instant (`timestamptz`) and takes the column
    -- default: the bigint `v_now` below is epoch ms for the client-facing
    -- `firm_members` stamps only.
    insert into public.firms (
      name, owner_id, subscription_status, subscription_expiry
    )
    select
      v_name,
      v_user_id,
      p.subscription_status,
      p.subscription_expiry
      from public.profiles p
     where p.id = v_user_id
    returning * into v_firm;

    if not found then
      -- No profile row: the sign-up trigger creates one, so this is a bug state,
      -- never something to explain to a user. Raising here rolls the firm back.
      raise exception 'ensure_firm: no profiles row for the caller'
        using errcode = 'P0001';
    end if;

    v_created := true;
  elsif v_name is distinct from v_firm.name then
    update public.firms f
       set name = v_name
     where f.id = v_firm.id
    returning * into v_firm;
  end if;

  -- The conversion itself: firm scope for every policy, owner role for the app.
  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = v_firm.id,
         role = 'owner'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  -- The owner holds every permission explicitly, so `can_edit_firm` /
  -- `can_delete_firm` and the client's cached flags agree with the role.
  insert into public.firm_members (
    firm_id, user_id, role, can_add, can_edit, can_delete,
    synced_at, permissions_synced_at
  )
  values (
    v_firm.id, v_user_id, 'owner', true, true, true, v_now, v_now
  )
  on conflict (firm_id, user_id) do update
    set role = 'owner',
        can_add = true,
        can_edit = true,
        can_delete = true,
        synced_at = excluded.synced_at,
        permissions_synced_at = excluded.permissions_synced_at;

  -- Sharing the diary: every ledger row the owner authored while firm-less
  -- becomes the chamber's (§1). The four case-data tables first, then the six
  -- reference tables — custom rows only, because a built-in row (`is_custom =
  -- false`) has no author and is the globally shared baseline every install
  -- reads — and finally the owner's pending delete requests.
  if v_created then
    foreach v_table in array v_case_tables loop
      execute format(
        'update public.%I t '
        '   set firm_id = $1, '
        '       version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
        '       updated_at = $3 '
        ' where t.user_id = $2 '
        '   and t.firm_id is null',
        v_table
      ) using v_firm.id, v_user_id, v_now;
    end loop;

    foreach v_table in array v_reference_tables loop
      execute format(
        'update public.%I t '
        '   set firm_id = $1, '
        '       version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
        '       updated_at = $3 '
        ' where t.user_id = $2 '
        '   and t.firm_id is null '
        '   and t.is_custom = true',
        v_table
      ) using v_firm.id, v_user_id, v_now;
    end loop;

    -- A resolved request is audit history rather than a ledger row, so only a
    -- pending one follows the owner into his chamber.
    update public.delete_requests t
       set firm_id = v_firm.id,
           version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1,
           updated_at = v_now
     where t.requested_by = v_user_id
       and t.firm_id is null
       and t.status = 'pending';
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ready',
    'firm_id', v_firm.id,
    'name', v_firm.name
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.ensure_firm(text) is
  'Idempotent owner-side firm establishment: creates the caller''s firm (premium-gated at the creation moment), relinks profiles.firm_id/role, upserts the owner''s firm_members row, and shares the caller''s firm-less diary into the new firm (cases, case history, notes, case references, custom reference rows and pending delete requests — tombstones included — each with a version bump and a refreshed updated_at/server_updated_at so every device converges). Refuses a member of another firm. The invite generator (and therefore the app) has no other way to reach firm scope.';

revoke all on function public.ensure_firm(text) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.ensure_firm(text) to authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- push_changes — the scope columns are the server's
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.push_changes(rows jsonb)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  -- Read once: every insert in this batch is scoped to the caller's own firm,
  -- and a profile change mid-batch must not be able to split the batch's scope.
  v_firm_id uuid := public.current_firm_id();
  v_entitled boolean;
  v_n integer;
  v_results jsonb[];
  v_order integer[];
  v_idx integer;
  v_row jsonb;
  v_mutation_id text;
  v_entity_type text;
  v_entity_id text;
  v_operation text;
  v_table text;
  v_payload jsonb;
  v_base_version integer;
  v_existing jsonb;
  v_final jsonb;
  v_new_row jsonb;
  v_old_version integer;
  v_ms bigint;
  v_hash text;
  v_receipt public.mutation_receipts%rowtype;
  v_status text;
  v_error_code text;
  v_message text;
  v_result jsonb;
  v_cols text;
  v_vals text;
  v_bad integer;
  v_has_created_at boolean;
  v_prov jsonb;
  v_hist jsonb;
  v_hist_row jsonb;
  v_child jsonb;
  v_children jsonb;
  v_state text;
  v_msg text;
  -- Delete-review accumulators (Task 20 Phase 4).
  v_target jsonb;
  v_target_type text;
  v_target_table text;
  v_expected integer;
  v_req_status text;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- Batch invariant: the Flutter client always sends one JSON array.
  if rows is null or jsonb_typeof(rows) <> 'array' then
    raise exception 'push_changes: rows must be a JSON array'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  v_n := jsonb_array_length(rows);
  if v_n = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('results', '[]'::jsonb);
  end if;

  v_entitled := public.has_sync_entitlement(v_actor);
  v_ms := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;

  -- One slot per submitted row, so the response is exactly one result per
  -- mutation_id in input order even though processing follows dependency order.
  v_results := array_fill(null::jsonb, array[v_n]);

  select array_agg(i order by r, i)
    into v_order
    from (
      select i,
             public.sync_dependency_rank(
               coalesce(rows -> (i - 1) ->> 'entity_type', '')
             ) as r
        from generate_series(1, v_n) as i
    ) s;

  foreach v_idx in array v_order loop
    v_row := rows -> (v_idx - 1);

    -- Reset every per-mutation accumulator so nothing from the previous
    -- iteration can leak into this one's result.
    v_status := null;
    v_error_code := null;
    v_message := null;
    v_existing := null;
    v_final := null;
    v_new_row := null;
    v_children := null;
    v_hist_row := null;
    v_target := null;
    v_target_type := null;
    v_target_table := null;
    v_expected := null;
    v_req_status := null;

    v_mutation_id := nullif(v_row ->> 'mutation_id', '');
    v_entity_type := nullif(v_row ->> 'entity_type', '');
    v_entity_id := nullif(v_row ->> 'entity_id', '');
    v_operation := nullif(v_row ->> 'operation', '');

    if v_mutation_id is null or v_entity_type is null
       or v_entity_id is null or v_operation is null then
      raise exception
        'push_changes: every row needs mutation_id, entity_type, entity_id and operation'
        using errcode = '22023';
    end if;

    v_table := public.sync_entity_table(v_entity_type);
    v_hash := public.sha256_hex(v_row::text);

    -- Idempotency: a known mutation_id with the same canonical hash returns the
    -- original result and applies nothing; a different hash is refused.
    select * into v_receipt
      from public.mutation_receipts r
     where r.mutation_id = v_mutation_id;
    if found then
      if v_receipt.request_hash = v_hash then
        v_results[v_idx] := v_receipt.result_payload;
      else
        v_results[v_idx] := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', 'mutation_id_reused',
          'message', 'This mutation id was already used with a different payload.'
        );
      end if;
      continue;
    end if;

    -- The implicit savepoint for this logical mutation: a permanent failure
    -- rolls back only this block, while a receipt (written after the block) and
    -- every other mutation survive.
    begin
      if not v_entitled then
        v_status := 'rejected';
        v_error_code := 'entitlement_required';
        v_message := 'Online sync requires an active subscription.';
      elsif v_table is null then
        v_status := 'rejected';
        v_error_code := 'unknown_entity';
        v_message := format('Unknown entity type %s.', v_entity_type);
      else
        -- The scope columns are never taken from a payload (§3.3): `scope_owner_id`
        -- belongs to the dissolve, and `firm_id` is derived below on insert and
        -- preserved on an existing row. Stripping here is what makes both true
        -- for every path at once — insert, update, delete and the delete-review
        -- branch all read this one variable.
        v_payload := coalesce(v_row -> 'payload', '{}'::jsonb)
          - 'scope_owner_id' - 'firm_id';

        -- A payload key that is not a real column is a client validation error,
        -- never a silent no-op.
        select count(*) into v_bad
          from jsonb_object_keys(v_payload) k
         where not exists (
           select 1
             from pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
             join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = a.attrelid
             join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
            where n.nspname = 'public'
              and c.relname = v_table
              and a.attname = k
              and a.attnum > 0
              and a.attisdropped = false
         );
        if v_bad > 0 then
          raise exception 'unknown_column'
            using errcode = '42703',
                  hint = 'The payload names a column that does not exist on the server table.';
        end if;

        v_base_version := nullif(v_row ->> 'base_version', '')::int;

        if v_operation = 'insert' then
          -- Inserts require no existing row.
          execute format(
            'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
            v_table
          ) into v_existing using v_entity_id;

          if v_existing is not null then
            v_status := 'conflict';
            v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
            v_message := 'A row with this id already exists.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          else
            -- Server-owned columns are never taken from the client; the
            -- server_updated_at trigger stamps its own column.
            v_final := v_payload
              - 'server_updated_at' - 'version' - 'last_modified_by';
            if v_table = 'conflict_log' then
              -- The server column is a timestamptz defaulted to server now();
              -- the client's epoch-ms value must not be cast into it.
              v_final := v_final - 'created_at';
            end if;
            v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object(
              'version', 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text,
              -- §1: a chamber account holds chamber rows and nothing else, so a
              -- new row's firm is the caller's own — null for an individual, the
              -- chamber for a member. This is what makes firm mode work at all:
              -- the client's whole-row payload carries its local `firm_id`
              -- (null), and without this derivation a member's case landed as a
              -- personal row inside the chamber, invisible to everybody else.
              'firm_id', v_firm_id
            );
            -- Only a table whose `created_at` is an epoch-ms *integer* column may
            -- receive the fallback: the six reference tables have none, and
            -- `conflict_log.created_at` is a server-owned timestamptz that must
            -- take its own default rather than the client's milliseconds.
            select exists (
              select 1
                from pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
                join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = a.attrelid
                join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
               where n.nspname = 'public'
                 and c.relname = v_table
                 and a.attname = 'created_at'
                 and a.attnum > 0
                 and a.atttypid in ('int8'::regtype, 'int4'::regtype)
            ) into v_has_created_at;
            if v_has_created_at and v_final ->> 'created_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('created_at', v_ms);
            end if;
            if v_final ->> 'updated_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('updated_at', v_ms);
            end if;
            -- `insert ... select *` reads NULL for an absent key rather than
            -- the column default, so a soft-delete flag must be explicit.
            if v_final ->> 'is_deleted' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('is_deleted', false);
            end if;

            if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'insert') then
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message := 'The caller may not create this row.';
            else
              -- Only the columns the snapshot carries are named, so a column
              -- the payload omitted still gets its own default rather than
              -- NULL (jsonb_populate_record does not apply defaults).
              select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                     string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                into v_cols, v_vals
                from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k;

              execute format(
                'insert into public.%I (%s) select %s from '
                'jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v',
                v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
              ) using v_final;
              execute format(
                'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                v_table
              ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
              v_status := 'accepted';
            end if;
          end if;
        else
          -- Lock the target row first, then decide.
          execute format(
            'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1 for update',
            v_table
          ) into v_existing using v_entity_id;

          if v_existing is null then
            v_status := 'rejected';
            v_error_code := 'not_found';
            v_message := 'The row no longer exists on the server.';
          elsif (v_existing ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean = true
                and v_operation = 'update' then
            v_status := 'tombstone';
            v_error_code := 'tombstone';
            v_message := 'The row was deleted on the server.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          elsif (v_existing ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean = true
                and v_operation = 'delete' then
            v_status := 'already_resolved';
            v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
            v_message := 'The row was already deleted.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;

          -- -----------------------------------------------------------------
          -- Delete-review approval (Task 20 Phase 4). The request row is the
          -- one locked above; the target is locked next.
          -- -----------------------------------------------------------------
          elsif v_table = 'delete_requests'
                and (v_payload ->> 'status') = 'approved' then
            v_req_status := coalesce(v_existing ->> 'status', '');

            if v_req_status in ('approved', 'rejected') then
              -- Already decided: nothing to do, and no second tombstone.
              v_status := 'already_resolved';
              v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
              v_message := 'This request was already reviewed.';
              v_new_row := v_existing;
            elsif not public.can_delete_firm(
                    nullif(v_existing ->> 'firm_id', '')::uuid) then
              -- The requester cannot approve their own request: only a member
              -- with delete permission may review one.
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message :=
                'Only a member with delete permission may review this request.';
            elsif v_base_version is null
                  or v_base_version <> (v_existing ->> 'version')::int then
              v_status := 'conflict';
              v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
              v_message := 'The request changed since this decision was made.';
              v_new_row := v_existing;
            else
              v_target_type := nullif(v_existing ->> 'entity_type', '');
              v_target_table := public.sync_entity_table(v_target_type);
              v_expected := nullif(v_existing ->> 'target_base_version', '')::int;

              if v_target_table is null or v_target_table not in (
                'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references'
              ) then
                v_status := 'rejected';
                v_error_code := 'unsupported_target';
                v_message :=
                  'This request names a record that cannot be deleted here.';
              else
                execute format(
                  'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1 for update',
                  v_target_table
                ) into v_target using (v_existing ->> 'entity_id');

                if v_target is null
                   or coalesce((v_target ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean, false) then
                  -- Nothing left to approve. The request is untouched audit
                  -- history; the tombstone rides back for the reviewer.
                  v_status := 'already_resolved';
                  v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
                  v_message := 'The record was already deleted.';
                  v_new_row := v_existing;
                elsif coalesce(v_target ->> 'firm_id', '')
                      is distinct from coalesce(v_existing ->> 'firm_id', '') then
                  v_status := 'rejected';
                  v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                  v_message := 'The record is not in this request''s firm.';
                elsif v_expected is null
                      or v_expected <> (v_target ->> 'version')::int then
                  -- The record moved under the request: park the request as
                  -- stale and adopt the version the reviewer just saw, so a
                  -- reconfirm re-decides against the row that exists now.
                  v_final := (v_existing || jsonb_build_object(
                      'status', 'stale_review_required',
                      'target_base_version', (v_target ->> 'version')::int,
                      'updated_at', v_ms,
                      'version', (v_existing ->> 'version')::int + 1,
                      'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
                    )) - 'server_updated_at';

                  if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'update') then
                    v_status := 'rejected';
                    v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                    v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
                  else
                    select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                           string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                      into v_cols, v_vals
                      from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
                     where k <> 'server_updated_at';

                    execute format(
                      'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                      'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                      'where t.id = $2',
                      v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
                    ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

                    execute format(
                      'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                      v_table
                    ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
                    v_status := 'target_conflict';
                    v_error_code := 'target_conflict';
                    v_message :=
                      'The record changed since this request was made.';
                  end if;
                else
                  -- Reconfirmed against the row that exists now: tombstone the
                  -- target in this same savepoint.
                  execute format(
                    'update public.%I t set is_deleted = true, '
                    '  version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
                    '  last_modified_by = $1, updated_at = $2 '
                    'where t.id = $3 returning to_jsonb(t)',
                    v_target_table
                  ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, (v_existing ->> 'entity_id')
                  into v_target;

                  -- The same cascade an ordinary case delete performs, so an
                  -- approved request cannot leave live children behind. The
                  -- request stores the singular `entity_type` ('case'), so the
                  -- test is against the resolved *table* ('cases').
                  if v_target_table = 'cases' then
                    v_children := '[]'::jsonb;
                    for v_child in execute format(
                      'update public.case_history t '
                      'set is_deleted = true, '
                      '    version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
                      '    last_modified_by = $1, '
                      '    updated_at = $2 '
                      'where t.case_id = $3 and t.is_deleted = false '
                      'returning to_jsonb(t)'
                    ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, (v_existing ->> 'entity_id')
                    loop
                      v_children := v_children || jsonb_build_array(v_child);
                    end loop;
                  end if;

                  -- Resolve the request beside the tombstone.
                  v_final := (v_existing || jsonb_build_object(
                      'status', 'approved',
                      'reviewed_by', v_actor::text,
                      'review_note', coalesce(
                        v_payload ->> 'review_note',
                        v_existing ->> 'review_note'),
                      'updated_at', v_ms,
                      'version', (v_existing ->> 'version')::int + 1,
                      'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
                    )) - 'server_updated_at';

                  if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'update') then
                    v_status := 'rejected';
                    v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                    v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
                  else
                    select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                           string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                      into v_cols, v_vals
                      from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
                     where k <> 'server_updated_at';

                    execute format(
                      'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                      'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                      'where t.id = $2',
                      v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
                    ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

                    execute format(
                      'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                      v_table
                    ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
                    v_status := 'accepted';
                  end if;
                end if;
              end if;
            end if;
          elsif v_base_version is null
                or v_base_version <> (v_existing ->> 'version')::int then
            v_status := 'conflict';
            v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
            v_message := 'The server version changed since this edit was made.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          else
            v_old_version := (v_existing ->> 'version')::int;
            -- `firm_id` is subtracted as well: an existing row keeps the firm it
            -- has, whatever the payload named, so no update can move a case out
            -- of the chamber it belongs to (§3.3).
            v_final := (v_existing || v_payload)
              - 'server_updated_at' - 'version' - 'last_modified_by' - 'firm_id';
            if v_table = 'conflict_log' then
              v_final := v_final - 'created_at';
            end if;
            v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object(
              'version', v_old_version + 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
            );
            if v_operation = 'delete' then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('is_deleted', true);
            end if;
            if v_final ->> 'updated_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('updated_at', v_ms);
            end if;

            if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, v_operation) then
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
            else
              -- Update every column the final snapshot carries, except
              -- server_updated_at, which the trigger owns.
              -- Both lists are ordered by the same key, so the columns and
              -- their values can never fall out of step.
              select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                     string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                into v_cols, v_vals
                from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
               where k <> 'server_updated_at';

              execute format(
                'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                'where t.id = $2',
                v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
              ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

              execute format(
                'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                v_table
              ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
              v_status := 'accepted';
            end if;
          end if;
        end if;

        -- Atomic history and cascade soft-delete, only on an accepted case
        -- mutation. A delete-request approval whose target is a case performs
        -- its own cascade inside the branch above, so this stays case-only.
        if v_status = 'accepted' and v_table = 'cases' then
          if v_operation = 'delete' then
            -- One accepted case delete soft-deletes its children in this same
            -- savepoint; the changed children ride back to the caller.
            v_children := '[]'::jsonb;
            for v_child in execute format(
              'update public.case_history t '
              'set is_deleted = true, '
              '    version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
              '    last_modified_by = $1, '
              '    updated_at = $2 '
              'where t.case_id = $3 and t.is_deleted = false '
              'returning to_jsonb(t)'
            ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, v_entity_id
            loop
              v_children := v_children || jsonb_build_array(v_child);
            end loop;
          elsif v_operation = 'update'
                and (v_final ->> 'next_date') is distinct from
                    (v_existing ->> 'next_date') then
            -- The client's provisional preview supplies its identity so the
            -- authoritative event replaces it one-for-one.
            v_prov := v_row -> 'provisional_history';
            if v_prov is null or jsonb_typeof(v_prov) <> 'object' then
              v_prov := '{}'::jsonb;
            end if;

            v_hist := v_prov || jsonb_build_object(
              'id', coalesce(v_prov ->> 'id', gen_random_uuid()::text),
              'case_id', v_entity_id,
              'user_id', v_new_row -> 'user_id',
              'firm_id', v_new_row -> 'firm_id',
              'source_mutation_id',
                coalesce(v_prov ->> 'source_mutation_id', v_mutation_id),
              'created_by', v_actor,
              'base_case_version',
                coalesce(nullif(v_prov ->> 'base_case_version', '')::int,
                         v_old_version),
              'result_case_version', (v_new_row ->> 'version')::int,
              'version', 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text,
              'is_deleted', false,
              'updated_at', v_ms
            );
            -- Nothing the client omitted is invented: the previous values come
            -- from the authoritative base row.
            if v_hist ->> 'hearing_date' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'hearing_date',
                coalesce(nullif(v_existing ->> 'next_date', '')::bigint, v_ms)
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'last_step' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'last_step', v_existing -> 'last_step'
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'note_result' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'note_result', v_existing -> 'notes_results'
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'result' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'result', v_existing -> 'result'
              );
            end if;

            execute format(
              'insert into public.case_history select * from '
              'jsonb_populate_record(null::public.case_history, $1)'
            ) using v_hist;

            -- Hand the authoritative row back so the client can reconcile its
            -- provisional preview (same id) in one write.
            execute format(
              'select to_jsonb(t) from public.case_history t where t.id = $1'
            ) into v_hist_row using v_hist ->> 'id';
          end if;
        end if;
      end if;

      -- Terminal result for this mutation.
      if v_status = 'accepted' then
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'accepted',
          'version', (v_new_row ->> 'version')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'children', coalesce(v_children, '[]'::jsonb),
          'history', v_hist_row,
          -- A delete-request approval carries the target it tombstoned, so the
          -- reviewer's client can apply the record's disappearance in one pass.
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type
        );
      elsif v_status = 'target_conflict' then
        -- The request was parked as stale_review_required; hand back both rows
        -- so the reviewer can inspect the record that exists now.
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'target_conflict',
          'version', nullif(v_new_row ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type,
          'target_version', nullif(v_target ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'error_code', v_error_code,
          'message', v_message
        );
      elsif v_status in ('conflict', 'tombstone', 'already_resolved') then
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', v_status,
          'version', nullif(v_new_row ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type,
          'error_code', v_error_code,
          'message', v_message
        );
      else
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', coalesce(v_error_code, 'validation_failed'),
          'message', coalesce(v_message, 'The mutation was refused.')
        );
      end if;
    exception
      when others then
        get stacked diagnostics
          v_state = returned_sqlstate,
          v_msg = message_text;
        -- A permanent, per-mutation failure is caught and reported; anything
        -- else is infrastructure and aborts the whole RPC.
        if v_state not in (
          '42501', 'P0001', '23502', '23503', '23505', '23514',
          '22P02', '22007', '22003', '42804', '42703'
        ) then
          raise;
        end if;
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', case v_state
            when '42501' then 'permission_denied'
            when 'P0001' then 'entitlement_required'
            else 'validation_failed'
          end,
          'message', v_msg
        );
    end;

    -- Receipt for every terminal result, in the same transaction. It is written
    -- after the savepoint block so a per-mutation rejection still records one.
    insert into public.mutation_receipts (
      mutation_id, actor_id, entity_type, entity_id, request_hash,
      terminal_status, result_payload
    ) values (
      v_mutation_id, v_actor, v_entity_type, v_entity_id, v_hash,
      v_result ->> 'status', v_result
    )
    on conflict (mutation_id) do nothing;

    v_results[v_idx] := v_result;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object('results', (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(v_results[k] order by k), '[]'::jsonb)
      from generate_subscripts(v_results, 1) as k
  ));
end;
$$;

comment on function public.push_changes(jsonb) is
  'Single atomic push pipeline: optimistic concurrency, per-mutation savepoints, idempotent receipts, authoritative case history and cascade soft-deletes, and the delete-review approval branch (locking, target_conflict/stale_review_required, already_resolved, atomic tombstone). The scope columns belong to the server: an insert takes its firm_id from current_firm_id(), an existing row keeps the firm it has, and scope_owner_id is never taken from a payload.';

-- Same surface as before: `anon` and `public` stay refused.
revoke all on function public.push_changes(jsonb) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.push_changes(jsonb) to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.523 — Firm Mode Phase 3 — A Seat Must Be Empty, And The Chamber Must Have One

### 0.0.523 · `20261015120000_firm_mode_join_gate.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-15.** Firm mode: a seat must be empty and the chamber must have one. join_firm refuses an account holding its own diary — counting the individual cases its answer quotes and restoring the row in the same transaction, so the count is atomic with the check (the restore is the 'has_own_diary' bug fix: without it a refused join lost the caller's own row) — refuses past the tier's seat cap, and joins with §3.1's defaults (associate, can_add and can_edit in, can_delete out) and both freshness stamps while retiring an already-member's code as revoked rather than used. holds_own_diary and individual_diary_cases, the two helpers the gate and the screens share, are granted to authenticated alone so a signed-out caller cannot probe another account's diary count.

```sql
-- Firm mode, phase 3 — the join gate.
--
-- Three rulings land here, and they share one RPC because they are one decision
-- made at one moment: `firm_invites` redemption. The second guard this replaces
-- the shipped `join_firm` (20260929102300_phase3_join_firm.sql) had was only
-- "is this code valid"; everything below is what else has to be true before a
-- stranger's rows enter a chamber.
--
--   1. **A seat starts empty** (§2.1). Joining is refused when the redeemer
--      already holds their own diary: non-deleted rows they authored as an
--      individual — `firm_id is null` **and no scope owner**, which is what stops
--      a dissolved chamber's rows (§4.4) ever counting as anybody's own diary.
--      Rows authored *inside* a chamber are the chamber's and never block a
--      later join, which is what lets a removed member join another chamber with
--      the same account.
--   2. **The seat cap** (§5.3, §5.4). A tier sells seats — Pro 0, Firm 5, Firm
--      Plus 20 — and until now no `join_firm` of any version checked a seat
--      count at all, so a Firm chamber could seat a hundred associates. The cap
--      reads the **effective** tier, because a chamber whose subscription is
--      lapsed past the grace window has no tier in force, and a lapsed chamber is
--      deliberately still joinable (§2.4): its seats stay open while it is lapsed
--      and close again on renewal.
--   3. **The default permissions** (§3.1). A newly joined associate starts with
--      `can_add = true` and `can_edit = true`, superseding the shipped
--      `can_edit = false`; `can_delete` stays false, because deletion inside a
--      chamber runs through the owner-reviewed delete-request flow.
--
-- The §2.5 fumble is fixed in the same transaction: an already-member
-- redemption still answers `already_member`, but the code is **retired as
-- revoked** rather than consumed as `used_by`, so the owner's list reads
-- *retired* instead of *used by [member]* — the owner is not left thinking a new
-- colleague joined, and the code is still dead for a stranger, which was the only
-- reason the shipped version consumed it.
--
-- The refusal counts live cases and returns their number so the client can word
-- the sentence §2.1 specifies. Nothing is written on any refusal path, and none
-- of them raises: a returned status is what makes the outcome reportable rather
-- than a stack trace, except the rate limit, which the shipped version already
-- raises deliberately and this one keeps raising.
--
-- What the client is owed, and what this migration does NOT do (later work):
-- `ensure_firm`'s creation gate still points at `is_premium()`. It belongs with
-- the seat cap — creation needs Firm or above, and Pro's cap is 0 — but the
-- tier columns it would read at the same time do not exist yet, so the creation
-- gate moves with them; the seat cap below is written so that adding them is
-- one `when` branch and nothing else. This is the approved sequence's Phase 3;
-- the creation-gate re-point and `tier_pending` are owed separately, and the
-- seat check's live tier reads return null until `firms.tier` and
-- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm`'s widened trigger arrive.

-- What counts as *the caller's own diary*: rows they authored as an individual,
-- not rows authored inside a chamber they are (or were) a member of. A scope
-- owner marks an unscoped row as belonging to somebody by a dissolve, so such a
-- row is not a fresh diary either.
create or replace function public.individual_diary_cases(p_user_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select pg_catalog.count(*)::integer
    from public.cases c
   where c.user_id = p_user_id
     and c.is_deleted = false
     and c.firm_id is null
     and c.scope_owner_id is null;
$$;

comment on function public.individual_diary_cases(uuid) is
  'Non-deleted cases the account authored while it had no chamber and no scope owner — the §2.1 seat is empty test.';

-- Whether the account holds rows that make its diary its own: the same four
-- case-data tables plus every reference table, where a row it added or edited
-- counts even after a soft delete (`is_deleted` is not consulted here; a deleted
-- custom court is still a row the account authored for itself).
create or replace function public.holds_own_diary(p_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_table text;
  v_tables text[] := array[
    'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references',
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  ];
  v_found boolean;
begin
  foreach v_table in array v_tables loop
    execute format(
      'select exists (select 1 from public.%I t '
      ' where t.user_id = $1 and t.firm_id is null '
      '   and t.scope_owner_id is null)',
      v_table
    ) into v_found using p_user_id;

    if v_found then
      return true;
    end if;
  end loop;

  return false;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.holds_own_diary(uuid) is
  'Whether the account authored any firm-less, scope-owner-less row — the §2.1 test that a seat is not empty.';

-- How many seats the chamber's effective tier sells, or null for **unlimited**.
--
-- The tier map is a constant here rather than a lookup because there is nowhere
-- to look: the ladder's `firms.tier` column belongs to a later phase. Until it
-- arrives, a lapsed-or-not **premium** chamber is treated as a Firm chamber, and
-- the consequence is bounded and visible: a Firm Plus chamber sees its roster
-- refused at six rather than at twenty until the column lands, which the client
-- can word from the returned `seats`. Everything else is unchanged by the
-- substitution — see the note above about the creation gate; adding the column
-- is three lines here (`when 'firm_plus' then 20` already exists) and its
-- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm` widened trigger beside it.
--
-- Null is both "no tier in force" — a lapsed or never-purchased chamber, which
-- §2.4 keeps joinable — and "Unlimited by agreement". The two are the same
-- answer here on purpose: neither is a number to refuse at.
create or replace function public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select case
           when public.is_premium(f.owner_id) then 5
           else null
         end
    from public.firms f
   where f.id = p_firm_id;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) is
  'Seats the chamber''s effective tier sells (Firm 5 until firms.tier lands), null for unlimited or no tier in force.';

create or replace function public.join_firm(code text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- Five failures per 15 minutes, and attempts older than a day are dropped by
  -- the call itself, so no scheduled job is needed.
  c_max_failures constant integer := 5;
  c_window constant interval := interval '15 minutes';
  c_retention constant interval := interval '1 day';

  -- Two values only ever compared with each other, so they carry no status of
  -- their own.
  c_role_associate constant text := 'associate';

  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_code_hash text;
  v_invite public.firm_invites%rowtype;
  v_failures integer;
  v_used_at bigint;
  v_diary_cases integer;
  v_seat_cap integer;
  v_seats_taken integer;
  v_own_diary boolean;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  delete from public.invite_attempts a
   where a.attempted_at < now() - c_retention;

  select pg_catalog.count(*) into v_failures
    from public.invite_attempts a
   where a.user_id = v_user_id
     and a.attempted_at > now() - c_window;

  if v_failures >= c_max_failures then
    raise exception 'Too many attempts — try again later'
      using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;

  -- The normalization the client mirrors: trim, upper, then hash. Only the
  -- sha256 hex is ever compared, so a plaintext code exists only in the user's
  -- hands and the invite row (Task 20) must hash a code the same way.
  v_code_hash := public.sha256_hex(upper(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(code, ''))));

  select * into v_invite
    from public.firm_invites i
   where i.code_hash = v_code_hash
     and i.used_by is null
     and i.revoked = false
   for update;

  if not found then
    -- Non-exception return path: the attempt insert must commit.
    insert into public.invite_attempts (user_id) values (v_user_id);
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_code');
  end if;

  v_used_at := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;

  -- Retry by someone already in the firm. The code is retired as **revoked**,
  -- never as `used_by`, so the owner sees *retired* rather than a colleague who
  -- joined, while the code stays dead for a stranger. The single-use rule is
  -- unchanged; only its recording is.
  if exists (
    select 1 from public.firm_members m
     where m.firm_id = v_invite.firm_id and m.user_id = v_user_id
  ) then
    update public.firm_invites i
       set revoked = true
     where i.id = v_invite.id;

    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'already_member',
      'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
    );
  end if;

  -- A seat starts empty (§2.1). Rows authored inside a chamber are the chamber's
  -- and do not count, so a member removed from one chamber may still join
  -- another with the same account.
  v_diary_cases := public.individual_diary_cases(v_user_id);

  if public.holds_own_diary(v_user_id) then
    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'has_own_diary',
      'cases', v_diary_cases
    );
  end if;

  -- The seat cap (§5.3, §5.4). A member leaving deletes their `firm_members`
  -- row outright (`remove_firm_member`, phase 4 territory), so a plain count of
  -- the chamber's rows is the number of seats taken — the history of who was
  -- once here lives in the ledger's attribution, not in the membership table.
  v_seat_cap := public.firm_seat_cap(v_invite.firm_id);

  if v_seat_cap is not null then
    select pg_catalog.count(*) into v_seats_taken
      from public.firm_members m
     where m.firm_id = v_invite.firm_id;

    if v_seats_taken >= v_seat_cap then
      delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'seats_full',
        'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id,
        'seats', v_seat_cap
      );
    end if;
  end if;

  -- The defaults of §3.1: members write from the first day, and the owner
  -- narrows them afterwards if he wants to. `can_delete` stays false because
  -- deletion in a chamber is the owner-reviewed request flow.
  -- `firm_members` carries no sync columns of its own (it is a live read, not a
  -- ledger table): the two stamps are the client's permission-freshness pair.
  insert into public.firm_members (
    firm_id, user_id, role, can_add, can_edit, can_delete,
    synced_at, permissions_synced_at
  )
  values (
    v_invite.firm_id, v_user_id, c_role_associate, true, true, false,
    v_used_at, v_used_at
  )
  on conflict (firm_id, user_id) do update
    set role = 'associate',
        can_add = true,
        can_edit = true,
        can_delete = false,
        synced_at = excluded.synced_at,
        permissions_synced_at = excluded.permissions_synced_at;

  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = v_invite.firm_id,
         role = 'associate'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  update public.firm_invites i
     set used_by = v_user_id, used_at = v_used_at
   where i.id = v_invite.id;

  delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'joined',
    'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.join_firm(text) is
  'Single-use invite redemption: rate limit, hash, empty-seat and seat-cap gates, membership, profile relink, invite consumed — one transaction.';

-- `anon` is named explicitly for the same reason as `approve_payment`: a direct
-- EXECUTE grant from Supabase's default privileges outlives a revoke of PUBLIC.
revoke all on function public.join_firm(text) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.join_firm(text) to authenticated;

-- The three new helpers are `authenticated`-only, and `anon` is named
-- explicitly for the same reason as `join_firm` above: a direct EXECUTE grant
-- from Supabase's default privileges outlives a revoke of PUBLIC.
--
-- They are not opened to the app's client either. Each is a fact about **the
-- caller and their own chamber** — whether this account still holds an
-- individual diary, how many such cases it holds, and how many seats its
-- chamber sells — so a signed-out caller and a probing one must both be refused:
-- the gate's own refusal must not become an oracle for another account's diary,
-- and `firm_seat_cap` reads `firms` and `profiles`, which no client role may
-- read at all. `join_firm` and the screens' own local reads are what need them,
-- and both run as `authenticated` (or as the RPC's definer).
revoke all on function public.individual_diary_cases(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.holds_own_diary(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;

grant execute on function public.individual_diary_cases(uuid) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.holds_own_diary(uuid) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.524 — Firm Mode Phase 4 — Removing A Member Clears Their Push Tokens

### 0.0.524 · `20261015160000_firm_removal_clears_device_tokens.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-15.** Firm mode: removing a member clears that member's push tokens. remove_firm_member deleted the membership but left the removed member's device_tokens rows in place, so the chamber's other members kept addressing notifications to a device that is no longer in the chamber — the removal was silent on the one channel it needed to be heard on, and the removed member kept the firm's topics. The tokens are deleted for the removed member alone, in the same transaction as the membership, so a device that is no longer a member cannot be sent the firm's notices, and the row the removed member authored keeps its author untouched.

```sql
-- Firm mode (4) — a removed member's device stops being pushed to.
--
-- The gap. `remove_firm_member` revokes membership, relinks the profile to the
-- individual default and announces the revocation on both topics, but it leaves
-- the member's `device_tokens` rows behind. Those rows are the fan-set the admin
-- payment-alert sender reads, and they are the member's own to delete only while
-- they can still sign in — which, after removal, is a state the server may never
-- observe again: the device wipes itself on the next open and the row is only
-- cleaned up if the client runs its own sign-out path.
--
-- What that costs. A removed member's phone keeps receiving the chamber's pushes
-- (approval alerts, roster changes) even though their access has ended. The
-- chamber's data is unreachable — `profiles.firm_id` is null, so every read is
-- filtered and every write lands firm-less — but a phone being told about a
-- chamber it has left is both a leak of the chamber's activity and a reason for
-- the removed member to keep opening an app that erases their copy on launch.
--
-- The fix is one statement inside the same transaction as the revoke, so the two
-- cannot come apart: a removal that commits has already taken the tokens. It is
-- server-side on purpose (not left to the client's sign-out) because the whole
-- point is to reach the devices of an account that is no longer cooperating.
-- The service-role sender's fan-set is unaffected for every *current* member.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- remove_firm_member — clear the removed member's push registrations
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `create or replace` of the whole function: the body is otherwise unchanged, so
-- the diff against the previous revision is the DELETE below and nothing else.
create or replace function public.remove_firm_member(p_user_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path to 'pg_catalog', 'public'
as $function$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_locked boolean;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_request');
  end if;

  -- The caller's own firm, and only if they own it. A non-owner gets an answer
  -- rather than an error: it is a state the UI can word, not a bug.
  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  if p_user_id = v_actor then
    -- A firm is not transferable in this task, so removing the owner would
    -- leave `firms.owner_id` pointing at a non-member and the firm with nobody
    -- who may administer it.
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'cannot_remove_self');
  end if;

  -- Locked, so two concurrent removals cannot both claim the same row and one
  -- of them cannot report `removed` for a membership it did not delete.
  select true into v_locked
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  delete from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id;

  -- The revocation, in one statement: `firm_id` is what every scoped read, every
  -- topic join and every queued `push_changes` write at once. `role` follows it
  -- back to the individual default rather than being left as `associate` with no
  -- firm.
  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = null,
         role = 'individual'
   where p.id = p_user_id;

  -- The member's push registrations go with the access. A row here is keyed by
  -- the FCM token, so this reaches every device that registered one, including
  -- devices that will never sign in again to clean up after themselves.
  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = p_user_id;

  -- Two audiences, two topics — both as the trigger's own `row_change` event,
  -- so the client needs no second decoder:
  --
  --   * `user:{removed}` reaches the removed account's own devices at once,
  --     whatever topic they were joined to (`can_read_topic` always allows a
  --     caller their own user topic, including after the relink above);
  --   * `firm:{firm}` refreshes every remaining member's roster view.
  --
  -- The DELETE above fires no row trigger — the broadcast trigger is
  -- INSERT/UPDATE only — so this announcement is explicit rather than implied.
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'user:' || p_user_id::text,
    true
  );
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'firm:' || v_firm_id::text,
    true
  );

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'removed',
    'user_id', p_user_id,
    'firm_id', v_firm_id
  );
end;
$function$;

-- Same ownership contract as before: only `authenticated` may call it, and the
-- function itself refuses a non-owner. `anon` is named explicitly because a
-- direct EXECUTE grant from Supabase's default privileges outlives a revoke of
-- PUBLIC.
revoke all on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) to authenticated;

comment on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) is
  'Owner-only removal: locks the membership, deletes it, relinks the profile to the individual default, clears the member''s push registrations, and announces the revocation on the member''s own topic and the chamber''s. The member''s authored rows are untouched and stay the firm''s.';
```

## App Version 0.0.529 — Firm Mode Phase 5 — The Permission Boundary

### 0.0.529 · `20261016100000_firm_mode_permission_boundary.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-16.** Firm mode: a member's flags become a boundary on the server. can_add_firm joins its two siblings and enforce_member_permission() is attached BEFORE INSERT and BEFORE UPDATE to the ten gated tables in one loop, so can_add gates a create and can_edit every non-tombstone update — including the author's own chamber row, which is deliberately stricter than the shipped policy, because in a chamber most rows a member touches are ones they authored. The tombstone transition keeps can_delete's own gate rather than duplicating it. The function is SECURITY INVOKER on purpose: the permission rule is keyed on auth.uid() so both the direct-PostgREST and the push_changes door are bound while a migration, a fixture or a nightly job steps aside, and the scope rule is keyed on current_user so ensure_firm and the dissolve may still move a scope. §3.3's scope-column ruling lands here too: a client may not change a row's firm_id nor create a firm-less row while it holds a chamber — firm_id was still in the column grants after the scope_owner_id work, so a member could drop a chamber case into their own diary by direct update. sync_can_write is replaced with only its INSERT branch changed, in both the reference and the general branch, so the RPC refuses a create cleanly; its update branch, delete_requests and every RLS policy are untouched.

```sql
-- Firm mode Phase 5 — the permission boundary.
--
-- §3.3 rules that a member's flags are a boundary on the server, not an
-- intention in the app: a modified client, or a direct PostgREST call carrying a
-- member's own token, must not add or edit chamber data the owner has switched
-- off. What is added here, and nothing else:
--
--   1. `can_add_firm(uuid)` — the third helper beside `can_edit_firm` and
--      `can_delete_firm`. It did not exist, so both halves of the rule are new
--      work rather than the UPDATE half alone.
--   2. `enforce_member_permission()` — one BEFORE trigger function, attached
--      per table in the shape `enforce_delete_transition()` already uses.
--      INSERT is gated on `can_add`, UPDATE on `can_edit`, and the tombstone
--      transition is left to `can_delete`'s existing gate rather than
--      duplicated here (§3.3: the two permissions stay separate).
--   3. `sync_can_write` states the same rule for the RPC's door — `can_add` on a
--      create, and `can_edit` on every non-tombstone update of a firm-scoped row
--      — so a refused write is a clean per-mutation `permission_denied` rather
--      than a trigger error. The trigger covers the direct door and this covers
--      the queued one. The `can_delete` check on a tombstone, `delete_requests`,
--      `conflict_log` and every RLS policy are untouched.
--
-- §3.3's scope-column ruling is folded in at the same place, because the trigger
-- exists anyway: a client role may not move an existing row between scopes
-- (`firm_id` is the server's on every existing row), and a caller who holds a
-- chamber may not create a row outside it. `scope_owner_id` is already
-- server-only by column privilege (`20261015100000_firm_mode_read_scope.sql`);
-- `firm_id` was not, so a member could null it on their own row — dropping a
-- chamber's case into their personal diary — through a direct PostgREST update.
--
-- The trigger function is deliberately **SECURITY INVOKER**, and its two rules
-- are keyed on the two different things their cases require:
--
--   * the **scope** rule on the **role**, because what it must exclude is a
--     client write: `ensure_firm` stamps `firm_id` on a firm-less diary in the
--     transaction that creates the chamber, and the dissolve nulls it again, and
--     both run as their owner. `push_changes` derives and preserves `firm_id`
--     itself, so the RPC needs nothing from this rule.
--   * the **permission** rule on the **caller** (`auth.uid()`), because it must
--     bind the same write through both doors — a direct PostgREST write (role
--     `authenticated`) and the identical write queued through `push_changes`,
--     which is SECURITY DEFINER and so runs as its owner — while a migration, a
--     nightly job or a fixture that has impersonated nobody must step aside.
--     `auth.uid()` is precisely the thing those two have and a script does not.
--
-- Keying the permission rule on the role instead leaves the RPC door ungated, and
-- that was **measured rather than assumed**: with the role keying in place, a
-- `can_edit = false` member's queued update came back `accepted` instead of
-- `permission_denied`. The price of the caller keying is that a statement which
-- sets a claim and then writes as the database owner is judged as that caller's
-- write — which is what a claim means — so a proof must put the session back the
-- way it found it: `reset role` alone leaves `request.jwt.claims` behind, and
-- `firm_mode_join_gate_test.sql`'s `pg_temp.as_owner()` clears it for exactly
-- that reason.
--
-- Declaring this function SECURITY DEFINER would make `current_user` the owner
-- for every caller and switch the scope rule off, which is why it is not
-- declared — and it is also why the permission rule cannot be keyed on the role.
--
-- No grant is written below, on purpose. `can_add_firm` is a **new** function,
-- so Supabase's default privileges grant it EXECUTE directly to `anon` and
-- `authenticated`, exactly as they do for its two siblings: RLS policy
-- expressions run with the *caller's* privileges, so revoking would break the
-- policies that use them, and the helper answers only for the caller, so it
-- discloses nothing. `sync_can_write` is replaced rather than recreated, so its
-- existing ACL is preserved.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The third access helper
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- True when the caller may add a firm-scoped row: the chamber's owner, or a
-- member whose `can_add` flag is on. A null firm (an individual account) is
-- never firm-scoped, so this is false for it — the callers' own
-- `firm_id is not null` guards are what keep a personal row unaffected.
create or replace function public.can_add_firm(p_firm_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select p_firm_id is not null
     and (
       exists (select 1 from public.firms f
                where f.id = p_firm_id and f.owner_id = auth.uid())
       or exists (select 1 from public.firm_members m
                   where m.firm_id = p_firm_id
                     and m.user_id = auth.uid()
                     and m.can_add)
     );
$$;

comment on function public.can_add_firm(uuid) is
  'True when the caller may add a firm-scoped row: the firm owner, or a member whose can_add flag is on. A null firm is never firm-scoped, so it is false for an individual account.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The boundary itself, and the server's ownership of the scope columns
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.enforce_member_permission()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The roles PostgREST sets for a request. A role outside this list is the
  -- database owner: a migration, a nightly job, or server code inside a
  -- SECURITY DEFINER function such as `ensure_firm`.
  c_client_roles constant text[] := array['authenticated', 'anon'];
begin
  -- 1. The scope columns belong to the server (§3.3): a client may not move a
  --    row between scopes. Keyed on the role, so `ensure_firm` and the dissolve
  --    — which move a scope legitimately, as their owner — are skipped.
  if current_user::text = any (c_client_roles) then
    if tg_op = 'INSERT' then
      if public.current_firm_id() is not null and new.firm_id is null then
        raise exception 'scope_change_not_permitted'
          using errcode = '42501',
                hint = 'A chamber holds chamber rows; only the server sets the scope.';
      end if;
    elsif new.firm_id is distinct from old.firm_id then
      raise exception 'scope_change_not_permitted'
        using errcode = '42501',
              hint = 'A row''s firm is derived when it is created and never changed by a client.';
    end if;
  end if;

  -- 2. The member's flags, keyed on the caller rather than the role: this is
  --    what binds the RPC's door as well as PostgREST's. A statement carrying no
  --    claim is a migration, a nightly job, or a fixture still to impersonate.
  if auth.uid() is null then
    return new;
  end if;

  -- 3. `can_add` gates a create.
  if tg_op = 'INSERT' then
    if new.firm_id is not null and not public.can_add_firm(new.firm_id) then
      raise exception 'add_not_permitted'
        using errcode = '42501',
              hint = 'Requires can_add in this firm.';
    end if;
    return new;
  end if;

  -- 4. The tombstone transition keeps `can_delete`'s own gate
  --    (`enforce_delete_transition`), so a member whose edits are switched off
  --    may still be allowed to delete, and the two permissions are not merged.
  if old.is_deleted = false and new.is_deleted = true then
    return new;
  end if;

  -- 5. `can_edit` gates every other update to a firm-scoped row — including the
  --    author's own, which is deliberately stricter than the RLS policy: in a
  --    chamber most rows a member touches are ones they authored, so an author
  --    exception would leave the owner's toggle nearly meaningless (§3.2, §3.3).
  if new.firm_id is not null and not public.can_edit_firm(new.firm_id) then
    raise exception 'edit_not_permitted'
      using errcode = '42501',
            hint = 'Requires can_edit in this firm.';
  end if;
  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.enforce_member_permission() is
  'BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE on the ten permission-gated tables. The scope rule is keyed on the client role (so ensure_firm and the dissolve may move a scope) and the permission rule on the caller, auth.uid() (so a create and every non-tombstone update are gated through both the direct-PostgREST and the push_changes door, while a migration, a nightly job or an un-impersonated fixture steps aside). can_add gates a create, can_edit every non-tombstone update of a firm-scoped row, and a client may not change a row''s firm_id nor create a firm-less row while it holds a chamber. Deliberately SECURITY INVOKER: SECURITY DEFINER would make current_user the owner for every caller and switch the scope rule off.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Attach the two triggers to the ten gated tables
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- One loop over an explicit array, the Phase 3 shape: a table missed here cannot
-- pass unnoticed, and the proof enumerates the same ten by name.
--
-- `delete_requests` and `conflict_log` are deliberately absent. Raising a delete
-- request is how a member without `can_delete` asks for a deletion, so it must
-- stay open to every member (§3.1); `conflict_log`'s rows are per-device merge
-- diagnostics, not chamber data.

do $$
declare
  v_table text;
  v_tables text[] := array[
    'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references', 'court_categories',
    'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types', 'on_behalfs'
  ];
begin
  foreach v_table in array v_tables loop
    execute format(
      'drop trigger if exists trg_%1$s_add_permission on public.%1$I',
      v_table
    );
    execute format(
      'create trigger trg_%1$s_add_permission before insert on public.%1$I '
      'for each row execute function public.enforce_member_permission()',
      v_table
    );

    execute format(
      'drop trigger if exists trg_%1$s_edit_permission on public.%1$I',
      v_table
    );
    execute format(
      'create trigger trg_%1$s_edit_permission before update on public.%1$I '
      'for each row execute function public.enforce_member_permission()',
      v_table
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. sync_can_write: the INSERT branch reads can_add
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- Only the two `insert` returns change. Everything else in this body — the
-- authorship rules, the `is not distinct from` firm comparisons, the reference
-- immutability rule, `delete_requests`, and the update/delete branch including
-- the `can_delete` check on a tombstone — is the shipped body verbatim
-- (`20260930210000_sync_can_write_firm_membership.sql`), so the RPC's answer and
-- the trigger's answer agree for a create and the refusal arrives as a clean
-- `permission_denied` result rather than an exception.
--
-- The `can_add` disjunct follows the shape already beside it: `firm_id is null`
-- short-circuits first, so an individual's personal row needs no flag — there is
-- no chamber in whose name it is being written.
--
-- An update is deliberately **not** gated here. `push_changes` subtracts
-- `firm_id` from the row it hands this function (§3.3's "an existing row keeps
-- the firm it has"), so on an update the row carries no firm to weigh — and a
-- rule that cannot see the firm cannot apply `can_edit`. The trigger does it
-- instead, which is why the trigger's permission rule is keyed on the caller.
create or replace function public.sync_can_write(
  p_table text,
  p_row jsonb,
  p_operation text
)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_is_reference boolean := p_table in (
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  );
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    return false;
  end if;

  if p_operation = 'insert' then
    if p_table = 'delete_requests' then
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'requested_by')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
             is not distinct from public.current_firm_id();
    elsif v_is_reference then
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'is_custom')::boolean, false)
         and coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
                is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
         )
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or public.can_add_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
         );
    else
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
                is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
         )
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or public.can_add_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
         );
    end if;
  end if;

  -- update / delete
  if p_table = 'delete_requests' then
    -- The requester may edit or withdraw their own request while it is pending,
    -- but only while the request's firm is still theirs: a removed requester must
    -- not be able to touch it. A member with delete permission may still review.
    return (
      coalesce((p_row ->> 'requested_by')::uuid, null) = v_actor
      and (p_row ->> 'status') = 'pending'
      and coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
            is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
    ) or public.can_delete_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null));
  elsif v_is_reference then
    -- A built-in row has no creator and no firm; only a custom row is writable.
    if not coalesce((p_row ->> 'is_custom')::boolean, false) then
      return false;
    end if;
    return (
        coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
        and (
          p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
          or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
               is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
        )
      )
      or public.can_edit_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null));
  elsif p_table = 'conflict_log' then
    return coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor;
  else
    -- Authorship only counts while the row's firm is still the caller's firm: a
    -- removed member keeps their own personal rows but not the firm's.
    if not (
      (
        coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
        and (
          p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
          or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
               is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
        )
      )
      or public.can_edit_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
    ) then
      return false;
    end if;
    -- The delete transition additionally needs can_delete, mirroring
    -- enforce_delete_transition().
    if p_operation = 'delete' and (p_row ->> 'firm_id') is not null then
      return public.can_delete_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null));
    end if;
    return true;
  end if;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sync_can_write(text, jsonb, text) is
  'Explicit write re-check for push_changes: same rules as the Phase 4 RLS policies, evaluated on the row that would be written, plus the Phase 5 can_add gate on a create. A firm comparison uses `is not distinct from`, because `=` against a NULL current_firm_id would yield NULL and slip past an `if not`. Authorship of a firm-scoped row is honoured only while the row''s firm is still the caller''s firm, so a removed member cannot merge a queued write. An update is not gated here: enforce_member_permission() is the enforcement for can_edit, and it can be, because push_changes subtracts firm_id from the row it passes here — a rule that cannot see the firm cannot weigh can_edit.';
```

## App Version 0.0.530 — Firm Mode Phase 6 — The In-Use Guard For Reference Rows

### 0.0.530 · `20261016110000_firm_mode_reference_in_use_guard.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-16.** Firm mode: the in-use guard for reference rows. enforce_reference_not_in_use() is attached BEFORE UPDATE to the four tables the nine foreign keys point at — court_categories, case_categories, courts and on_behalfs — and refuses the tombstone transition while a **live** dependent still names the row, raising reference_in_use as 23503 so push_changes rejects that one mutation instead of aborting the batch. steps and case_types deliberately take no trigger: cases.case_type and cases.last_step are free text, so nothing references either and no server guard can protect them. purge_tombstones() is rewritten to delete one candidate at a time and skip a row a dependent still names — one blocked tombstone used to abort the whole nightly purge — with the retention argument, the children-first order and the returned count unchanged.

```sql
-- Firm mode Phase 6 — the in-use guard for reference rows.
--
-- §3.2 rules that a reference row a **live** case still names cannot be deleted,
-- and §10.6 that the nightly purge must not be the thing that discovers the
-- collision. Two halves, and nothing else:
--
--   1. `enforce_reference_not_in_use()` — a BEFORE UPDATE trigger function on the
--      reference tables that have dependents, refusing the tombstone transition
--      (`is_deleted false -> true`) while a live dependent row still names the
--      row. The dependency graph is **nine foreign keys over four parents**, all
--      declared in `20260929100000_phase1_core_schema.sql`, and it is not what an
--      older one-line summary implied:
--
--        court_categories  <- case_categories.court_category_id
--                          <- courts.court_category_id
--                          <- steps.court_category_id
--                          <- case_types.court_category_id
--                          <- on_behalfs.court_category_id
--        case_categories   <- case_types.case_category_id
--                          <- cases.case_category_id
--        courts            <- cases.court_id
--        on_behalfs        <- cases.on_behalf_id
--
--      `steps` and `case_types` are deliberately **not** attached: nothing
--      references either by id — `cases.case_type` and `cases.last_step` are free
--      text, not foreign keys — so no server guard can protect them and a trigger
--      that could never fire would be noise. The proof asserts that limit rather
--      than claiming a guard the server cannot have.
--
--      Only a **live** dependent blocks. A dependent that is itself a tombstone
--      does not hold its parent back, because it is on its way out — which is why
--      this check is not simply the foreign key, and why the purge half below
--      still has work to do when a dependent is too young to have been purged.
--
--      The function is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, like
--      `enforce_delete_transition()` beside it, so the rule is about the **data**
--      and not about what the caller happens to be allowed to read: it must answer
--      the same way for a member, for the owner and for a maintenance script. It
--      is keyed on nothing else — no role, no `auth.uid()` — because the rule has
--      nothing to do with who is writing. `DELETE` never fires it, which is
--      exactly why a purge needs its own half.
--
--      The refusal is raised as errcode `23503` (foreign key violation) rather
--      than `42501`: it is a referential-integrity refusal, and `push_changes`
--      already catches `23503` per mutation, so a queued tombstone comes back as a
--      clean `rejected` / `validation_failed` result carrying this message
```
