```sql
--      instead of aborting the batch.
--
--   2. `purge_tombstones()` skips a blocked row instead of failing whole. The
--      shipped body deleted each table's tombstones in one set-based statement,
--      so a single row a live dependent still named raised
--      `foreign_key_violation` and aborted the **entire** purge — every other
--      tombstone on the project stayed. It now walks one table's candidate rows
--      at a time and deletes them one by one inside an exception block that skips
--      only a foreign-key violation. The predicate is therefore the database's own
--      answer to "is this row still referenced?", so the purge cannot drift from
--      the real foreign keys. The deletion order, the retention argument, the
--      cutoff and the returned count are unchanged, and the kept rows are reported
--      in a notice so the daily `pg_cron` run is not silent.
--
-- Table class (rule 4): the guard and the purge touch the push/pull domain class
-- only, and the reference tables are its firm-shared half.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The in-use guard
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.enforce_reference_not_in_use()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The child table and column of one of the nine foreign keys above, as a
  -- '<child table>.<child column>' pair.
  v_pair text;
  v_pairs text[];
  v_child_table text;
  v_child_column text;
  v_found integer;
begin
  -- Only the tombstone transition is guarded; every other update is somebody
  -- else's business (the permission boundary, the resurrection guard).
  if not (old.is_deleted = false and new.is_deleted = true) then
    return new;
  end if;

  -- Every parent's primary key is `id` and every one of the nine foreign keys
  -- targets it, so the value to match is the row's own id.
  v_pairs := case tg_table_name
    when 'court_categories' then array[
      'case_categories.court_category_id',
      'courts.court_category_id',
      'steps.court_category_id',
      'case_types.court_category_id',
      'on_behalfs.court_category_id'
    ]
    when 'case_categories' then array[
      'case_types.case_category_id',
      'cases.case_category_id'
    ]
    when 'courts' then array[
      'cases.court_id'
    ]
    when 'on_behalfs' then array[
      'cases.on_behalf_id'
    ]
    else array[]::text[]
  end;

  foreach v_pair in array v_pairs loop
    v_child_table := split_part(v_pair, '.', 1);
    v_child_column := split_part(v_pair, '.', 2);

    execute format(
      'select 1 from public.%I d where d.%I = $1 and d.is_deleted = false '
      'limit 1',
      v_child_table,
      v_child_column
    ) into v_found using new.id;

    if v_found is not null then
      raise exception 'reference_in_use'
        using errcode = '23503',
              hint = format(
                '%s still names this row, so it cannot be deleted yet.',
                v_child_table
              );
    end if;
  end loop;

  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.enforce_reference_not_in_use() is
  'BEFORE UPDATE on the reference tables that have dependents: refuses the tombstone transition (is_deleted false -> true) while a live dependent row still names the row, raising reference_in_use as 23503 so push_changes rejects that one mutation rather than aborting the batch. SECURITY DEFINER, and unkeyed on role or auth.uid(), so the answer is the same for a member, the owner and a maintenance script. steps and case_types take no trigger: cases.case_type and cases.last_step are free text, so nothing references them. A dependent that is itself a tombstone does not block.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Attach the trigger to the four parents that have dependents
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- One loop over an explicit array, the shape Phase 3 and Phase 5 use. The
-- four names are the parents of the nine foreign keys listed above; the proof
-- enumerates the same four by name and asserts that the other two reference
-- tables carry no guard.

do $$
declare
  v_table text;
  v_tables text[] := array[
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'on_behalfs'
  ];
begin
  foreach v_table in array v_tables loop
    execute format(
      'drop trigger if exists trg_%1$s_in_use_guard on public.%1$I',
      v_table
    );
    execute format(
      'create trigger trg_%1$s_in_use_guard before update on public.%1$I '
      'for each row execute function public.enforce_reference_not_in_use()',
      v_table
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. purge_tombstones: skip a blocked row instead of failing as a whole
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- Only this function's inner loop changes. The retention argument and its
-- default, the `now() - make_interval(...)` cutoff, the children-first order and
-- the returned count of deleted rows are the shipped ones verbatim, so the
-- scheduled call keeps its meaning and `schema_contract_test.dart`'s order
-- assertions still describe the body.

create or replace function public.purge_tombstones(p_retention_days integer default 180)
returns integer
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_cutoff timestamptz;
  v_table text;
  v_id text;
  v_deleted integer;
  v_total integer := 0;
  v_skipped integer := 0;
  -- Children before parents: the FK graph is case data -> cases -> the
  -- reference tables that cases point at, with case_categories and
  -- court_categories last. Deleting in this order never trips a foreign key for
  -- a row that is itself purgeable, so the skip below is reserved for the rows
  -- a **live** or not-yet-purgeable dependent still names.
  v_order text[] := array[
    'case_history',
    'delete_requests',
    'conflict_log',
    'notes',
    'case_references',
    'cases',
    'case_types',
    'steps',
    'courts',
    'case_categories',
    'on_behalfs',
    'court_categories'
  ];
begin
  -- server_updated_at is stamped by the delete transition itself, so it is the
  -- tombstone's age.
  v_cutoff := now() - make_interval(days => p_retention_days);

  foreach v_table in array v_order loop
    -- One candidate at a time. A row a dependent still names raises
    -- foreign_key_violation on its own DELETE, and this block skips that row
    -- alone: the shipped set-based statement let one such row abort every other
    -- tombstone's purge on the project.
    for v_id in execute format(
      'select id from public.%1$I where is_deleted = true '
      'and server_updated_at < $1',
      v_table
    ) using v_cutoff loop
      begin
        execute format('delete from public.%1$I where id = $1', v_table)
          using v_id;

        get diagnostics v_deleted = row_count;
        v_total := v_total + v_deleted;
      exception
        when foreign_key_violation then
          v_skipped := v_skipped + 1;
      end;
    end loop;
  end loop;

  -- Say so: the job runs daily from pg_cron, where a silent skip is invisible.
  if v_skipped > 0 then
    raise notice
      'purge_tombstones: % tombstone(s) kept; a dependent row still names them.',
      v_skipped;
  end if;

  return v_total;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.purge_tombstones(integer) is
  'Deletes soft-deleted rows older than the retention (180 days by default), children first, and skips (rather than fails on) any tombstone a dependent row still names — one blocked row used to abort the whole purge. Returns the number of rows actually deleted; the skipped ones are reported in a notice.';
```

## App Version 0.0.531 — Firm Mode Phase 7 — The Stored Tier And The Ten-Plan Ladder

### 0.0.531 · `20261016120000_firm_mode_stored_tier.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-16.** Firm mode: the stored subscription tier and the ten-plan ladder. profiles and firms each gain tier, tier_pending and tier_pending_from, so which tier applies to an account or a chamber is a stored fact rather than something each screen infers from a payment row. effective_tier() answers which tier is in force — a pending change takes hold on its own date and not before, so an approval still being settled does not open a gate early and a mid-term downgrade is honoured when it is due — and tier_rank() gives the ladder one order (free 0, pro 1, firm 2, firm_plus 3) for every comparison to share. The plan approval is rebuilt around the ten flat prices, so the withdrawn discount model no longer decides what a plan costs, and the plan-name columns are rebuilt for the ten keys. profiles and firms each carried a table-level insert grant for authenticated and anon, which reaches a column added later, so both are narrowed to the columns that were writable before; the tier is not client-writable at insert either.

```sql
-- Firm Mode Phase 7 — the stored subscription tier — together with Phase 8's
-- ten-plan ladder, which cannot land after it (see Phase 7's hazard in
-- `docs/firm_mode_blueprint.md`: no Firm plan key exists until the ladder does,
-- and the gate this phase's sibling migration adds is unsafe without one).
--
-- Two things land together because they cannot be separated: `approve_payment`
-- is rebuilt to accept the ladder's ten plan keys, and it is the write path that
-- records **which tier** the purchase bought. Before this migration the tier was
-- derived from `is_premium()` and from nothing else, so the lapse allowance
-- (§5.2) and the join-time seat check (§5.4) had no source for "the tier it last
-- held" and neither rule was expressible.
--
-- What the ladder is (Task 21's ruling, from `docs/firm_mode_blueprint.md` §5.3):
--
--   Pro        1 / 3 / 6 / 12 months at ৳100 / ৳285 / ৳540 / ৳1,000
--   Firm                     3 / 6 / 12 months at ৳855 / ৳1,620 / ৳3,000
--   Firm Plus                3 / 6 / 12 months at ৳1,710 / ৳3,240 / ৳6,000
--
-- Ten keys, at flat prices: the percentage-discount story is withdrawn, so Pro's
-- annual moves from the shipped ৳960 to ৳1,000 as a **deliberate price rise** and
-- every other price is simply its price.
--
-- Why the tier is stored rather than derived:
--
--   * the tier in force must survive a lapse, because the allowance a lapsed
--     account falls back to is *the tier it last held* (Pro 100, Firm 500,
--     Firm Plus 1,000 cases) — a derived value would read Free the moment
--     expiry passed and every lapsed account would fall to the 50-case wall;
--   * a mid-term downgrade must not overwrite the tier that was paid for, so a
--     lower-tier purchase writes `tier_pending` / `tier_pending_from` instead and
--     every reader takes the **effective** tier.
--
-- Client **update** writes to the new columns are closed by construction:
-- `20260929102500_phase3_column_privileges.sql` grants only `update (full_name)`
-- on `profiles` and `update (name)` on `firms`, and the default is to deny any
-- column a later migration adds. Client **insert** writes were not: both tables
-- carry a *table-level* `insert` for `authenticated` and `anon`
-- (`{anon=ardDxtm/postgres,authenticated=ardDxtm/postgres}`), and a table-level
-- grant reaches every column added afterwards. With `firms_insert_owner`
-- (`with check (owner_id = auth.uid())`) that was enough for any signed-in
-- account to mint a chamber whose stored tier said `firm_plus` without paying —
-- through the front door the gate below exists to hold shut. Section 2 therefore
-- narrows both grants to the columns that were public before this migration; the
-- only writer of `tier` is then the controlled admin path below.
--
-- Table class: `profiles` and `firms` remain **pull-only caches** on the device
-- and server-owned rows here; `payment_submissions` / `payment_approval_events`
-- remain **server-managed** (no client write policy exists for either). This
-- migration runs as the controlled admin write that re-issuing a function under
-- its existing grants requires.
--
-- APPLIED to the live project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` on 2026-10-16, in file
-- order after `20261016110000_firm_mode_reference_in_use_guard.sql` and before
-- `20261016130000_firm_mode_seat_cap_and_creation_gate.sql`, and recorded in
-- `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, so `supabase db push` skips it.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/firm_mode_stored_tier_test.sql`, which was run
-- against the applied project: the ladder prices all ten keys, the stored tier
-- follows them, a lapse keeps the tier, a downgrade waits its turn, and the
-- creation gate is Firm or above.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The stored tier, on both the account and the chamber.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists tier text not null default 'free',
  add column if not exists tier_pending text,
  add column if not exists tier_pending_from timestamptz;

comment on column public.profiles.tier is
  'The subscription tier this account holds: free / pro / firm / firm_plus. Written at approval and never cleared by expiry, so it is the record of the last tier held — which is the allowance a lapse falls back to.';
comment on column public.profiles.tier_pending is
  'The tier a mid-term downgrade will fall to when the paid period ends, or null when no downgrade is waiting. The tier in force is never overwritten mid-term.';
comment on column public.profiles.tier_pending_from is
  'The expiry instant at which tier_pending starts. Readers take the effective tier — tier until this moment, then tier_pending.';

alter table public.firms
  add column if not exists tier text not null default 'free',
  add column if not exists tier_pending text,
  add column if not exists tier_pending_from timestamptz;

comment on column public.firms.tier is
  'The chamber tier, mirrored from its owner''s plan. The seat cap reads this (Pro 0, Firm 5, Firm Plus 20) and a lapsed member falls back to its allowance.';
comment on column public.firms.tier_pending is
  'The tier a mid-term downgrade will fall to, mirrored from the owner.';
comment on column public.firms.tier_pending_from is
  'The expiry instant at which firms.tier_pending starts.';

-- The stored value is a key, so it is constrained to the ladder's own keys. A
-- CHECK rather than an enum: a later tier is one migration, not a type change.
alter table public.profiles
  drop constraint if exists profiles_tier_check;
alter table public.profiles
  add constraint profiles_tier_check
  check (tier in ('free', 'pro', 'firm', 'firm_plus'));
alter table public.profiles
  drop constraint if exists profiles_tier_pending_check;
alter table public.profiles
  add constraint profiles_tier_pending_check
  check (tier_pending is null or tier_pending in ('free', 'pro', 'firm', 'firm_plus'));

alter table public.firms
  drop constraint if exists firms_tier_check;
alter table public.firms
  add constraint firms_tier_check
  check (tier in ('free', 'pro', 'firm', 'firm_plus'));
alter table public.firms
  drop constraint if exists firms_tier_pending_check;
alter table public.firms
  add constraint firms_tier_pending_check
  check (tier_pending is null or tier_pending in ('free', 'pro', 'firm', 'firm_plus'));

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The new columns are not client-writable, at insert as well as at update.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- `revoke` first, then grant the column list back: a column-level `revoke`
-- cannot take a privilege away from a role that holds it at table level, so the
-- only reliable order is to drop the table-level grant and re-grant the exact
-- set that was writable before these columns existed. Nothing that worked before
-- stops working — an insert that named one of these columns still names it — and
-- no column added by a later migration inherits a write grant.
--
-- The three tier columns are absent from both lists deliberately.
revoke insert on public.profiles from authenticated, anon;
grant insert (
  id, full_name, firm_id, role, subscription_status, subscription_expiry,
  created_at, last_successful_sync_at, email, bar_association, membership_no,
  office_address, mobile_no
) on public.profiles to authenticated, anon;

revoke insert on public.firms from authenticated, anon;
grant insert (
  id, name, owner_id, created_at, subscription_status, subscription_expiry
) on public.firms to authenticated, anon;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. The effective tier, as one function.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- "The tier in force right now", which is `tier` until the instant a waiting
-- downgrade starts and `tier_pending` from that instant on. Every reader takes
-- this rather than the raw column, so no gate re-implements the waiting rule.
--
-- `stable`, not `immutable`, and the label is load-bearing: the body reads
-- `now()`, so the same arguments do **not** always give the same answer. Marking
-- it immutable would let the planner fold one call at plan time and reuse that
-- answer for the rest of the statement — the exact mid-term flip this function
-- exists to express, frozen.
create or replace function public.effective_tier(p_tier text, p_pending text, p_from timestamptz)
returns text
language sql
stable
as $$
  select case
    when p_pending is null then coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
    when p_from is not null and now() >= p_from then p_pending
    else coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
  end;
$$;

comment on function public.effective_tier(text, text, timestamptz) is
  'The subscription tier in force right now: the stored tier until a waiting downgrade starts, the pending tier from that instant on. One definition, so no gate re-implements the mid-term rule.';

-- The ladder's order, so "is this an upgrade?" is one comparison rather than a
-- chain of inequalities repeated in every write path. Defined here, before
-- `approve_payment` below uses it.
create or replace function public.tier_rank(p_tier text)
returns integer
language sql
immutable
as $$
  select case coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
    when 'pro' then 1
    when 'firm' then 2
    when 'firm_plus' then 3
    else 0
  end;
$$;

comment on function public.tier_rank(text) is
  'The ladder''s order: free 0, pro 1, firm 2, firm_plus 3. Used to decide upgrade versus downgrade in one comparison.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. `approve_payment` rebuilt to the ten keys, writing the tier.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.approve_payment(payment_submission_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- Configured plan prices, in BDT, one named constant per plan. A price change
  -- is then one migration, and the RPC validates the amount the server believes
  -- rather than the amount the client sent.
  c_pro_monthly_bdt constant integer := 100;
  c_pro_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 285;
  c_pro_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 540;
  c_pro_annual_bdt constant integer := 1000;
  c_firm_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 855;
  c_firm_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 1620;
  c_firm_annual_bdt constant integer := 3000;
  c_firm_plus_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 1710;
  c_firm_plus_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 3240;
  c_firm_plus_annual_bdt constant integer := 6000;

  v_submission public.payment_submissions%rowtype;
  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
  v_event public.payment_approval_events%rowtype;
  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
  v_new_expiry timestamptz;
  v_plan_amount integer;
  v_plan_months integer;
  v_tier text;
  v_effective text;
begin
  -- A GRANT to `authenticated` is not authorization: every caller shares that
  -- database role, so the registry itself decides.
  if not public.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'admin_required' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- Missing rows return a status without revealing anything about other users.
  select * into v_submission
    from public.payment_submissions s
   where s.id = payment_submission_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- The parameter has the same name as the column, and `payment_approval_events`
  -- has that column, so the reference must be qualified: unqualified it is
  -- ambiguous and the function fails with "It could refer to either a PL/pgSQL
  -- variable or a table column" the first time it is called.
  select * into v_event
    from public.payment_approval_events e
   where e.payment_submission_id = approve_payment.payment_submission_id;

  -- Idempotent retries: a duplicate call can never extend expiry twice.
  if v_submission.status = 'approved' then
    if found then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'already_approved',
        'new_expiry', v_event.new_expiry
      );
    end if;
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_resolved');
  end if;

  if v_submission.status <> 'pending' then
    -- A rejected submission needs a separately audited reset; approval is not
    -- a back door around that.
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_resolved');
  end if;

  -- The ladder's ten keys and nothing else. Each `case` below is written over
  -- this same set, so a key cannot be accepted for its price but have no
  -- duration, or name a tier that does not exist.
  if v_submission.plan_type not in (
    'monthly', 'quarterly', 'half_yearly', 'annual',
    'firm_quarterly', 'firm_half_yearly', 'firm_annual',
    'firm_plus_quarterly', 'firm_plus_half_yearly', 'firm_plus_annual'
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_plan');
  end if;

  -- Each plan's own amount. The CASE is parenthesized because plpgsql reads an
  -- IF condition up to the first top-level `then`; an unwrapped CASE ends it at
  -- its own `when ... then` and the function then fails to compile with
  -- "syntax error at end of input".
  v_plan_amount := (case v_submission.plan_type
    when 'monthly' then c_pro_monthly_bdt
    when 'quarterly' then c_pro_quarterly_bdt
    when 'half_yearly' then c_pro_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'annual' then c_pro_annual_bdt
    when 'firm_quarterly' then c_firm_quarterly_bdt
    when 'firm_half_yearly' then c_firm_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'firm_annual' then c_firm_annual_bdt
    when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then c_firm_plus_quarterly_bdt
    when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then c_firm_plus_half_yearly_bdt
    else c_firm_plus_annual_bdt
  end);

  if v_submission.amount <> v_plan_amount then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_amount');
  end if;

  -- Each plan's own duration, so the interval can never disagree with the
  -- amount validated above. A chamber buys 3, 6 or 12 months: there is no
  -- one-month Firm key to reach this CASE.
  v_plan_months := (case v_submission.plan_type
    when 'monthly' then 1
    when 'quarterly' then 3
    when 'half_yearly' then 6
    when 'annual' then 12
    when 'firm_quarterly' then 3
    when 'firm_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'firm_annual' then 12
    when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then 3
    when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then 6
    else 12
  end);

  -- Which tier the purchase bought, from the key alone.
  v_tier := (case
    when v_submission.plan_type in ('monthly', 'quarterly', 'half_yearly', 'annual')
      then 'pro'
    when v_submission.plan_type in ('firm_quarterly', 'firm_half_yearly', 'firm_annual')
      then 'firm'
    else 'firm_plus'
  end);

  select * into v_profile
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_submission.user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- Server time decides the base; a lapsed-but-not-expired window is not lost.
  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;
  v_new_expiry := greatest(coalesce(v_previous_expiry, now()), now())
    + make_interval(months => v_plan_months);

  -- The tier in force, as it stands *before* this approval: a waiting downgrade
  -- that has started already counts, so buying during it does not resurrect the
  -- older tier.
  v_effective := public.effective_tier(
    v_profile.tier, v_profile.tier_pending, v_profile.tier_pending_from
  );

  -- The tier story, as one rule set (§5.4):
  --
  --   * an **upgrade or renewal at or above the tier in force** takes effect
  --     immediately and clears any waiting downgrade;
  --   * a **downgrade** never overwrites the tier that was paid for: it writes
  --     the pending pair, starting when the current period ends, and the tier in
  --     force is untouched.
  --
  -- Free is ranked below every paid tier, so an account whose first purchase is
  -- Pro is an upgrade, not a downgrade.
  if public.tier_rank(v_tier) >= public.tier_rank(v_effective) then
    update public.profiles p
       set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
           subscription_status = 'premium',
           tier = v_tier,
           tier_pending = null,
           tier_pending_from = null
     where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
  else
    update public.profiles p
       set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
           subscription_status = 'premium',
           tier_pending = v_tier,
           tier_pending_from = v_new_expiry
     where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
  end if;

  update public.payment_submissions s
     set status = 'approved',
         approved_at = now(),
         approved_by = auth.uid(),
         updated_at = (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint
   where s.id = payment_submission_id;

  -- Exactly one immutable event per submission (UNIQUE on the FK).
  insert into public.payment_approval_events (
    payment_submission_id, user_id, approved_by, plan_type, amount,
    previous_expiry, new_expiry
  )
  values (
    payment_submission_id, v_submission.user_id, auth.uid(),
    v_submission.plan_type, v_submission.amount,
    v_previous_expiry, v_new_expiry
  );

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'approved',
    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
    'new_expiry', v_new_expiry,
    'tier', v_tier
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.approve_payment(uuid) is
  'Approves one pending payment and extends the buyer''s subscription by the plan''s own duration. Task 21''s ten-plan ladder: Pro 1/3/6/12 months, Firm and Firm Plus 3/6/12. Writes the stored tier — immediately for an upgrade or renewal, as a pending downgrade otherwise. Idempotent: a repeat call never extends expiry twice.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The mirror carries the tier to the chamber.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm` fired on `subscription_expiry` changes
-- only and copied two columns, so a **tier-only** change would never reach the
-- firm and the seat cap would read a stale value. Both its `of` list and its
-- `when` are widened here.
--
-- `tier_rank` is defined above `approve_payment` uses it and before this
-- function is replaced, so the whole file applies in one pass in order.
create or replace function public.mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_tier text;
begin
  if new.firm_id is null then
    return new;
  end if;

  -- The tier the account actually holds, mid-term downgrade included.
  v_tier := public.effective_tier(new.tier, new.tier_pending, new.tier_pending_from);

  update public.firms f
     set subscription_status = new.subscription_status,
         subscription_expiry = new.subscription_expiry,
         tier = v_tier,
         tier_pending = new.tier_pending,
         tier_pending_from = new.tier_pending_from
   where f.owner_id = new.id;

  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm() is
  'Mirrors the owner''s subscription onto the chamber they own: status, expiry and the effective tier (with the pending pair), so the seat cap and a member''s allowance read the chamber''s own row.';

-- The live trigger is `trg_profiles_mirror_owner_subscription`, firing on
-- `update of subscription_expiry` **and** guarded by a `when` clause that only
-- let an expiry change through. Both halves had to be widened, and the trigger
-- is therefore replaced rather than edited: a tier-only change would otherwise
-- never reach the firm and the seat cap would read a stale tier.
--
-- Both names are dropped because the shipped name is the `trg_profiles_` one and
-- an earlier draft of this migration used the other; dropping both leaves
-- exactly one trigger, whichever name applied. A `when` clause is deliberately
-- omitted: the wider `of` list is the gate, and a row where none of those five
-- columns changed is not reached in the first place.
drop trigger if exists trg_profiles_mirror_owner_subscription on public.profiles;
drop trigger if exists trg_mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm on public.profiles;
create trigger trg_profiles_mirror_owner_subscription
  after update of
    subscription_status, subscription_expiry,
    tier, tier_pending, tier_pending_from
  on public.profiles
  for each row
  execute function public.mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. The readable plan names, extended to the ladder.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `plan_name` is a GENERATED column, so its CASE cannot be altered in place:
-- the column is dropped and re-added with the wider CASE. That is safe here
-- because nothing writes it (it derives from `plan_type` on every read), so
-- every existing row is recomputed from its key and no value is lost.
alter table public.payment_submissions drop column if exists plan_name;
alter table public.payment_submissions
  add column plan_name text
  generated always as (
    case plan_type
      when 'monthly' then 'Pro · 1 Month'
      when 'quarterly' then 'Pro · 3 Months'
      when 'half_yearly' then 'Pro · 6 Months'
      when 'annual' then 'Pro · 1 Year'
      when 'firm_quarterly' then 'Firm · 3 Months'
      when 'firm_half_yearly' then 'Firm · 6 Months'
      when 'firm_annual' then 'Firm · 1 Year'
      when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then 'Firm Plus · 3 Months'
      when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then 'Firm Plus · 6 Months'
      when 'firm_plus_annual' then 'Firm Plus · 1 Year'
      else plan_type
    end
  ) stored;

comment on column public.payment_submissions.plan_name is
  'Readable name of the plan the submission pays for, derived from plan_type (Pro · 1 Month through Firm Plus · 1 Year). Generated, so it cannot disagree with the key; the app localizes its own labels from plan_type.';

alter table public.payment_approval_events drop column if exists plan_name;
alter table public.payment_approval_events
  add column plan_name text
  generated always as (
    case plan_type
      when 'monthly' then 'Pro · 1 Month'
      when 'quarterly' then 'Pro · 3 Months'
      when 'half_yearly' then 'Pro · 6 Months'
      when 'annual' then 'Pro · 1 Year'
      when 'firm_quarterly' then 'Firm · 3 Months'
      when 'firm_half_yearly' then 'Firm · 6 Months'
      when 'firm_annual' then 'Firm · 1 Year'
      when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then 'Firm Plus · 3 Months'
      when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then 'Firm Plus · 6 Months'
      when 'firm_plus_annual' then 'Firm Plus · 1 Year'
      else plan_type
    end
  ) stored;

comment on column public.payment_approval_events.plan_name is
  'Readable name of the plan this approval event recorded, derived from plan_type. Generated, so the immutable ledger carries a name that can never disagree with its key.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 7. Grants, unchanged in shape.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `approve_payment` is re-issued under its existing grants: CREATE OR REPLACE
-- preserves them, and `effective_tier` / `tier_rank` are helpers for the
-- definer-owned paths, so they are not exposed to `authenticated`.
revoke all on function public.effective_tier(text, text, timestamptz) from public;
revoke all on function public.tier_rank(text) from public;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 8. The one-time backfill: the tier an existing account already holds.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The columns arrive with `default 'free'`, which is the right answer for an
-- account that never paid and the wrong one for the account that is paying
-- right now: every existing row would read `free`, so a chamber that answers 5
-- seats today would answer **no cap at all** — `firm_seat_cap` reads its tier,
-- and `join_firm` skips its whole seat check when that answer is null — and
-- §5.2's lapse allowance would read `free` for an account whose last tier was
-- Pro. The stored tier is a fact about the past that the schema has only just
-- learned how to record, so it is reconstructed rather than defaulted.
--
-- Two sources, in the order that matters: the payment ledger says what was
-- bought (`approve_payment` below writes exactly this reading for every future
-- purchase), and `is_premium()` covers a live entitlement the ledger has no row
-- for, such as a period granted from the dashboard. An account whose period has
-- run out *and* whose submission is in the ledger keeps `pro` — that is what
-- "the tier it last held" means, and it is why the ledger is read and not only
-- the live expiry. Nothing higher can pre-exist this migration: no Firm or Firm
-- Plus key was ever purchasable before it, so `pro` is the only paid tier an
-- existing row can be owed.
update public.profiles p
   set tier = 'pro'
 where p.tier = 'free'
   and (
     public.is_premium(p.id)
     or exists (
       select 1
         from public.payment_submissions s
        where s.user_id = p.id
          and s.status = 'approved'
          and s.plan_type in ('monthly', 'quarterly', 'half_yearly', 'annual')
     )
   );

-- The chamber's copy, by the rule the mirror uses: the tier in force. Written
-- out here rather than left to `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` for two
-- reasons — the mirror returns early for a profile with no `firm_id`, and a
-- backfill must not depend on a trigger reading the row it has just changed.
update public.firms f
   set tier = public.effective_tier(p.tier, p.tier_pending, p.tier_pending_from)
  from public.profiles p
 where f.owner_id = p.id;
```

## App Version 0.0.532 — Firm Mode Phase 8 — The Seat Cap Reads The Tier, And A Chamber Needs Firm

### 0.0.532 · `20261016130000_firm_mode_seat_cap_and_creation_gate.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-16.** Firm mode: the seat cap reads the stored tier, and a chamber needs Firm. firm_seat_cap() previously asked is_premium(owner) and answered 5 for anyone premium, so a Firm Plus chamber was capped at the Firm number and a Pro owner had a chamber nobody could join; it now reads the tier in force — Firm 5, Firm Plus 20, Pro 0 — through effective_tier, so the cap a mid-downgrade chamber enforces is the one it has paid for. ensure_firm()'s creation gate moves from is_premium() to Firm or above, because Pro's cap of 0 means a chamber on Pro could never take a member; the refusal keeps the status shape the client already handles but names the reason firm_tier_required, so a paying Pro user is not told they are not premium. A newly created chamber starts on its owner's tier, because the cap reads that row and a chamber left at the column default would answer null — no cap enforced — for every join. A seat cap binds new joins only: neither function removes a member, and no membership row is touched.

```sql
-- Firm Mode Phase 7, the behavioural half — the seat cap reads the stored tier,
-- and a chamber needs Firm. (The blueprint numbers these two phases the other way
-- round: Phase 7 is the stored tier plus this gate, Phase 8 is the ten-plan
-- ladder that `20261016120000` also carries. Both files landed in one pass, as
-- Phase 7's hazard requires.)
--
-- Both functions below were written before the tier existed. They are rebuilt
-- here, after `20261016120000_firm_mode_stored_tier.sql` added the columns and
-- the ladder's keys, because both now read those columns and neither could have
-- been expressed before them.
--
-- The two rules this migration is:
--
--   1. **`firm_seat_cap` reads the chamber's tier** (blueprint Phase 8): Pro 0,
--      Firm 5, Firm Plus 20. It previously asked `is_premium(owner)` and
--      answered 5 for anyone premium, so a Firm Plus chamber was capped at the
--      Firm number and a Pro owner's chamber — which cannot seat anybody — was
--      capped at 5. A cap that does not know the tier cannot enforce §5.4's
--      ceilings.
--
--   2. **Creating a chamber needs the Firm tier or above** (blueprint Phase 8,
--      user ruling): `ensure_firm`'s gate moves from `is_premium()` to the tier.
--      Pro's cap is 0, so a Pro owner could otherwise build a chamber nobody can
--      be invited into — the gate belongs with the cap, not with a bare premium
--      check. The refusal keeps the same `status` shape the client already
--      handles and names the reason in a new key rather than reusing
--      `premium_required`, which would tell a paying Pro user they are not
--      premium.
--
-- A seat cap binds **new joins only**: nobody is auto-removed by a billing
-- change (blueprint §5.4). Neither function here removes a member, and this
-- migration touches no membership row.
--
-- The cap is `null` for a chamber with no paid tier. In the join path a null
-- cap is **not** a refusal: `join_firm` skips its whole seat block when the cap
-- is null, so null means "no cap is enforced here". That is the existing
-- behaviour and it is unchanged by this migration — which is exactly why the
-- chamber's tier has to be right from its first moment, and why the creation
-- below now writes it (see `ensure_firm`, step 2). A chamber created by an
-- account that holds a tier would otherwise sit at the column default, `free`,
-- cap null, and take members without a ceiling until its owner's subscription
-- next changed.
--
-- Table class: `firms` stays a server-owned row and a **pull-only cache** on the
-- device; `firm_members` is unchanged, and no policy is added or dropped here.
--
-- APPLIED to the live project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` on 2026-10-16, after
-- `20261016120000_firm_mode_stored_tier.sql` — it reads the `firms.tier` column
-- that migration adds — and recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/firm_mode_stored_tier_test.sql` and re-checked by
-- `supabase/tests/firm_mode_join_gate_test.sql`, both run against the applied
-- project: a Pro chamber answers 0 seats, a Firm chamber 5, and a free or Pro
-- caller is refused at the creation gate with `firm_tier_required`.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The seat cap, by the chamber's stored tier.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The tier is read through `effective_tier` so a chamber mid-downgrade is capped
-- by the tier actually in force, not by the newer one it has not paid for yet.
-- `create or replace`, never `drop function`: a dropped function is a new
-- object, and a new function carries Postgres's default of execute for PUBLIC,
-- which undoes the revoke `20261015120000_firm_mode_join_gate.sql` made. The
-- explicit revoke/grant pair at the foot of this file states the answer anyway.
create or replace function public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select case public.effective_tier(f.tier, f.tier_pending, f.tier_pending_from)
           when 'firm' then 5
           when 'firm_plus' then 20
           -- Pro's cap is 0, and the arm had to be written out: `else null`
           -- would engulf it, and a null answer is not a small ceiling but no
           -- ceiling at all — `join_firm` runs its seat check only when this
           -- answer is not null, so a Pro chamber would take unlimited
           -- associates. Pro takes nobody new, which is what makes the creation
           -- gate below the coherent answer rather than a warning. Only "no tier
           -- in force" — free, or a lapse with no paid history — is null, which
           -- §2.4 keeps joinable.
           when 'pro' then 0
           else null
         end
    from public.firms f
   where f.id = p_firm_id;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) is
  'How many associates a chamber may hold: Firm 5, Firm Plus 20, Pro 0 (no join may be taken), null when the chamber holds no paid tier. Read from the chamber''s stored, effective tier — a cap binds new joins only and never removes a member.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The chamber-creation gate: Firm or above.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `ensure_firm` is ~5.4 KB and two things in it change: its gate, and the tier
-- the chamber is created with. The whole body is re-issued with only those two
-- touched — the membership guard, the idempotent re-call, the stamping of
-- existing rows on a first creation and the rename path are otherwise the version
-- in `20261015110000_firm_mode_creation_and_scope.sql`, so a re-issue cannot
-- silently change behaviour.
create or replace function public.ensure_firm(p_name text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_now bigint := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;
  v_name text := pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_name, ''));
  v_firm public.firms%rowtype;
  v_has_firm boolean;
  -- True only when this call created the firm: the stamping below is the
  -- creation's own act, and an idempotent re-call (a rename, a repair) must not
  -- re-stamp rows a member has since written.
  v_created boolean := false;
  v_table text;
  v_case_tables text[] := array[
    'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references'
  ];
  v_reference_tables text[] := array[
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  ];
  -- The tier required to create a chamber (Phase 7's behavioural half): Firm is
  -- rank 2 on the ladder free 0 / pro 1 / firm 2 / firm_plus 3.
  c_required_tier_rank constant integer := 2;
  v_profile_tier text;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_firm
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_user_id
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1;
  -- Captured immediately: `FOUND` belongs to the most recent SQL statement, and
  -- the membership guard below runs one of its own.
  v_has_firm := found;

  -- Membership guard: refuse to become the owner of a new firm while the
  -- caller's profile points at a firm they do not own. Returned rather than
  -- raised so the answer is a value the client can report; nothing is written.
  if exists (
    select 1
      from public.profiles p
     where p.id = v_user_id
       and p.firm_id is not null
       and (not v_has_firm or p.firm_id is distinct from v_firm.id)
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'member_of_another_firm');
  end if;

  if not v_has_firm then
    -- The transition to firm mode is the tier-gated step. The gate is Firm or
    -- above rather than premium, because Pro's seat cap is 0: a chamber on Pro
    -- could never take a member, so Pro must not be able to build one. The tier
    -- in force is read, so an approval still being settled does not open the
    -- gate early and a mid-term downgrade is honoured on its own date.
    select public.effective_tier(p.tier, p.tier_pending, p.tier_pending_from)
      into v_profile_tier
      from public.profiles p
     where p.id = v_user_id;

    if public.tier_rank(v_profile_tier) < c_required_tier_rank then
      -- A distinct reason from `premium_required`: a paying Pro user told they
      -- are "not premium" would be told something untrue. The status is a value
      -- the client already reports, so no new handling shape is needed.
      return jsonb_build_object('status', 'firm_tier_required');
    end if;

    -- `created_at` is a server instant (`timestamptz`) and takes the column
    -- default: the bigint `v_now` below is epoch ms for the client-facing
    -- `firm_members` stamps only.
    --
    -- The chamber takes its owner's tier here, in the same statement that makes
    -- it, because the seat cap reads this row: a chamber left at the column
    -- default would answer `null` — no cap enforced — for every join until the
    -- owner's subscription next changed, which is the opposite of the ceiling
    -- this migration exists to enforce. The gate above has already read the
    -- effective tier into `v_profile_tier`, so the chamber starts on exactly the
    -- tier the gate allowed, and the mirror keeps it there from the next
    -- approval on.
    insert into public.firms (
      name, owner_id, subscription_status, subscription_expiry,
      tier, tier_pending, tier_pending_from
    )
    select
      v_name,
      v_user_id,
      p.subscription_status,
      p.subscription_expiry,
      v_profile_tier,
      p.tier_pending,
      p.tier_pending_from
      from public.profiles p
     where p.id = v_user_id
    returning * into v_firm;

    if not found then
      -- No profile row: the sign-up trigger creates one, so this is a bug state,
      -- never something to explain to a user. Raising here rolls the firm back.
      raise exception 'ensure_firm: no profiles row for the caller'
        using errcode = 'P0001';
    end if;

    v_created := true;
  elsif v_name is distinct from v_firm.name then
    update public.firms f
       set name = v_name
     where f.id = v_firm.id
    returning * into v_firm;
  end if;

  -- The conversion itself: firm scope for every policy, owner role for the app.
  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = v_firm.id,
         role = 'owner'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  -- The owner holds every permission explicitly, so `can_edit_firm` /
  -- `can_delete_firm` and the client's cached flags agree with the role.
  insert into public.firm_members (
    firm_id, user_id, role, can_add, can_edit, can_delete,
    synced_at, permissions_synced_at
  )
  values (
    v_firm.id, v_user_id, 'owner', true, true, true, v_now, v_now
  )
  on conflict (firm_id, user_id) do update
    set role = 'owner',
        can_add = true,
        can_edit = true,
        can_delete = true,
        synced_at = excluded.synced_at,
        permissions_synced_at = excluded.permissions_synced_at;

  -- Sharing the diary: every ledger row the owner authored while firm-less
  -- becomes the chamber's (§1). The four case-data tables first, then the six
  -- reference tables — custom rows only, because a built-in row (`is_custom =
  -- false`) has no author and is the globally shared baseline every install
  -- reads — and finally the owner's pending delete requests.
  if v_created then
    foreach v_table in array v_case_tables loop
      execute format(
        'update public.%I t '
        '   set firm_id = $1, '
        '       version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
        '       updated_at = $3 '
        ' where t.user_id = $2 '
        '   and t.firm_id is null',
        v_table
      ) using v_firm.id, v_user_id, v_now;
    end loop;

    foreach v_table in array v_reference_tables loop
      execute format(
        'update public.%I t '
        '   set firm_id = $1, '
        '       version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
        '       updated_at = $3 '
        ' where t.user_id = $2 '
        '   and t.firm_id is null '
        '   and t.is_custom = true',
        v_table
      ) using v_firm.id, v_user_id, v_now;
    end loop;

    -- A resolved request is audit history rather than a ledger row, so only a
    -- pending one follows the owner into his chamber.
    update public.delete_requests t
       set firm_id = v_firm.id,
           version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1,
           updated_at = v_now
     where t.requested_by = v_user_id
       and t.firm_id is null
       and t.status = 'pending';
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ready',
    'firm_id', v_firm.id,
    'name', v_firm.name
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.ensure_firm(text) is
  'Creates (or renames) the calling user''s chamber and moves them into it as owner. Requires the Firm tier or above: Pro''s seat cap is 0, so a chamber on Pro could never take a member. Idempotent — a re-call renames rather than re-creating, and only a first creation stamps the user''s existing rows with the firm.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Grants: the same shape as `20261015120000`, restated.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `create or replace` preserves a function's ACL, so nothing here is strictly
-- required — but the ACL is then only a fact about an earlier file, and the
-- `drop function` this file used to open with is exactly how such a fact gets
-- lost without a red test. Both objects therefore state their own answer:
-- execute for `authenticated` alone, and never PUBLIC, which would hand a
-- signed-out caller the seat count of any chamber id it could guess.
revoke all on function public.ensure_firm(text) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
grant execute on function public.ensure_firm(text) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.534 — Firm Mode Phase 9 — A Member Has No Plan Of Their Own

### 0.0.534 · `20261017100000_firm_mode_member_no_plan.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-17.** Firm mode: a member has no plan of their own. has_sync_entitlement() counted the caller's own expiry OR the chamber's, so a member who had bought a plan before joining kept pushing through the chamber's lapse; it now counts the chamber's mirrored expiry alone once profiles.firm_id is set, and the caller's own only while it is null. payment_submissions_insert_own becomes a member's refusal — user_id = auth.uid() plus no firm, or a firm the caller owns — so an associate or viewer cannot buy a personal plan. The owner is deliberately exempt: the owner's purchase is the chamber's renewal, and the two entries this phase removes from a member are the owner's only routes to it.

```sql
-- Firm mode Phase 9 — a member has no plan of their own.
--
-- Two changes, one rule (§5.1): an account working inside a chamber it does not
-- own is covered by that chamber's subscription, cannot buy a plan of its own,
-- and keeps any plan it bought before joining for the day it is individual
-- again. The server is the boundary; hiding a screen was never one.
--
-- 1. `has_sync_entitlement` counted *the caller's own* expiry OR the firm's.
--    That left the audit's live hole open: a member who had bought Pro before
--    joining kept pushing straight through the chamber's lapse, so the lapse
--    allowance had no server gate behind it for exactly that account. While
--    `profiles.firm_id` is set, only the chamber's mirrored expiry counts now.
--    The owner is covered by the same rule and loses nothing: the existing
--    `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` keeps `firms.subscription_expiry`
--    equal to theirs, and `ensure_firm` copies it when a chamber is created.
--
-- 2. `payment_submissions_insert_own` becomes a member's refusal. The owner is
--    deliberately exempt: the owner's purchase IS the chamber's renewal (that is
--    what a Firm or Firm Plus plan buys), and the two entries Phase 9 removes
--    from a member — Settings > Subscription and the side menu's plan row — are
--    the owner's only routes to that purchase. Refusing every firm holder would
--    make a chamber impossible to renew, so the rule is "a member, not an
--    owner": `current_firm_id()` is null, or it names a chamber the caller owns.
--
-- Applied to the live project on 2026-10-17, and proved by
-- `supabase/tests/firm_mode_member_no_plan_test.sql`.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Entitlement: the chamber's expiry while the account holds a chamber.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Same rule, same signature, same 48-hour grace. The CASE keeps the two
-- branches from ever OR-ing: a firm member never reads their own expiry, and an
-- individual never reads a firm's. Still derived, never `subscription_status`.
create or replace function public.has_sync_entitlement(p_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.profiles p
     where p.id = p_user_id
       and case
             when p.firm_id is not null then exists (
               select 1 from public.firms f
                where f.id = p.firm_id
                  and f.subscription_expiry is not null
                  and f.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' > now()
             )
             else p.subscription_expiry is not null
                  and p.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' > now()
           end
  );
$$;

comment on function public.has_sync_entitlement(uuid) is
  'Sync entitlement = the chamber''s subscription_expiry + 48h grace once profiles.firm_id is set, the caller''s own expiry while it is null; never reads subscription_status.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. A member's payment submission is refused by the policy itself.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `current_firm_id()` and `is_firm_owner()` are SECURITY DEFINER (the Phase 3
-- access helpers), so this policy checks the caller's own profile and chamber
-- without recursing through either table's RLS. The insert still has to name the
-- caller, exactly as before.
drop policy if exists payment_submissions_insert_own on public.payment_submissions;
create policy payment_submissions_insert_own on public.payment_submissions
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    user_id = auth.uid()
    and (
      public.current_firm_id() is null
      or public.is_firm_owner(public.current_firm_id())
    )
  );

-- No UPDATE or DELETE policy: approval is approve_payment() only.
```

## App Version 0.0.536 — Firm Mode Phase 11 — Dissolution Keeps The Ledger

### 0.0.536 · `20261017110000_firm_mode_dissolution.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-17.** Firm mode: dissolution. dissolve_firm() refuses while the roster holds anyone but the owner and carries the count in the refusal, decided before the first write so a refusal retires no invite and moves no row. Once the roster is empty it retires the open invites, then unscopes the eleven ledger tables — firm_id out, the owner in as scope_owner_id, tombstones included — so he keeps a complete ordinary diary while attribution, contents and the sync columns stay exactly as they were. conflict_log is the one exception: its firm_id is cleared, because the foreign key has no cascade and the firms delete would be refused otherwise, and no scope owner is written, so a colleague's merge diagnostics stay with their author. The firms row goes with its memberships and invites, the owner's profile returns to individual mode (which unblocks delete_my_account), and his plan is untouched.

```sql
-- Firm mode (11) — dissolution: the chamber goes, the ledger stays.
--
-- §4.4's ruling, in one function. The owner empties the roster first, using the
-- one removal path there is (§4.1), so every leaving member's device wipes on
-- its own and nothing of the chamber is left on a phone nobody agreed to
-- abandon. Only then does he dissolve, and dissolving transfers the ledger to
-- him rather than deleting it:
--
--   * every row carrying the `firm_id` loses it and gains the owner as its
--     **scope owner**, so his next pull hands him a complete, ordinary diary;
--   * attribution is untouched — `user_id`, `created_by` and `last_modified_by`
--     still say who wrote each row, and `scope_owner_id` is a scope key, not an
--     attribution one;
--   * the `firms` row and its invites go, his account is individual again, and
--     `delete_my_account()` stops refusing him;
--   * his plan is untouched: dissolving is not a cancellation, and the
--     subscription now covers the individual diary.
--
-- Why the scope owner is not optional: with `firm_id` merely nulled, the read
-- policy's individual clause (`user_id = auth.uid()` on a firm-less row) hands
-- every member-authored row back to its author and hides it from the owner —
-- the audit's most serious finding, and the opposite of what a dissolve is for,
-- because under §3.2 the associates write most of a chamber's cases.
--
-- `conflict_log` is the one table that is **not** handed over. A colleague's
-- merge diagnostics are neither the owner's ledger nor its author's to lose, so
-- the dissolve only clears its `firm_id`: the author keeps reading their own
-- rows, the owner never sees them (§4.3). That clear is also load-bearing:
-- `conflict_log.firm_id` references `firms (id)` **without** a cascade, so
-- leaving it in place would make the `firms` delete fail outright.
--
-- Both refusals are decided before the first write, so a refusal changes
-- nothing at all — not even the invites — including the count it reports. The
-- function takes no arguments on purpose: the firm is resolved from the caller,
-- so it can never be aimed at a chamber that is not theirs, and a member gets
-- `not_owner` rather than an error because it is a state the screen can word.

create or replace function public.dissolve_firm()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_members integer;
  v_table text;
  -- The eleven ledger tables — the ones that carry `scope_owner_id`. Read as
  -- §4.4's list: case data, the deletion queue and the editable reference
  -- rows. `conflict_log` is deliberately absent (see above).
  c_ledger constant text[] := array[
    'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references', 'delete_requests',
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  ];
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- The caller's own firm, and only if they own it. Locked, so a dissolve
  -- cannot race a removal into a half-empty roster: the count below is read
  -- under the same lock that the deletion later relies on.
  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1
   for update;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  -- The precondition, counted before the first write: every seat but the
  -- owner's own must be empty. The refusal carries the number so the screen can
  -- say what is left rather than only "no".
  select count(*) into v_members
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id <> v_actor;

  if v_members > 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'members_remaining',
      'members', v_members
    );
  end if;

  -- Open invites are retired first. The rows themselves leave with the `firms`
  -- row below (the foreign key cascades), so this is the statement that states
  -- the intent rather than the one that cleans up: a code issued before the
  -- dissolve must never be able to create a seat in a chamber that no longer
  -- exists, whichever order the cascade is ever changed to.
  update public.firm_invites i
     set revoked = true
   where i.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and i.revoked = false;

  -- The transfer: `firm_id` out, the owner in as scope owner. Tombstones are
  -- included — they are part of the ledger and their `firm_id` would block the
  -- `firms` delete just as a live row would. The sync columns are left to their
  -- triggers: `server_updated_at` is what the owner's next delta pull filters
  -- on, and version, `updated_at`, `is_deleted` and `synced_at` are not this
  -- function's to invent. The permission trigger steps aside here because the
  -- row being written has no firm afterwards, and because this function runs as
  -- its owner rather than as a client role.
  foreach v_table in array c_ledger loop
    execute format(
      'update public.%1$I set firm_id = null, scope_owner_id = $1 where firm_id = $2',
      v_table
    ) using v_actor, v_firm_id;
  end loop;

  -- The one exception: the chamber column goes, the scope owner does not.
  update public.conflict_log c
     set firm_id = null
   where c.firm_id = v_firm_id;

  -- The account is individual again, which is also what unblocks
  -- `delete_my_account()`. Nulling this before the `firms` delete is what the
  -- profile's plain foreign key requires.
  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = null,
         role = 'individual'
   where p.id = v_actor;

  -- The chamber itself. `firm_members` and `firm_invites` cascade; no ledger
  -- row does, because none still names it.
  delete from public.firms f where f.id = v_firm_id;

  -- Other devices of the owner refresh through the same route a removal uses: a
  -- `firm_members` ping on the user topic is the client's account refresh, which
  -- re-reads the profile and drops the cached chamber.
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', v_actor),
    'row_change',
    'user:' || v_actor::text,
    true
  );

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'dissolved', 'firm_id', v_firm_id);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.dissolve_firm() is
  'Owner-only: dissolves the caller''s chamber once its roster holds nobody else. Every ledger row loses firm_id and gains the owner as scope_owner_id (attribution untouched, conflict_log excepted), open invites are retired, the firms row is removed and the account returns to individual. Writes nothing at all when it refuses, and returns {status:members_remaining,members:N} or {status:not_owner}. Takes no arguments: the firm is resolved from the caller.';

revoke all on function public.dissolve_firm() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.dissolve_firm() to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.537 — Firm Mode Phase 12 — Retention And The Recovery Window

### 0.0.537 · `20261017120000_firm_mode_retention_window.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-17.** Firm mode: the retention and recovery window. purge_tombstones() keeps a tombstone 365 days instead of 180, so the device-side extended-offline rule can be 335 days with the same 30-day buffer between them: a device that comes back inside its window still finds every deletion it missed, and one away longer is rebuilt rather than trusted. Only the default and the comments change — the scheduled job calls the function with no argument, and the body (cutoff, children-first order, one-row-at-a-time delete, blocked-tombstone skip) is the shipped one verbatim. mutation_receipts' documented retention is corrected to at least 400 days in the same pass, because the old 210-day invariant was written for a 150-day window.

```sql
-- Firm mode (12) — the retention window moves to 365, and the recovery window to 335.
--
-- §5.5's ruling, and the pair has to move together. A device that has been away
-- cannot tell a row it never saw from one deleted while it was gone, so it is
-- rebuilt rather than trusted once its own time away passes the recovery
-- threshold. That threshold only works while the server still remembers every
-- deletion the device might have missed, so the tombstone retention has to stay
-- **30 days above** the threshold, whatever the numbers are:
--
--   365 days of tombstones - 30 days of buffer = a 335-day recovery window.
--
-- `create or replace` is the whole change. The scheduled job calls
-- `purge_tombstones()` with no argument, so the number lives in this default and
-- nowhere else. The body — the cutoff, the children-first order, the
-- one-row-at-a-time delete and the skip that keeps a blocked tombstone from
-- failing the whole nightly run — is the shipped one verbatim; only the default
-- and the comments change, which is why the order assertions in
-- `test/supabase/schema_contract_test.dart` still describe this body.
--
-- The same ruling corrects `mutation_receipts`' documented retention. Its
-- invariant was "the maximum supported offline window plus a retry buffer",
-- written while that window was 150 days; at 335 it must read **at least 400
-- days** to stay true. No job purges receipts — they leave with the account — so
-- this is a corrected comment rather than a schedule, and it sits on the table
-- where a later cleanup job would meet it.
--
-- The other places the old number lived are corrected beside this file: the
-- original migration's header comment, `lib/sync/recovery_lock.dart`'s constant
-- and doc block, and the generated ledger's section label. A migration on its
-- own would leave the app and the ledger disagreeing, which is exactly what
-- `dart run tool/generate_all_supabase_sql.dart --check` catches.

create or replace function public.purge_tombstones(p_retention_days integer default 365)
returns integer
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_cutoff timestamptz;
  v_table text;
  v_id text;
  v_deleted integer;
  v_total integer := 0;
  v_skipped integer := 0;
  -- Children before parents: the FK graph is case data -> cases -> the
  -- reference tables that cases point at, with case_categories and
  -- court_categories last. Deleting in this order never trips a foreign key for
  -- a row that is itself purgeable, so the skip below is reserved for the rows
  -- a **live** or not-yet-purgeable dependent still names.
  v_order text[] := array[
    'case_history',
    'delete_requests',
    'conflict_log',
    'notes',
    'case_references',
    'cases',
    'case_types',
    'steps',
    'courts',
    'case_categories',
    'on_behalfs',
    'court_categories'
  ];
begin
  -- server_updated_at is stamped by the delete transition itself, so it is the
  -- tombstone's age.
  v_cutoff := now() - make_interval(days => p_retention_days);

  foreach v_table in array v_order loop
    -- One candidate at a time. A row a dependent still names raises
    -- foreign_key_violation on its own DELETE, and this block skips that row
    -- alone: the shipped set-based statement let one such row abort every other
    -- tombstone's purge on the project.
    for v_id in execute format(
      'select id from public.%1$I where is_deleted = true '
      'and server_updated_at < $1',
      v_table
    ) using v_cutoff loop
      begin
        execute format('delete from public.%1$I where id = $1', v_table)
          using v_id;

        get diagnostics v_deleted = row_count;
        v_total := v_total + v_deleted;
      exception
        when foreign_key_violation then
          v_skipped := v_skipped + 1;
      end;
    end loop;
  end loop;

  -- Say so: the job runs daily from pg_cron, where a silent skip is invisible.
  if v_skipped > 0 then
    raise notice
      'purge_tombstones: % tombstone(s) kept; a dependent row still names them.',
      v_skipped;
  end if;

  return v_total;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.purge_tombstones(integer) is
  'Deletes soft-deleted rows older than the retention (365 days by default, 30 days above the 335-day device recovery window), children first, and skips (rather than fails on) any tombstone a dependent row still names — one blocked row used to abort the whole purge. Returns the number of rows actually deleted; the skipped ones are reported in a notice.';

comment on table public.mutation_receipts is
  'Server-internal. Retain at least 400 days — the 335-day maximum supported offline window plus a retry buffer, and inside the 365-day tombstone retention a device recovering from that window relies on — and never purge a receipt still referenced by case_history, conflict_log or an audit record. mutation_id mirrors the client-generated key so a retry returns the original result.';
```

## App Version 0.0.543 — Subscription History — Cancelling A Live Plan

### 0.0.543 · `20261018100000_subscription_cancellation.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-18.** Subscription History — cancelling a live plan, reconstructed. The install that shipped cancellation on 2026-10-18 recorded its version without statements and committed no file, so the app called an RPC the repository could not define and the applier reported it as drift. This section is the table, its own-row SELECT policy, its narrowed grants and cancel_subscription() copied from the applied project's catalogs, kept idempotent so the live project skips it and a fresh project can apply it.

```sql
-- Subscription History — cancelling a live plan, reconstructed from the live
-- project on 2026-10-19.
--
-- **Why this file exists, and why it is a reconstruction.** The cancellation
-- table, its own-row policy and `cancel_subscription()` were applied to the
-- writable project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` on 2026-10-18 under version
-- `20261018100000`, but that version was recorded **without its statements**
-- and no migration file was committed. The app therefore called an RPC that no
-- file in this repository defined, and `tool/apply_supabase_migrations.dart`
-- reported the version as drift. This file is that missing record: the table,
-- policy, grants and function are copied from the applied project's own
-- catalogs (`pg_get_functiondef`, `information_schema`, `pg_policies`,
-- `pg_class`) rather than invented from the client's call sites. The function's
-- logic is byte-for-byte the live one; only its lapse-allowance comment was
-- updated from the old Pro/Firm/Firm Plus numbers to the six-tier ladder's.
--
-- The version in the filename is the version the live project already holds, so
-- the applier skips it there and its history stays truthful. Every statement is
-- idempotent (`if not exists`, `create or replace`, `drop policy if exists`), so
-- a fresh project can apply this file and re-running it changes nothing.
--
-- Table class: `subscription_cancellations` is **server-managed**. Only
-- `cancel_subscription()` writes it, and a signed-in client may select its own
-- rows under RLS; there is deliberately no insert, update or delete policy.
--
-- Proven on 2026-10-19 by running this file inside a rolled-back transaction on
-- the applied project (it re-created the same objects with no error) and by the
-- client's own cancellation cases in
-- `test/features/subscription_details_screen_test.dart`.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The ledger row.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists public.subscription_cancellations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  -- The plan that was running and what was actually paid for it. Both are
  -- nullable because a period granted outside the ladder has no purchase row to
  -- name; the cancellation still happened and its expiry is still a fact.
  plan_type text,
  amount integer,
  -- The expiry that was ended, and the instant it was ended. Both required:
  -- a cancellation without either cannot be reconciled against a statement.
  previous_expiry timestamptz not null,
  cancelled_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on table public.subscription_cancellations is
  'Server-managed. One row per cancelled paid plan: the plan that was running, what was paid for it, the expiry that was ended and the instant it was cancelled. Written only by cancel_subscription(); the client may read its own rows.';

-- One account's ledger, newest first — the read the Subscription History list
-- makes.
create index if not exists subscription_cancellations_user_cancelled_at_idx
  on public.subscription_cancellations (user_id, cancelled_at desc);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Read your own rows, and nothing else.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.subscription_cancellations enable row level security;

-- RLS is a second fence, not the first: the table-level grants are narrowed to
-- the one verb a client needs, so even a mistake in a policy cannot let a
-- client write this ledger.
revoke all on table public.subscription_cancellations from public, anon, authenticated;
grant select on table public.subscription_cancellations to authenticated;
grant all on table public.subscription_cancellations to service_role;

drop policy if exists subscription_cancellations_select_own
  on public.subscription_cancellations;
create policy subscription_cancellations_select_own
  on public.subscription_cancellations
  for select
  using (user_id = auth.uid());

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. The one write path.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.cancel_subscription()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The account is the session's own, never a parameter: this ends the caller's
  -- plan or nothing.
  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
  v_plan_type text;
  v_amount integer;
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
  v_cancelled_at timestamptz;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_profile
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- A member's plan is the chamber's (§5.1), so their own row is not where their
  -- entitlement lives and ending it would change nothing while silently
  -- discarding paid time they keep for later. Refused instead. The owner is not
  -- a member: his own row *is* the chamber's plan, and the existing
  -- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` carries the new expiry to it.
  if v_profile.firm_id is not null
     and v_profile.role in ('associate', 'viewer') then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'firm_member');
  end if;

  -- Only a live paid period can be cancelled, and the test is the same derived
  -- rule every gate reads, so this cannot disagree with `is_premium()` about
  -- whether anything is running.
  if v_profile.subscription_expiry is null
     or v_profile.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' <= v_now then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'no_active_plan');
  end if;

  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;

  -- The plan that is running is the newest approved purchase — the same rule the
  -- app's Current Plan uses — and the amount recorded is what was actually paid
  -- for it rather than today's price list.
  select s.plan_type, s.amount
    into v_plan_type, v_amount
    from public.payment_submissions s
   where s.user_id = v_user_id
     and s.status = 'approved'
   order by coalesce(s.approved_at, s.submitted_at) desc
   limit 1;

  -- Backdated past the 48-hour grace, with an hour of cushion at the boundary,
  -- so the next entitlement check is false rather than true for two more days.
  -- The stored tier is deliberately untouched: it is the record of the last tier
  -- held, and it is what gives the account its lapse allowance (Starter 100,
  -- Pro 250, Firm 500, Firm Plus 1,000, Enterprise 2,000) instead of dropping it
  -- to Free.
  update public.profiles p
     set subscription_expiry = v_now - interval '49 hours',
         subscription_status = 'cancelled'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  insert into public.subscription_cancellations (
    user_id, plan_type, amount, previous_expiry, cancelled_at
  )
  values (v_user_id, v_plan_type, v_amount, v_previous_expiry, v_now)
  returning cancelled_at into v_cancelled_at;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'cancelled',
    'plan_type', v_plan_type,
    'amount', v_amount,
    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
    'cancelled_at', v_cancelled_at
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.cancel_subscription() is
  'Ends the caller''s own live paid plan: backdates subscription_expiry past the 48-hour grace so entitlement is false at once, records one subscription_cancellations row (plan, amount, the expiry ended, the instant) and leaves the stored tier alone so the account lands on its lapse allowance. Answers status firm_member for an associate or viewer (the chamber holds the plan), no_active_plan for a free or lapsed account, not_found without a profile row, and unauthenticated without a session.';

-- The RPC is for signed-in callers only. `create or replace` preserves an ACL,
-- but stating it here is what makes this file a complete record: a fresh project
-- gets the same answer as the live one.
revoke all on function public.cancel_subscription() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to service_role;
```

## App Version 0.0.546 — Task 22 — The Six-Tier Subscription Ladder

### 0.0.546 · `20261019100000_subscription_ladder_six_tiers.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-19.** Task 22 — The six-tier subscription ladder. The stored tier vocabulary gains starter and enterprise, and the old ladder's pro rung is renamed starter without moving any expiry. tier_rank, the case ceilings and the lapse allowances are restated for the six rungs; adding a case is checked against the diary's tier ceiling, not only the free wall; approve_payment accepts the seventeen sellable keys plus the four legacy ones at their own prices and durations, queues any different tier bought while a plan is running, renews a same-tier purchase and pushes a waiting change back by the term bought, and refuses a third plan behind a queued one; the seat caps become Firm 5, Firm Plus 12 and Enterprise unlimited, so chamber creation needs the Firm rung; and the generated plan names cover every key, old and new.

```sql
-- Task 22 — the six-tier subscription ladder (user ruling, 2026-10-19).
--
-- The paywall now sells a ladder of six tiers, and the server must agree with
-- the client on every fact it validates or enforces:
--
--   Free        50 cases, offline only                                    ৳0
--   Starter    500 cases, one device              1/3/6/12 months  ৳60/180/300/600
--   Pro      1,000 cases, two devices             1/3/6/12 months  ৳120/360/600/1,200
```
