```sql
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.session_id = v_session;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'unregistered',
      'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1)
    );
  end if;

  if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'revoked',
      'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1),
      'reason', v_row.revoked_reason,
      'revoked_at', v_row.revoked_at,
      'flushed', v_row.flushed_at is not null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label)
    );
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'active',
    'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1),
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.device_state() is
  'The launch check: active, revoked (with its reason) or unregistered, plus the cap and the device list.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 10. The lawyer frees a slot themselves.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.revoke_device(p_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.id = p_id
     and d.user_id = v_user
     for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_revoked');
  end if;

  if v_row.session_id = public.current_session_id() then
    -- A device removing itself is a sign-out, not a slot to free.
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'is_current');
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_reason = 'user'
   where d.id = v_row.id;

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_row.device_key;

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'revoked', 'id', v_row.id);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.revoke_device(uuid) is
  'Frees one of the caller''s own device slots. The revoked device flushes its unsent work and erases at its next contact; a device cannot revoke itself.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 11. The revoked device reports that it has handed over its work and erased.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.ack_device_wipe(p_device_key text default null)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_count integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set flushed_at = now()
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is not null
     and d.flushed_at is null
     and (
       (v_session is not null and d.session_id = v_session)
       or (p_device_key is not null and d.device_key = p_device_key)
     );

  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'ok', 'flushed', v_count);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.ack_device_wipe(text) is
  'Records that a revoked device has flushed its unsent work and erased itself, so the eviction is auditable rather than assumed.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Grants: the RPCs are the whole surface.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

revoke all on function public.register_device(text, text, text) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.revoke_device(uuid) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.device_state() from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.ack_device_wipe(text) from public, anon;

grant execute on function public.register_device(text, text, text) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.revoke_device(uuid) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.device_state() to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.ack_device_wipe(text) to authenticated;
```

### 0.0.565 · `20261022110000_device_limit_enforcement.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Task 22 — Enforcing the device limit. A limit a client can ignore by never registering is not a limit, so three gates: device_may_push admits an active device, a revoked device inside its 14-day flush window — the window is what lets unsent work reach the account before the device erases — and a caller carrying no session at all (psql, the service role); device_may_read admits only an active device, plus an unregistered session until the same roll-out end so an install that has not updated yet keeps working; and push_changes keeps its body — renamed push_changes_core with its grants, never re-typed — behind a wrapper that refuses a revoked session past its window with device_revoked. The eleven ledger tables and conflict_log gain device_may_read() in their SELECT policies, which is the same condition a Realtime subscription reads. profiles, the billing tables and the firm roster stay readable on purpose: a revoked device needs its own profile to explain itself, and it erases at its next contact anyway.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device limit (2/2) — enforcement: writes, reads, and the flush window.
--
-- **Why.** `20261022100000` gives the server the registry and the decision
-- table; this migration makes an unregistered or revoked session unable to
-- write or pull. A limit a client can ignore by not calling `register_device`
-- is not a limit.
--
-- **Three gates.**
--
--   1. **Writes** — `push_changes` gains a guard. The existing body is not
--      re-typed: it is renamed to `push_changes_core` (grants and all) and a
--      small wrapper checks the device before delegating. Re-typing a 400-line
--      function to add one `if` is how its rules silently change.
--   2. **Reads and pulls** — pulls are plain PostgREST selects, so this is an
--      RLS change: `device_may_read()` is ANDed into the read policy of the
--      eleven ledger tables and `conflict_log`. Realtime is governed by the
--      same policies, so a revoked device stops receiving frames on its next
--      subscription.
--   3. **The flush window** — a revoked device may still **write** for 14 days
--      so its unsent work reaches the account before it erases (the user's
--      rule: nothing is erased that could have been saved). It may not read.
--
-- **What is deliberately not gated here.** `profiles` and the billing tables
-- stay readable: a revoked device needs its own profile to show the refusal
-- screen, and billing history is the account's, not the chamber's. The roster
-- (`firms`, `firm_members`) is left readable for the same reason — the device
-- erases at its next contact anyway. Recorded rather than silently widened.
--
-- **Trusted paths.** A caller with no session claim (psql, the service role,
-- every SQL proof in `supabase/tests`) is allowed through every gate. A
-- PostgREST request always carries a session claim, so no client can reach that
-- branch by stripping one.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The two predicates.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Writes: an active device, or a revoked one inside its 14-day flush window.
create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active()
      or exists (
           select 1
             from public.user_devices d
            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
              and d.revoked_at is not null
              and d.revoked_at + interval '14 days' > p_at
         );
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device, a revoked device still inside its 14-day flush window, or a caller with no session claim.';

-- Reads: an active device. A revoked device reads nothing new. A session that
-- never registered is the roll-out case — an install that has not updated yet —
-- and is admitted only until the same date registrations stop being
-- grandfathered, so an old app keeps working through the update and no longer
-- after it.
create or replace function public.device_may_read(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active()
      or (
           p_at < public.device_rollout_end()
           and not exists (
             select 1
               from public.user_devices d
              where d.user_id = auth.uid()
                and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
           )
         );
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_read(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device, a caller with no session claim, or an unregistered session before the roll-out end (2026-11-21). A revoked session is always false.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Writes: one guard in front of the existing push_changes.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do $$
begin
  -- Idempotent: a second apply finds the core already in place.
  if to_regprocedure('public.push_changes_core(jsonb)') is null then
    alter function public.push_changes(jsonb) rename to push_changes_core;
  end if;
end;
$$;

revoke all on function public.push_changes_core(jsonb) from public, anon, authenticated;

create or replace function public.push_changes(rows jsonb)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  if not public.device_may_push() then
    -- The client maps this message to its "this device was signed out" state.
    raise exception 'device_revoked' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  return public.push_changes_core(rows);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.push_changes(jsonb) is
  'The device gate in front of push_changes_core: refuses a revoked session that is past its flush window. A caller carrying no session (service role, psql) passes.';

revoke all on function public.push_changes(jsonb) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.push_changes(jsonb) to authenticated, service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Reads: the ledger tables and the merge log.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The four case-data tables: one shape, one loop (copied from
-- `20261015100000` with `device_may_read()` added), so their spellings cannot
-- drift.
do $$
declare
  v_table text;
  v_tables text[] := array['cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references'];
begin
  foreach v_table in array v_tables loop
    execute format(
      'drop policy if exists %1$s_select_scoped on public.%1$I',
      v_table
    );
    execute format(
      'create policy %1$s_select_scoped on public.%1$I for select to '
      'authenticated using (public.device_may_read() and '
      '((user_id = auth.uid() and firm_id is null and '
      'scope_owner_id is null) or firm_id = public.current_firm_id() or '
      'scope_owner_id = auth.uid()))',
      v_table
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- The six reference tables keep the built-in baseline readable to every
-- registered install; only a *custom* row is scoped.
do $$
declare
  v_table text;
  v_tables text[] := array[
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  ];
begin
  foreach v_table in array v_tables loop
    execute format(
      'drop policy if exists %1$s_select_scoped on public.%1$I',
      v_table
    );
    execute format(
      'create policy %1$s_select_scoped on public.%1$I for select to '
      'authenticated using (public.device_may_read() and '
      '(is_custom = false or (user_id = auth.uid() and '
      'firm_id is null and scope_owner_id is null) or firm_id = '
      'public.current_firm_id() or scope_owner_id = auth.uid()))',
      v_table
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- delete_requests: the author column is `requested_by`.
drop policy if exists delete_requests_select_firm on public.delete_requests;
drop policy if exists delete_requests_select_scoped on public.delete_requests;
create policy delete_requests_select_scoped on public.delete_requests
  for select to authenticated
  using (
    public.device_may_read()
    and (
      (requested_by = auth.uid() and firm_id is null and scope_owner_id is null)
      or firm_id = public.current_firm_id()
      or scope_owner_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- conflict_log: membership condition only, no scope owner.
drop policy if exists conflict_log_select_own on public.conflict_log;
create policy conflict_log_select_own on public.conflict_log
  for select to authenticated
  using (
    public.device_may_read()
    and user_id = auth.uid()
    and (
      firm_id is null
      or firm_id is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
    )
  );

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Grants.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

revoke all on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.device_may_read(timestamptz) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) to authenticated, service_role;
grant execute on function public.device_may_read(timestamptz) to authenticated, service_role;
```

## App Version 0.0.566 — Task 22 — The Device Limit, Made Correct

### 0.0.566 · `20261022120000_device_trim_counts_the_caller.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Task 22 — Device trim counts the caller only when it holds a slot. The proof caught the first run of the limit admitting a third sign-in on a two-device plan and revoking one of the two devices already there as lapse: device_trim_surplus kept cap-minus-one devices other than the caller, which is right only while the caller already occupies a slot, and register_device trims before it knows. It now asks user_devices whether the caller holds an active row and subtracts one only then; a new device leaves the whole cap to the devices present, so a full plan answers device_limit_reached, and an account already above its cap is still trimmed back to it.

```sql
-- Device trim counts the caller only when it holds a slot.
--
-- The proof `supabase/tests/device_limit_test.sql` caught this on its first run:
-- a third sign-in on a two-device Pro account was **admitted**, and one of the
-- two devices already holding the slots was revoked as `lapse` — the plan-full
-- screen could never appear, and the lawyer's other phone was told the plan had
-- changed when nothing had.
--
-- The cause was here. `register_device` trims before it knows whether the caller
-- already has a row, and this function always kept `p_cap - 1` devices *other
-- than the caller* — arithmetic that is right only when the caller occupies one
-- of the slots. A brand-new device holds none, so the first trim of its
-- registration threw away a legitimate device and then found a free slot.
--
-- The fix is to ask the table instead of assuming: a caller with an active row
-- keeps the cap minus its own slot, and a caller with no row leaves the whole
-- cap to the devices that are actually there. Trimming above the cap still
-- happens for both — a fallen ceiling, or an account that is over it, is
-- trimmed to the cap and no further, so a new device still meets the plan-full
-- rules rather than a silent eviction.
--
-- Everything else is unchanged: the function returns without touching anything
-- while the account has no live plan, revokes the surplus as `lapse` (not
-- `cap`, so the owner is told the plan changed), clears the evicted devices'
-- push tokens in the same statement pair, and never revokes the caller.

create or replace function public.device_trim_surplus(
  p_user_id uuid,
  p_session_id uuid,
  p_cap integer
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_holds_slot boolean;
  v_ids uuid[];
  v_keys text[];
begin
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(p_user_id) then
    return;
  end if;

  -- Does the caller already hold one of the slots? A brand-new device does not,
  -- and must not be counted as if it did.
  v_holds_slot := exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.user_id = p_user_id
       and d.session_id = p_session_id
       and d.revoked_at is null
  );

  select array_agg(s.id), array_agg(s.device_key)
    into v_ids, v_keys
    from (
      select d.id, d.device_key
        from public.user_devices d
       where d.user_id = p_user_id
         and d.revoked_at is null
         and d.session_id is distinct from p_session_id
       order by d.last_seen_at desc
       offset greatest(p_cap - case when v_holds_slot then 1 else 0 end, 0)
    ) s;

  if v_ids is null then
    return;
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_reason = 'lapse'
   where d.id = any(v_ids);

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = p_user_id
     and t.device_key = any(v_keys);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.device_trim_surplus(uuid, uuid, integer) is
  'Revokes the devices above the cap after the ceiling falls (downgrade, lapse and renewal), least recently seen first and never the caller, and only while the account has a live plan. The caller counts against the cap only when it already holds an active row, so a device signing in for the first time does not evict a device that does.';
```

## App Version 0.0.567 — Task 22 — The Device Limit, Rolled Out On Both Sides

### 0.0.567 · `20261022130000_device_push_rollout_window.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Task 22 — Writes get the roll-out window reads already had. The enforcement migration admitted an unregistered session to READ until the 2026-11-21 roll-out end and gave it no such allowance to WRITE, so an install that had not updated could pull the diary down and could not hand one edit back up: its first push was refused as device_revoked, and because a refusal is not retryable the client blocked every queued change. device_may_push now admits a session with no user_devices row at all until the same date; a revoked device is unaffected because revocation stamps revoked_at on a row rather than deleting it, so the branch is reachable only by a session that never registered, and both gates close on one date.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device limit (3/3) — writes get the same roll-out window as reads.
--
-- **Why.** `20261022110000` gave an unregistered session ("an install that has
-- not updated yet") until `device_rollout_end()` to READ, so the update strands
-- nobody, but gave it no such allowance to WRITE. The result was the opposite
-- of the promise in the plan: an install that had not updated could pull the
-- account's diary down and could not hand a single edit back up. Its queued
-- mutations were refused as `device_revoked` on the first push, and because a
-- refusal is not retryable the client marked each one `blocked` — visible in
-- Sync Status as *the server refused this change*, but never sent again on its
-- own. A limit that turns a lawyer's backup off silently is worse than one that
-- arrives a month later.
--
-- **What changes.** One branch, the same shape and the same date as
-- `device_may_read`'s: a session with **no row in `user_devices` at all** is
-- admitted to push while `now() < device_rollout_end()`. A session that has a
-- row is not affected in the slightest — an active device is admitted as
-- before, and a revoked device keeps exactly its 14-day flush window.
--
-- **Why this cannot become a loophole.** Revocation in this registry is a
-- timestamp on a row, never a deletion: `revoke_device` and
-- `device_trim_surplus` both `update` `revoked_at`, so every session the server
-- has ever seen a registration for still has its row. The unregistered branch is
-- therefore reachable only by a session that has never called `register_device`
-- — the old install, and nobody else. A device the server revoked, by any
-- reason and at any time, stays refused, including during the window.
--
-- **After the window nothing changes for a revoked device**, and an old install
-- stops writing at the same instant it stops reading: one date closes both
-- gates, so the two halves cannot drift apart again.
-- ===========================================================================

create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active()
      -- The roll-out case, identical to device_may_read's: a session that never
      -- registered is an install that has not updated yet, admitted only until
      -- the same date registrations stop being grandfathered.
      or (
           p_at < public.device_rollout_end()
           and not exists (
             select 1
               from public.user_devices d
              where d.user_id = auth.uid()
                and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
           )
         )
      -- A revoked device may still hand its unsent work over before it erases.
      or exists (
           select 1
             from public.user_devices d
            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
              and d.revoked_at is not null
              and d.revoked_at + interval '14 days' > p_at
         );
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device, a revoked device still inside its 14-day flush window, an unregistered session before the roll-out end (2026-11-21), or a caller with no session claim. A revoked session is never admitted by the roll-out branch, because revocation stamps a row rather than deleting it.';
```

## App Version 0.0.590 — Payment Support — The Payer's Name And E-mail On Both Ledgers

### 0.0.590 · `20261022140000_payment_party_identity.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Payment support — both payment ledgers carry the payer. payment_submissions and payment_approval_events gain full_name and email snapshots, filled from profiles by a BEFORE INSERT trigger that overrides any client text; existing rows are backfilled from the profile they already point at, so troubleshooting no longer needs a join to identify who paid.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Payment identity snapshots
--
-- The payment tables are read by the payer and by admins for troubleshooting,
-- but a bare user_id forces a join to profiles/auth before anyone can tell who
-- paid. Both now carry the payer's display name and login e-mail as they stood
-- when the row was written.
--
-- A BEFORE INSERT trigger fills them from profiles and overwrites anything a
-- client sends, so the columns stay trustworthy even though `authenticated`
-- holds a table-wide INSERT grant on payment_submissions.
-- ===========================================================================

alter table public.payment_submissions
  add column if not exists full_name text not null default '',
  add column if not exists email text not null default '';

alter table public.payment_approval_events
  add column if not exists full_name text not null default '',
  add column if not exists email text not null default '';

comment on column public.payment_submissions.full_name is
  'Payer display name at submission time, copied from profiles by fill_payment_party_identity(); a snapshot for support, not a live join.';
comment on column public.payment_submissions.email is
  'Payer login e-mail at submission time, copied from profiles by fill_payment_party_identity(); a snapshot for support, not a live join.';
comment on column public.payment_approval_events.full_name is
  'Payer display name at approval time, copied from profiles by fill_payment_party_identity(); a snapshot for support, not a live join.';
comment on column public.payment_approval_events.email is
  'Payer login e-mail at approval time, copied from profiles by fill_payment_party_identity(); a snapshot for support, not a live join.';

-- Backfill existing rows from the profile they already point at. A row whose
-- profile has since been deleted keeps the blank default.
update public.payment_submissions s
   set full_name = p.full_name,
       email = p.email
  from public.profiles p
 where p.id = s.user_id
   and (s.full_name = '' or s.email = '');

-- The approval ledger refuses every UPDATE by its immutability trigger. This
-- one administrative backfill is the exception: the trigger is disabled and
-- re-enabled inside the same transaction, so a failure rolls the disable back
-- and the ledger is never left mutable.
alter table public.payment_approval_events
  disable trigger trg_payment_approval_events_immutable;

update public.payment_approval_events e
   set full_name = p.full_name,
       email = p.email
  from public.profiles p
 where p.id = e.user_id
   and (e.full_name = '' or e.email = '');

alter table public.payment_approval_events
  enable trigger trg_payment_approval_events_immutable;

-- The identity always comes from the row's user_id, never from client text.
-- SECURITY DEFINER so a PostgREST insert made by `authenticated` can read the
-- profile row it is copying.
create or replace function public.fill_payment_party_identity()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  select p.full_name, p.email
    into new.full_name, new.email
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = new.user_id;

  if not found then
    new.full_name := '';
    new.email := '';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.fill_payment_party_identity() is
  'Copies the payer profile''s full_name and email onto a new payment row; both payment tables keep the snapshot for support.';

drop trigger if exists trg_payment_submissions_party_identity
  on public.payment_submissions;
create trigger trg_payment_submissions_party_identity
  before insert on public.payment_submissions
  for each row
  execute function public.fill_payment_party_identity();

drop trigger if exists trg_payment_approval_events_party_identity
  on public.payment_approval_events;
create trigger trg_payment_approval_events_party_identity
  before insert on public.payment_approval_events
  for each row
  execute function public.fill_payment_party_identity();
```

## App Version 0.0.592 — Device Limit — The Grace Period Is Closed

### 0.0.592 · `20261022150000_device_no_grace.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Device limit — the grace period is closed. The roll-out row is removed: a third device at the cap is refused unless an idle spare may be evicted, an unregistered session reads and pushes nothing, and a revoked device loses the 14-day flush. register_device now returns the active-device list, and two RPCs are added: sign_out_device for the third-device window (reason signed_out) and touch_device for the real-use heartbeat. One-time cleanup revokes any row above its cap and clears the obsolete grandfathered flag.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device limit — the grace period is closed.
--
-- The roll-out exemption was written for a public update: it let a third
-- device register as `grandfathered`, and let a session that had never
-- registered read and push, until 2026-11-21. This app is in active
-- development, currently alpha, tested only by the owner and family, so the
-- exemption protects nobody and is removed here.
--
-- After this migration:
--   * the cap is hard — a third device at the cap is refused unless a device
--     idle for seven days may be evicted (that rule stays);
--   * an unregistered session reads and pushes nothing;
--   * a revoked device reads and pushes nothing — the 14-day flush window is
--     gone, because every removal now discards rather than saves;
--   * `signed_out` is a distinct revocation reason for the third-device window;
--   * `touch_device()` lets the app mark real use on resume/sync so the idle
--     rule does not mistake a running app for an unused one;
--   * every successful `register_device` returns the active-device list, which
--     fixes the empty Manage Account → Devices screen.
--
-- The `grandfathered` flag is kept as history but no longer set; active rows
-- are cleared and surplus rows are revoked in the one-time cleanup below.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Reads and writes: an active device only.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active();
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device or a caller with no session claim. A revoked device cannot push, even immediately after revocation; a device that never registered cannot push either.';

create or replace function public.device_may_read(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active();
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_read(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device or a caller with no session claim. A revoked or never-registered session reads nothing.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The new revocation reason.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.user_devices
  drop constraint if exists user_devices_reason_check;
alter table public.user_devices
  add constraint user_devices_reason_check
  check (
    revoked_reason is null
    or revoked_reason in ('replaced', 'user', 'cap', 'lapse', 'signed_out')
  );

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. register_device: no grandfather; every success carries the device list.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.register_device(
  p_device_key text,
  p_platform text default 'unknown',
  p_label text default ''
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The user's own ruling: only a spare this idle may be evicted automatically.
  c_evict_after constant interval := interval '7 days';

  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_cap integer;
  v_key text := pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_device_key, ''));
  v_platform text := case
                       when p_platform in ('android', 'ios', 'windows') then p_platform
                       else 'unknown'
                     end;
  v_label text := left(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_label, '')), 120);
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_evicted public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_active integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  -- A caller with no session (psql, service role) has nothing to register.
  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  if v_key = '' then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_device_key');
  end if;

  v_cap := coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1);

  -- Serialise two devices racing for the last slot: without it both could read
  -- "one free" and both insert.
  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('user_devices:' || v_user::text));

  -- The ceiling may have fallen since these rows were written. A revoked caller
  -- is skipped: it cannot take a slot, so trimming for it would be unfair.
  if not exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.session_id = v_session
       and d.revoked_at is not null
  ) then
    perform public.device_trim_surplus(v_user, v_session, v_cap);
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- This session is already known.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.session_id = v_session
     and d.user_id = v_user;

  if found then
    if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
      -- It has been revoked: the client must wipe and sign out, never revive.
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'revoked',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', v_row.revoked_reason
      );
    end if;

    update public.user_devices d
       set device_key = v_key,
           platform = v_platform,
           label = v_label
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The same phone, a different session: it replaces its own row.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.device_key = v_key
     and d.revoked_at is null
     for update;

  if found then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = v_now,
           revoked_reason = 'replaced',
           flushed_at = v_now
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    insert into public.user_devices (user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label)
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- A new device: a free slot, the idle-spare eviction, or a refusal.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select count(*) into v_active
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  if v_active < v_cap then
    insert into public.user_devices (user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label)
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- The least recently seen device, under a row lock so two registrations
  -- cannot evict the same one.
  select * into v_evicted
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null
   order by d.last_seen_at asc, d.created_at asc
   limit 1
   for update;

  -- Rule 2: with no live plan the evicted device has nowhere to hand its work,
  -- so nothing is evicted and the new device is refused instead.
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(v_user) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 3: only a device idle for a week may be evicted automatically.
  if v_evicted.id is null
     or v_evicted.last_seen_at > v_now - c_evict_after then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 1: the device is signed out now; it discards and wipes at its next
  -- contact. There is no save-then-erase flush after this migration.
  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = v_now,
         revoked_reason = 'cap'
   where d.id = v_evicted.id;

  -- Its push registration goes with it, in the same transaction.
  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_evicted.device_key;

  insert into public.user_devices (user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label)
  values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label)
  returning * into v_row;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'cap', v_cap,
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user),
    'evicted', jsonb_build_object(
      'id', v_evicted.id,
      'label', v_evicted.label,
      'platform', v_evicted.platform,
      'last_seen_at', v_evicted.last_seen_at
    )
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.register_device(text, text, text) is
  'Claims a device slot for the caller''s session: re-registering is idempotent, the same device key replaces its own row, a free slot is taken, and at the cap the least recently seen device is evicted only when it has been idle 7+ days and the account has a live plan; otherwise the call answers device_limit_reached with the list. Every success carries the active-device list.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Explicit sign-out from the third-device window.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.sign_out_device(p_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.id = p_id
     and d.user_id = v_user
     for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_revoked');
  end if;

  if v_row.session_id = v_session then
    -- A device removing itself is a sign-out, not a slot to free.
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'is_current');
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_reason = 'signed_out'
   where d.id = v_row.id;

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_row.device_key;

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'revoked', 'id', v_row.id, 'reason', 'signed_out');
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sign_out_device(uuid) is
  'Signs out one of the caller''s other devices with reason signed_out. The device discards its unsynced work and wipes at its next contact; a device cannot sign itself out this way.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. Real-use heartbeat.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.touch_device()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_count integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set last_seen_at = now()
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.session_id = v_session
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  if v_count = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_active');
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'ok');
end;
$$;

comment on function public.touch_device() is
  'Marks the caller''s active device as used, so the seven-day idle rule measures real contact rather than app launches. A revoked or unregistered session updates nothing.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. One-time cleanup: no one stays over the cap, and no stale flag remains.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do $$
declare
  r record;
begin
  for r in
    select ranked.id, ranked.user_id, ranked.device_key
      from (
        select d.id,
               d.user_id,
               d.device_key,
               row_number() over (
                 partition by d.user_id
                 order by d.last_seen_at desc, d.created_at desc
               ) as rn,
               coalesce(public.device_cap(d.user_id), 1) as cap
          from public.user_devices d
         where d.revoked_at is null
      ) ranked
     where ranked.rn > ranked.cap
       and public.has_sync_entitlement(ranked.user_id)
  loop
    update public.user_devices
       set revoked_at = now(),
           revoked_reason = 'cap'
     where id = r.id;

    delete from public.device_tokens
     where user_id = r.user_id
       and device_key = r.device_key;
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- The grace flag is no longer set anywhere; clear it from every row.
update public.user_devices
   set grandfathered = false
 where grandfathered;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 7. The roll-out seam is gone.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

drop function if exists public.device_rollout_end();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 8. Grants for the new RPCs.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

revoke all on function public.sign_out_device(uuid) from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.touch_device() from public, anon;

grant execute on function public.sign_out_device(uuid) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.touch_device() to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.595 — Device Limit — A Session Belongs To Its Install

### 0.0.595 · `20261022160000_device_install_secret.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-22.** Device limit — a session belongs to its install. Every install mints a 32-byte secret kept in this-device-only secure storage and sends it as x-install-secret (and p_install_secret); user_devices stores only its sha256. A known session presented with a different secret answers session_in_use, no secret at all answers invalid_install_secret, and replaced now needs the same device key and the same secret, so a restored backup is a new device. Push and heartbeat fail closed on a mismatch; reads keep a permissive fallback when no secret is present because Realtime does not reliably forward custom headers.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device limit — a session belongs to the install that created it.
--
-- The cap counts sessions, and until now a copied access token could be
-- replayed from a second phone: that phone presented a *known* session, was
-- re-registered as the same device, and the original row's `device_key` was
-- simply overwritten. One sign-in could therefore drive any number of installs.
--
-- **The binding.** Every install generates a 32-byte random secret once, keeps
-- it in this-device-only secure storage, and sends it as `x-install-secret` on
-- every Supabase request and as `p_install_secret` to `register_device`. The
-- server stores only `sha256(secret)`:
--
--   * a known session presented with a different secret answers
--     `session_in_use` — the app discards and wipes, it never revives;
--   * `replaced` (a re-login from the same phone) now needs the same
--     `device_key` **and** the same install secret, so a restored backup is a
--     new device, not the old one;
--   * `push_changes`, `touch_device` and `register_device` refuse a mismatched
--     install; reads decline only when a secret is present and wrong, because
--     Realtime does not reliably forward custom headers and must keep working.
--
-- **Known limits, accepted for an alpha tested by owner and family:**
--   * the *first* registration of a session binds the secret, so a clone that
--     connects before the real device after this migration wins that row;
--   * a full-device clone (token + secret) is indistinguishable from the
--     original. The connection does not bind to hardware.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The hash on the device row.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.user_devices
  add column if not exists install_secret_hash text;

comment on column public.user_devices.install_secret_hash is
  'sha256 of the install secret that claimed this session; a request presenting a different secret is a clone. Null on rows written before the binding existed, which bind on their next registration.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. What secret did this request carry?
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.current_install_secret()
returns text
language plpgsql
stable
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_headers text := current_setting('request.headers', true);
  v_value text;
begin
  if v_headers is null or v_headers = '' then
    return null;
  end if;

  -- PostgREST builds this GUC as JSON; anything unreadable is treated as absent.
  begin
    v_value := v_headers::jsonb ->> 'x-install-secret';
  exception when others then
    return null;
  end;

  return nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(v_value), '');
end;
$$;

comment on function public.current_install_secret() is
  'The x-install-secret request header, or null when the caller sent none (psql, service role, a client without the header, Realtime).';

create or replace function public.current_install_hash()
returns text
language sql
stable
set search_path = pg_catalog, public, extensions
as $$
  select case
           when s is null then null
           else public.sha256_hex(s)
         end
    from (select public.current_install_secret() as s) q;
$$;

comment on function public.current_install_hash() is
  'sha256 of the caller''s install secret, or null when none was sent.';

revoke all on function public.current_install_secret() from public, anon;
revoke all on function public.current_install_hash() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.current_install_secret() to authenticated, service_role;
grant execute on function public.current_install_hash() to authenticated, service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Writes and reads: an active device on the right install.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or exists (
           select 1
             from public.user_devices d
            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
              and d.revoked_at is null
              and (
                d.install_secret_hash is null
                or d.install_secret_hash = public.current_install_hash()
              )
         );
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device whose install secret matches the row, or a caller with no session claim. A revoke, an unregistered session and a cloned session all fail closed.';

-- Reads keep a permissive fallback when no secret is present: Realtime does not
-- reliably carry custom headers, and its rows must still arrive. A present but
-- wrong secret is refused.
create or replace function public.device_may_read(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or exists (
           select 1
             from public.user_devices d
            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
              and d.revoked_at is null
              and (
                public.current_install_hash() is null
                or d.install_secret_hash is null
                or d.install_secret_hash = public.current_install_hash()
              )
         );
$$;

comment on function public.device_may_read(timestamptz) is
  'True for an active device. A present secret must match the row; with no secret (Realtime, older clients) reads stay open so real-time delivery does not break. Revoked and unregistered sessions read nothing either way.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. register_device: binding the session to the install.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The old 3-argument form must go: leaving it would let a caller skip the
-- secret and keep the clone path open.
drop function if exists public.register_device(text, text, text);

create or replace function public.register_device(
  p_device_key text,
  p_platform text default 'unknown',
  p_label text default '',
  p_install_secret text default null
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The user's own ruling: only a spare this idle may be evicted automatically.
  c_evict_after constant interval := interval '7 days';

  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_cap integer;
  v_key text := pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_device_key, ''));
  v_platform text := case
                       when p_platform in ('android', 'ios', 'windows') then p_platform
                       else 'unknown'
                     end;
  v_label text := left(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_label, '')), 120);
  -- The body parameter is the documented channel; the header is the one every
  -- client sends, so either can bind. A caller with neither has no install to
  -- bind and is refused below.
  v_secret text := coalesce(
    nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_install_secret, '')), ''),
    public.current_install_secret()
  );
  v_hash text := case
                   when v_secret is null then null
                   else public.sha256_hex(v_secret)
                 end;
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_evicted public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_active integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  -- A caller with no session (psql, service role) has nothing to register.
  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  if v_key = '' then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_device_key');
  end if;

  if v_hash is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_install_secret');
  end if;

  v_cap := coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1);

  -- Serialise two devices racing for the last slot: without it both could read
  -- "one free" and both insert.
  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('user_devices:' || v_user::text));

  -- The ceiling may have fallen since these rows were written. A revoked caller
  -- is skipped: it cannot take a slot, so trimming for it would be unfair.
  if not exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.session_id = v_session
       and d.revoked_at is not null
  ) then
    perform public.device_trim_surplus(v_user, v_session, v_cap);
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- This session is already known.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.session_id = v_session
     and d.user_id = v_user;

  if found then
    if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
      -- It has been revoked: the client must wipe and sign out, never revive.
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'revoked',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', v_row.revoked_reason
      );
    end if;

    -- A different install presenting this session's token is a clone. The row
    -- is left untouched, so the real device keeps its slot.
    if v_row.install_secret_hash is not null
       and v_row.install_secret_hash is distinct from v_hash then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'session_in_use',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', 'session_in_use'
      );
    end if;

    update public.user_devices d
       set device_key = v_key,
           platform = v_platform,
           label = v_label,
           -- Rows written before the binding existed bind on first contact.
           install_secret_hash = coalesce(d.install_secret_hash, v_hash)
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The same phone, a different session: it replaces its own row.
  --
  -- "Same phone" now means the same device key *and* the same install secret:
  -- a restored backup carries the key but not the this-device-only secret, so
  -- it is treated as a new device rather than as the old one.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.device_key = v_key
     and d.revoked_at is null
     and (d.install_secret_hash is null or d.install_secret_hash = v_hash)
     for update;

  if found then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = v_now,
           revoked_reason = 'replaced',
           flushed_at = v_now
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- A new device: a free slot, the idle-spare eviction, or a refusal.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select count(*) into v_active
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  if v_active < v_cap then
    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- The least recently seen device, under a row lock so two registrations
  -- cannot evict the same one.
  select * into v_evicted
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null
   order by d.last_seen_at asc, d.created_at asc
   limit 1
   for update;

  -- Rule 2: with no live plan the evicted device has nowhere to hand its work,
  -- so nothing is evicted and the new device is refused instead.
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(v_user) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 3: only a device idle for a week may be evicted automatically.
  if v_evicted.id is null
     or v_evicted.last_seen_at > v_now - c_evict_after then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 1: the device is signed out now; it discards and wipes at its next
  -- contact. There is no save-then-erase flush.
  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = v_now,
         revoked_reason = 'cap'
   where d.id = v_evicted.id;

  -- Its push registration goes with it, in the same transaction.
  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_evicted.device_key;

  insert into public.user_devices (
    user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
  )
  values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
  returning * into v_row;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'cap', v_cap,
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user),
    'evicted', jsonb_build_object(
      'id', v_evicted.id,
      'label', v_evicted.label,
      'platform', v_evicted.platform,
      'last_seen_at', v_evicted.last_seen_at
    )
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text) is
  'Claims a device slot for the caller''s session and binds it to the install secret (parameter or x-install-secret header): re-registering is idempotent, a different secret answers session_in_use, no secret at all answers invalid_install_secret, the same device key and secret replace their own row, a free slot is taken, and at the cap the least recently seen device is evicted only when idle 7+ days on a live plan; otherwise device_limit_reached with the list.';

revoke all on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text)
  from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text)
  to authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The launch check reports the clone instead of "active".
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.device_state()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.session_id = v_session;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'unregistered',
      'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1)
    );
  end if;

  if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'revoked',
      'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1),
      'reason', v_row.revoked_reason,
      'revoked_at', v_row.revoked_at,
      'flushed', v_row.flushed_at is not null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label)
    );
  end if;

  if v_row.install_secret_hash is not null
     and v_row.install_secret_hash is distinct from public.current_install_hash() then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'session_in_use',
      'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1),
      'reason', 'session_in_use'
    );
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'active',
    'cap', coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1),
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.device_state() is
  'The launch check: active, revoked (with its reason), session_in_use for a cloned session, or unregistered, plus the cap and the device list.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. The heartbeat only counts contact from the bound install.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.touch_device()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_count integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set last_seen_at = now()
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.session_id = v_session
     and d.revoked_at is null
     and (
       d.install_secret_hash is null
       or d.install_secret_hash = public.current_install_hash()
     );

  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  if v_count = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_active');
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'ok');
end;
$$;

comment on function public.touch_device() is
  'Marks the caller''s active device as used when its install secret matches, so neither a revoked session nor a clone can keep a slot warm.';
```

## App Version 0.0.600 — Device Registry — Unique Install Keys And Support Identity

### 0.0.600 · `20261023100000_device_identity_and_collision_guard.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-23.** Device registry — unique install keys and support identity. user_devices gains full_name and email, filled from profiles by a BEFORE INSERT trigger and backfilled for existing rows. The client now keys Android installs by a persisted UUID because device_info_plus's Android id is the build ID, which two identical phones share; register_device answers a key already held by another active device with device_limit_reached instead of raising 23505 on user_devices_active_device_idx, and a known session never rewrites its device_key to a key another active row holds.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device registry — who the device belongs to, and a collision that failed hard.
--
-- **The defect.** `device_info_plus`'s Android `id` is the *build ID*, not the
-- SSAID, and two identical phones on the same firmware report the same value.
-- Two Redmi Note 10 Pro handsets therefore presented `SKQ1.210908.001`. The
-- second one could not insert its active row past
-- `user_devices_active_device_idx`, so `register_device` raised 23505 and the
-- client saw a failed check: no sync, sign-out appeared to fail, and the device
-- list stayed incomplete. The client now uses a persisted per-install UUID; this
-- migration makes the server safe for old keys too.
--
-- **What changes here.**
--   * `full_name` and `email` are copied onto every device row at registration,
--     so support can identify the person without joining `profiles`.
--   * a key that an **active** row already holds is answered with
--     `device_limit_reached` instead of a unique-violation error; the existing
--     device keeps working and the new sign-in can free that slot from the
--     window like any other full plan;
--   * re-registering a known session no longer rewrites `device_key` to a key
--     another active row holds — the row keeps its own key and still returns ok.
--
-- **Table class.** `user_devices` stays server-managed; the trigger and the
-- RPCs are the only writers.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Who the device belongs to.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.user_devices
  add column if not exists full_name text not null default '',
  add column if not exists email text not null default '';

comment on column public.user_devices.full_name is
  'The account holder''s display name when this device registered; copied from profiles for support.';
comment on column public.user_devices.email is
  'The account holder''s login e-mail when this device registered; copied from profiles for support.';

-- Existing rows, revoked ones included, get the identity they already point at.
update public.user_devices d
   set full_name = p.full_name,
       email = p.email
  from public.profiles p
 where p.id = d.user_id
   and (d.full_name = '' or d.email = '');

-- A snapshot at registration, not a live join: a later rename or e-mail change
-- does not rewrite history, and the hourly heartbeat never pays for a profile
-- lookup.
create or replace function public.fill_device_party_identity()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  select p.full_name, p.email
    into new.full_name, new.email
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = new.user_id;

  if not found then
    new.full_name := '';
    new.email := '';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.fill_device_party_identity() is
  'Copies the account holder''s profile name and e-mail onto a new user_devices row.';

drop trigger if exists trg_user_devices_party_identity on public.user_devices;
create trigger trg_user_devices_party_identity
  before insert on public.user_devices
  for each row
  execute function public.fill_device_party_identity();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. register_device: refuse a key collision instead of raising 23505.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.register_device(
  p_device_key text,
  p_platform text default 'unknown',
  p_label text default '',
  p_install_secret text default null
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The user's own ruling: only a spare this idle may be evicted automatically.
  c_evict_after constant interval := interval '7 days';

  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_cap integer;
  v_key text := pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_device_key, ''));
  v_platform text := case
                       when p_platform in ('android', 'ios', 'windows') then p_platform
                       else 'unknown'
                     end;
  v_label text := left(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_label, '')), 120);
  -- The body parameter is the documented channel; the header is the one every
  -- client sends, so either can bind. A caller with neither has no install to
  -- bind and is refused below.
  v_secret text := coalesce(
    nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_install_secret, '')), ''),
    public.current_install_secret()
  );
  v_hash text := case
                   when v_secret is null then null
                   else public.sha256_hex(v_secret)
                 end;
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_evicted public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_active integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  -- A caller with no session (psql, service role) has nothing to register.
  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  if v_key = '' then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_device_key');
  end if;

  if v_hash is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_install_secret');
  end if;

  v_cap := coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1);

  -- Serialise two devices racing for the last slot: without it both could read
  -- "one free" and both insert.
  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('user_devices:' || v_user::text));

  -- The ceiling may have fallen since these rows were written. A revoked caller
  -- is skipped: it cannot take a slot, so trimming for it would be unfair.
  if not exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.session_id = v_session
       and d.revoked_at is not null
  ) then
    perform public.device_trim_surplus(v_user, v_session, v_cap);
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- This session is already known.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.session_id = v_session
     and d.user_id = v_user;

  if found then
    if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
      -- It has been revoked: the client must wipe and sign out, never revive.
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'revoked',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', v_row.revoked_reason
      );
    end if;

    -- A different install presenting this session's token is a clone. The row
    -- is left untouched, so the real device keeps its slot.
    if v_row.install_secret_hash is not null
       and v_row.install_secret_hash is distinct from v_hash then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'session_in_use',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', 'session_in_use'
      );
    end if;

    update public.user_devices d
       set device_key = case
             -- Never steal a key from another active row: the unique index
             -- would fail the whole registration. The session is what counts;
             -- this row keeps its own key and stays active.
             when exists (
               select 1
                 from public.user_devices x
                where x.user_id = v_user
                  and x.device_key = v_key
                  and x.revoked_at is null
                  and x.id <> v_row.id
             ) then d.device_key
             else v_key
           end,
           platform = v_platform,
           label = v_label,
           -- Rows written before the binding existed bind on first contact.
           install_secret_hash = coalesce(d.install_secret_hash, v_hash)
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The same phone, a different session: it replaces its own row.
  --
  -- "Same phone" now means the same device key *and* the same install secret:
  -- a restored backup carries the key but not the this-device-only secret, so
  -- it is treated as a new device rather than as the old one.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.device_key = v_key
     and d.revoked_at is null
     and (d.install_secret_hash is null or d.install_secret_hash = v_hash)
     for update;

  if found then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = v_now,
           revoked_reason = 'replaced',
           flushed_at = v_now
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The key is held by another active device. That is two different installs
  -- presenting one key (an old build-ID client, or a clone), never the same
  -- phone: the same-phone branch above would have taken it. The unique index
  -- allows one active row per key, so the only safe answer is the plan-full one
  -- — the existing device keeps working and the new sign-in can free its slot
  -- from the window. Returning this instead of inserting is what stops the
  -- 23505 that broke sync and sign-out.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  if exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.user_id = v_user
       and d.device_key = v_key
       and d.revoked_at is null
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- A new device: a free slot, the idle-spare eviction, or a refusal.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select count(*) into v_active
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  if v_active < v_cap then
    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- The least recently seen device, under a row lock so two registrations
  -- cannot evict the same one.
  select * into v_evicted
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null
   order by d.last_seen_at asc, d.created_at asc
   limit 1
   for update;

  -- Rule 2: with no live plan the evicted device has nowhere to hand its work,
  -- so nothing is evicted and the new device is refused instead.
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(v_user) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 3: only a device idle for a week may be evicted automatically.
  if v_evicted.id is null
     or v_evicted.last_seen_at > v_now - c_evict_after then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 1: the device is signed out now; it discards and wipes at its next
  -- contact. There is no save-then-erase flush.
  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = v_now,
         revoked_reason = 'cap'
   where d.id = v_evicted.id;

  -- Its push registration goes with it, in the same transaction.
  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_evicted.device_key;

  insert into public.user_devices (
    user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
  )
  values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
  returning * into v_row;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'cap', v_cap,
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user),
    'evicted', jsonb_build_object(
      'id', v_evicted.id,
      'label', v_evicted.label,
      'platform', v_evicted.platform,
      'last_seen_at', v_evicted.last_seen_at
    )
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text) is
  'Claims a device slot for the caller''s session and binds it to the install secret: a different secret answers session_in_use, no secret answers invalid_install_secret, a key held by another active device answers device_limit_reached instead of failing the unique index, the same device key and secret replace their own row, and at the cap the least recently seen device is evicted only when idle 7+ days on a live plan. Every success carries the active-device list.';
```

## App Version 0.0.602 — Device Revocation — A Realtime Push Instead Of Polling

### 0.0.602 · `20261023110000_device_revocation_broadcast.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-23.** Device revocation — the server tells the device over the channel it already holds. A guarded AFTER UPDATE trigger on user_devices, only on the null-to-non-null revoked_at transition, sends the existing row_change {table,id} ping to firm:<firm_id> for a chamber member or user:<user_id> for an individual, so a signed-out phone discards immediately without polling; a Realtime failure is swallowed and the revocation still commits.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device revocation — tell the device itself, over the channel it already holds.
--
-- A device signed out from another phone used to learn about it on its next
-- launch, resume, refused push or Devices-screen read. The foreground heartbeat
-- added in 0.0.601 covered an idle open app by polling every 30 seconds, but
-- that is two requests a minute for a rare event.
--
-- This migration reuses the app's **one** private Realtime channel. When a
-- `user_devices` row turns revoked, the trigger sends the existing `row_change`
-- `{table,id}` ping on the topic the device actually joined:
--
--   * `firm:<firm_id>` when the owner's profile holds a firm (the app joins the
--     firm topic in firm mode);
--   * `user:<user_id>` for an individual.
--
-- The client routes a `user_devices` ping to a light `touch_device` check, not
-- to the sync pull. The send is deliberately guarded: Realtime is a
-- notification, never the source of truth, so a failed send must not roll back
-- the revocation. The device still discovers it on launch, resume, rejoin or a
-- refused push.
--
-- Only the null -> non-null transition broadcasts. The BEFORE trigger rewrites
-- `last_seen_at` on every update, and re-registration, wipe acknowledgements and
-- the identity backfill must stay silent.
-- ===========================================================================

create or replace function public.broadcast_device_revoked()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_topic text;
begin
  select p.firm_id
    into v_firm_id
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = new.user_id;

  if v_firm_id is not null then
    v_topic := 'firm:' || v_firm_id::text;
  else
```
