```sql
    v_topic := 'user:' || new.user_id::text;
  end if;

  begin
    perform realtime.send(
      jsonb_build_object('table', TG_TABLE_NAME, 'id', new.id::text),
      'row_change',
      v_topic,
      true
    );
  exception when others then
    -- A Realtime failure must never undo a revocation: the device still learns
    -- on resume, on its next join, or from a refused push.
    raise warning 'device revocation broadcast failed (device %, topic %): %',
      new.id, v_topic, sqlerrm;
  end;

  return null;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.broadcast_device_revoked() is
  'AFTER UPDATE on user_devices, only when revoked_at turns from null to non-null: sends the existing row_change {table,id} ping to the owner''s firm topic or user topic, and never fails the revocation.';

drop trigger if exists trg_user_devices_revoked on public.user_devices;
create trigger trg_user_devices_revoked
after update on public.user_devices
for each row
when (old.revoked_at is null and new.revoked_at is not null)
execute function public.broadcast_device_revoked();
```

## App Version 0.0.604 — Device Retention — Six Months Of Revoked Rows

### 0.0.604 · `20261023120000_user_devices_retention.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-23.** Device registry retention — six months of revoked rows, plus the newest revoked row per (user_id, device_key) forever. A partial (user_id, device_key, revoked_at desc) index supports the lookup; public.prune_user_devices(interval default 6 months) deletes only old rows with a strictly newer revoked row for the same key, never active rows, and is internal-only (revoked from public, anon, authenticated). A guarded pg_cron job, prune-user-devices, runs daily at 03:45 after purge-tombstones.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Device registry retention — six months of history, the newest revoked row.
--
-- Every sign-in creates one `user_devices` row; the revoked ones are history,
-- and without a policy they accumulate forever. The owner chose this rule:
--
--   * every row from the last six months is kept;
--   * an active row (`revoked_at is null`) is never deleted;
--   * for each `(user_id, device_key)` the newest revoked row is kept even
--     when it is older than six months, so a device that returns late still
--     sees the revocation and discards;
--   * only revoked rows older than six months that have a strictly newer
--     revoked row for the same account/device key are deleted.
--
-- **Age is `revoked_at`, never `last_seen_at`:** the BEFORE UPDATE trigger
-- `trg_user_devices_touch` rewrites `last_seen_at := now()` on every update,
-- including the revocation itself and a later wipe acknowledgement, so it
-- cannot measure how long a session has been revoked.
--
-- **A DELETE here is silent:** no table references `user_devices`, no DELETE
-- trigger exists, and `device_tokens.device_key` is plain text with no foreign
-- key. Nothing cascades and no Realtime frame is sent.
--
-- **This function is deliberately internal.** `purge_tombstones` has no revoke
-- and is therefore callable by client roles with a caller-chosen retention; a
-- retention job for the device registry must not repeat that. Only the owner
-- and the pg_cron job may execute this one.
--
-- There is no delete in this migration. The first scheduled run (or a
-- deliberate manual run) performs the first deletion.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The revoked-row lookup behind the "newest revoked per device" check.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create index if not exists user_devices_revoked_retention_idx
  on public.user_devices (user_id, device_key, revoked_at desc)
  where revoked_at is not null;

comment on index public.user_devices_revoked_retention_idx is
  'Retention lookup: the newest revoked row for one (user_id, device_key). Partial because active rows are never pruned.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The pruner.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.prune_user_devices(
  p_retention interval default interval '6 months'
)
returns bigint
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_cutoff timestamptz;
  v_deleted bigint;
begin
  if p_retention is null or p_retention <= interval '0' then
    raise exception
      'prune_user_devices: p_retention must be a positive interval, got %',
      p_retention;
  end if;

  v_cutoff := now() - p_retention;

  -- The correlated EXISTS is the rule itself: an old row survives only when no
  -- newer revoked row exists for the same account/device key. Rows tied at the
  -- newest instant are all kept; none is strictly older than another.
  delete from public.user_devices d
   where d.revoked_at is not null
     and d.revoked_at < v_cutoff
     and exists (
       select 1
         from public.user_devices newer
        where newer.user_id = d.user_id
          and newer.device_key = d.device_key
          and newer.revoked_at is not null
          and newer.revoked_at > d.revoked_at
     );

  get diagnostics v_deleted = row_count;

  raise notice
    'prune_user_devices: % row(s) deleted; revoked before %, newest revoked per (user_id, device_key) kept',
    v_deleted, v_cutoff;

  return v_deleted;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.prune_user_devices(interval) is
  'Deletes revoked user_devices rows older than p_retention (six months by default) except the newest revoked row(s) for each (user_id, device_key); active rows are never touched. Internal: no client role may execute.';

-- A new function in public reaches anon/authenticated through Supabase's default
-- privileges, so the revoke is explicit. The owner and the pg_cron job keep it.
revoke all on function public.prune_user_devices(interval) from public, anon, authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Schedule it daily, after the tombstone purge.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

do $$
begin
  begin
    create extension if not exists pg_cron;
  exception
    when others then
      raise notice
        'pg_cron could not be created (%); schedule public.prune_user_devices() '
        'from the dashboard.', sqlerrm;
  end;

  if exists (select 1 from pg_extension where extname = 'pg_cron') then
    -- Re-running replaces the job instead of stacking a second one. The
    -- tombstone job is a different name and is never touched here.
    perform cron.unschedule('prune-user-devices')
     where exists (select 1 from cron.job where jobname = 'prune-user-devices');

    perform cron.schedule(
      'prune-user-devices',
      '45 3 * * *',
      'select public.prune_user_devices()'
    );

    raise notice 'pg_cron: prune-user-devices scheduled daily at 03:45.';
  else
    raise notice
      'pg_cron is not installed; public.prune_user_devices() exists but is not '
      'scheduled yet.';
  end if;
end;
$$;
```

## App Version 0.0.629 — Firm Identity — The Chamber Logo And The Side Menu

### 0.0.629 · `20261025120000_firm_logo_storage.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-25.** Chamber logo storage — a private, 50 KB, JPEG-only `firm-avatars` bucket holding one flat `{firm_id}.jpg` per chamber. Any member of a chamber may read its logo; only its owner, and only while the chamber plan is live, may write it; the owner may always delete it. public.can_write_firm_logo() carries both halves of the write rule because has_sync_entitlement is revoked from clients. `firms` gains the server-managed logo_path and logo_version, and a trigger on storage.objects bumps them on every write or delete.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- 2026-10-25 — The chamber logo: one private bucket, one small JPEG per firm.
--
-- Why. The side menu said "Legal Case Diary of <member>" with the member's own
-- picture, which credits the chamber's diary to whoever is signed in. A chamber
-- now shows its own logo and name, with the signed-in member and their role
-- underneath. The member's personal picture remains the fallback when the
-- chamber has not set a logo.
--
-- What this file creates, in order:
--
--   1. the **firm-avatars** bucket: private, 50 KB, JPEG only. It is one flat
--      folder; each chamber has exactly one object, `{firm_id}.jpg`.
--   2. two **server-managed columns** on public.firms, `logo_path` and
--      `logo_version`. They are deliberately not in any client UPDATE grant.
--   3. a **trigger** on storage.objects keeping those columns in step, so the
--      client learns that a logo changed without polling the bucket.
--
-- **The policies are manual, and why.** `storage.objects` is owned by
-- `supabase_storage_admin`; the migration role (`postgres`) is neither its
-- owner nor a member of that role, so `create policy` would fail here. The four
-- policies (member read; owner insert/update while the plan is live; owner
-- delete) live in `supabase/manual/storage_policies.sql`, are included in
-- `supabase/AllSupabaseSql.md` as a labelled manual section, and are applied
-- once through Supabase's Storage policy editor. The bucket, the columns and
-- the trigger below need no such step: `postgres` can insert the bucket and
-- holds TRIGGER on storage.objects.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Who may write a logo.
--
-- `has_sync_entitlement` had its EXECUTE revoked from every client role (it is
-- a server-side gate, used inside definer functions), so a storage policy
-- cannot call it directly. This helper runs as its definer and carries both
-- halves of the rule: the caller owns the chamber and the chamber's plan is
-- live. `current_firm_id()` and `is_firm_owner()` already resolve for
-- `authenticated` in the existing RLS policies.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.can_write_firm_logo()
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.is_firm_owner(public.current_firm_id())
     and public.has_sync_entitlement(auth.uid());
$$;

comment on function public.can_write_firm_logo() is
  'True when the caller owns their chamber and the chamber''s plan is live: the firm-logo upload/update gate (used by the storage policies in supabase/manual/storage_policies.sql).';

revoke all on function public.can_write_firm_logo() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.can_write_firm_logo() to authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The bucket.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values (
  'firm-avatars',
  'firm-avatars',
  false,
  51200,
  array['image/jpeg']
)
on conflict (id) do update
  set public = excluded.public,
      file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit,
      allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. The server-managed cache fields.
--
-- `firms` is a pull-only cache and the client may UPDATE only its name, so
-- these two columns are unwritable from a device by construction. They are
-- what a member's next profile refresh reads to learn a logo exists and
-- changed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.firms
  add column if not exists logo_path text,
  add column if not exists logo_version integer not null default 0;

comment on column public.firms.logo_path is
  'Object name of the chamber logo in the firm-avatars bucket, or null. Written only by sync_firm_logo_state().';
comment on column public.firms.logo_version is
  'Bumped on every logo write/delete so a member device knows to download or clear the local copy. Written only by sync_firm_logo_state().';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. The trigger.
--
-- Two triggers rather than one with a coalesce in its WHEN: an INSERT has no
-- OLD row and a DELETE has no NEW row, and each operation's own condition is
-- the clearer statement of what it acts on. `postgres` holds TRIGGER on
-- storage.objects, so no ownership switch is needed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.sync_firm_logo_state()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  if tg_op = 'DELETE' then
    update public.firms
       set logo_path = null,
           logo_version = logo_version + 1
     where id::text = split_part(old.name, '.', 1);
    return old;
  end if;

  update public.firms
     set logo_path = new.name,
         logo_version = logo_version + 1
   where id::text = split_part(new.name, '.', 1);
  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sync_firm_logo_state() is
  'Keeps firms.logo_path/logo_version in step with the firm-avatars bucket.';

revoke all on function public.sync_firm_logo_state() from public, anon, authenticated;

drop trigger if exists trg_firm_logo_write on storage.objects;
create trigger trg_firm_logo_write
after insert or update on storage.objects
for each row
when (new.bucket_id = 'firm-avatars')
execute function public.sync_firm_logo_state();

drop trigger if exists trg_firm_logo_delete on storage.objects;
create trigger trg_firm_logo_delete
after delete on storage.objects
for each row
when (old.bucket_id = 'firm-avatars')
execute function public.sync_firm_logo_state();
```

## App Version 0.0.630 — Profile Pictures — A 50 KB Cap And A Premium Cloud Copy

### 0.0.630 · `20261025180000_profile_avatar_storage.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-25.** Profile-picture storage — a private, 50 KB, JPEG-only `individual-avatars` bucket holding one flat `{user_id}.jpg` per account. The holder reads and deletes their own file; only a premium individual or a premium chamber owner may insert or replace it, through public.can_write_profile_avatar() because has_sync_entitlement is revoked from clients. `profiles` gains the server-managed avatar_path and avatar_version, and a trigger on storage.objects keeps them in step. Account deletion removes the object through the delete-account Edge Function, because Storage deletes must use the Storage API.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- 2026-10-25 — The profile picture: one private bucket, one 50 KB JPEG each.
--
-- Why. The picture is saved on the phone today, uncapped and unsynced: a photo
-- from the camera can be several megabytes, and another device of the same
-- account never sees it. A private bucket with a hard size and type limit makes
-- it safe to sync, and the 50 KB pipeline on the phone (avatar_image_processor)
-- makes that limit easy to meet.
--
-- Who may upload: a **premium individual** or a **chamber owner**. A chamber
-- member is premium through the chamber but cannot buy for it, and the firm's
-- logo is the workspace identity; a member's own picture stays local-only.
-- Free accounts are local-only too. A lapsed account keeps its picture readable
-- and may delete it, but cannot upload a new one.
--
-- What this file creates, in order:
--
--   1. public.can_write_profile_avatar() — the owner/entitlement predicate,
--      because has_sync_entitlement is revoked from client roles;
--   2. the **individual-avatars** bucket: private, 50 KB, JPEG only, one flat
--      `{user_id}.jpg` per account;
--   3. two server-managed columns on public.profiles, `avatar_path` and
--      `avatar_version`, which no client UPDATE grant reaches;
--   4. a trigger on storage.objects keeping those columns in step.
--
-- **The policies are manual, and why.** `storage.objects` is owned by
-- `supabase_storage_admin`; the migration role (`postgres`) is neither its
-- owner nor a member of that role, so `create policy` would fail here. The four
-- policies (owner read/delete; premium individual or owner insert/update) live
-- in `supabase/manual/storage_policies.sql`, are included in
-- `supabase/AllSupabaseSql.md` as a labelled manual section, and are applied
-- once through Supabase's Storage policy editor. The bucket, the columns and
-- the trigger below need no such step: `postgres` can insert the bucket and
-- holds TRIGGER on storage.objects.
--
-- Account deletion removes the object through the `delete-account` Edge
-- Function, not SQL: Supabase requires the Storage API for a real delete.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Who may write a profile picture.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.can_write_profile_avatar()
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.has_sync_entitlement(auth.uid())
     and (
       public.current_firm_id() is null
       or public.is_firm_owner(public.current_firm_id())
     );
$$;

comment on function public.can_write_profile_avatar() is
  'True for a premium individual or a premium chamber owner: the profile-picture upload/update gate (used by the storage policies in supabase/manual/storage_policies.sql).';

revoke all on function public.can_write_profile_avatar() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.can_write_profile_avatar() to authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. The bucket.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values (
  'individual-avatars',
  'individual-avatars',
  false,
  51200,
  array['image/jpeg']
)
on conflict (id) do update
  set public = excluded.public,
      file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit,
      allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. The server-managed cache fields. `profiles` is pull-only and the client
--    may UPDATE only its display fields, so both columns are unwritable from a
--    device by construction.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists avatar_path text,
  add column if not exists avatar_version integer not null default 0;

comment on column public.profiles.avatar_path is
  'Object name of the profile picture in the individual-avatars bucket, or null. Written only by sync_profile_avatar_state().';
comment on column public.profiles.avatar_version is
  'Bumped on every picture write/delete so a device knows to download or clear its local copy. Written only by sync_profile_avatar_state().';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. The trigger. `postgres` holds TRIGGER on storage.objects, so no
--    ownership switch is needed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.sync_profile_avatar_state()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  if tg_op = 'DELETE' then
    update public.profiles
       set avatar_path = null,
           avatar_version = avatar_version + 1
     where id::text = split_part(old.name, '.', 1);
    return old;
  end if;

  update public.profiles
     set avatar_path = new.name,
         avatar_version = avatar_version + 1
   where id::text = split_part(new.name, '.', 1);
  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sync_profile_avatar_state() is
  'Keeps profiles.avatar_path/avatar_version in step with the individual-avatars bucket.';

revoke all on function public.sync_profile_avatar_state() from public, anon, authenticated;

drop trigger if exists trg_profile_avatar_write on storage.objects;
create trigger trg_profile_avatar_write
after insert or update on storage.objects
for each row
when (new.bucket_id = 'individual-avatars')
execute function public.sync_profile_avatar_state();

drop trigger if exists trg_profile_avatar_delete on storage.objects;
create trigger trg_profile_avatar_delete
after delete on storage.objects
for each row
when (old.bucket_id = 'individual-avatars')
execute function public.sync_profile_avatar_state();
```

## App Version 0.0.635 — Shared Chamber Capacity — Slots Cover Associates And The Owner's Devices, And A Shrink Waits For The Grace

### 0.0.635 · `20261026100000_payment_downgrade_after_grace.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-26.** A queued downgrade now starts 48 hours after the paid period it replaces ends, so the old plan's capacity covers the whole grace. approve_payment gains the grace-aware start, applies a lower tier bought inside the grace as a pending pair, applies a higher tier after a started pending immediately, and refuses Starter/Pro for a chamber owner (tier_seat_cap is defined here and reused by the capacity migration). Existing queued downgrades are backfilled by 48h through profiles only, because the mirror trigger copies the value to firms.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- 2026-10-26 — A downgrade's smaller capacity waits for the 48-hour grace.
--
-- **Why.** `approve_payment` starts a queued downgrade at the instant the paid
-- period ends, while sync entitlement keeps running for another 48 hours. A
-- chamber would therefore lose devices and associates *during* the grace. The
-- user's ruling: the old plan's capacity applies for the whole grace; the lower
-- tier starts when the grace ends, and only then may an over-capacity chamber be
-- trimmed (`20261026110000_firm_shared_capacity.sql`).
--
-- **What changes, and only this:**
--
--   1. `tier_seat_cap(text)` is defined here because the new guard below needs
--      the tier's slot count. It is the one mapping (free/starter/pro 0, Firm 5,
--      Firm Plus 10, Enterprise 20) and the capacity migration reuses it.
--   2. `approve_payment` computes `v_capacity_start = old expiry + 48h` (or now,
--      when that is already past) and uses it as the queued start. The expiry
--      still grows from the old period's end, so the grace never adds 48h of
--      free paid term.
--   3. A **lower-tier purchase made inside the grace** no longer applies at
--      once: it is written as the pending pair starting at the grace's end.
--   4. An **upgrade bought after a pending change has started** is applied
--      immediately and clears the pending pair. The shipped code took the queue
--      branch and reported a future `starts_at` while the tier was already in
--      effect.
--   5. A chamber owner may no longer buy Starter or Pro (0 seats). It would sign
--      out every associate or leave the owner with one reserved device while the
--      card promises two. They must dissolve the chamber first.
--
-- **Backfill.** Existing queued downgrades get the grace too. The live code
-- writes `tier_pending_from` as the **old expiry** (not `subscription_expiry`),
-- so the predicate is "a lower pending whose start is still inside the window"
-- (`pending_from + 48h > now()`), not the old equality. Only `profiles` is
-- updated: `trg_profiles_mirror_owner_subscription` copies the new value to the
-- owner's `firms` row, and updating both would add 48h twice.
--
-- No grant changes: `create or replace` preserves the ACLs
-- `20261019100000` left on `approve_payment`.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The tier's slot count, used by the no-zero-seat guard below.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.tier_seat_cap(p_tier text)
returns integer
language sql
immutable
as $$
  select case coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
    when 'firm' then 5
    when 'firm_plus' then 10
    when 'enterprise' then 20
    else 0
  end;
$$;

comment on function public.tier_seat_cap(text) is
  'Slots a tier sells in a chamber: firm 5, firm_plus 10, enterprise 20, everything else 0 (no join may be taken).';

revoke all on function public.tier_seat_cap(text) from public, anon, authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. `approve_payment`: the grace-aware start and the zero-seat guard.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.approve_payment(payment_submission_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- Configured plan prices, in BDT, one named constant per plan. A price change
  -- is then one migration, and the RPC validates the amount the server believes
  -- rather than the amount the client sent.
  c_starter_monthly_bdt constant integer := 80;
  c_starter_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 180;
  c_starter_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 300;
  c_starter_annual_bdt constant integer := 540;
  c_pro_monthly_bdt constant integer := 150;
  c_pro_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 360;
  c_pro_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 660;
  c_pro_annual_bdt constant integer := 1200;
  c_firm_monthly_bdt constant integer := 300;
  c_firm_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 750;
  c_firm_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 1350;
  c_firm_annual_bdt constant integer := 2500;
  c_firm_plus_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 1500;
  c_firm_plus_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 2700;
  c_firm_plus_annual_bdt constant integer := 5000;
  c_enterprise_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 4500;
  c_enterprise_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 8000;
  c_enterprise_annual_bdt constant integer := 15000;

  -- The four keys the old ten-plan ladder sold. They are never offered again,
  -- but a submission made before the revamp may still be waiting.
  c_legacy_monthly_bdt constant integer := 100;
  c_legacy_quarterly_bdt constant integer := 285;
  c_legacy_half_yearly_bdt constant integer := 540;
  c_legacy_annual_bdt constant integer := 1000;

  v_submission public.payment_submissions%rowtype;
  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
  v_event public.payment_approval_events%rowtype;
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
  v_new_expiry timestamptz;
  -- The instant the newly bought (lower) tier may start: the end of the period
  -- it replaces, plus the 48-hour grace. Never later than now.
  v_capacity_start timestamptz;
  v_plan_amount integer;
  v_plan_months integer;
  v_tier text;
  v_effective text;
  v_active boolean;
  v_pending_live boolean;
  v_queue_start timestamptz;
  v_queued boolean := false;
begin
  -- A GRANT to `authenticated` is not authorization: every caller shares that
  -- database role, so the registry itself decides.
  if not public.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'admin_required' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  select * into v_submission
    from public.payment_submissions s
   where s.id = payment_submission_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  select * into v_event
    from public.payment_approval_events e
   where e.payment_submission_id = approve_payment.payment_submission_id;

  -- Idempotent retries: a duplicate call can never extend expiry twice.
  if v_submission.status = 'approved' then
    if found then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'already_approved',
        'new_expiry', v_event.new_expiry
      );
    end if;
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_resolved');
  end if;

  if v_submission.status <> 'pending' then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_resolved');
  end if;

  -- The ladder's keys and nothing else: eighteen sellable keys plus the four
  -- legacy ones.
  if v_submission.plan_type not in (
    'starter_monthly', 'starter_quarterly', 'starter_half_yearly', 'starter_annual',
    'pro_monthly', 'pro_quarterly', 'pro_half_yearly', 'pro_annual',
    'firm_monthly', 'firm_quarterly', 'firm_half_yearly', 'firm_annual',
    'firm_plus_quarterly', 'firm_plus_half_yearly', 'firm_plus_annual',
    'enterprise_quarterly', 'enterprise_half_yearly', 'enterprise_annual',
    'monthly', 'quarterly', 'half_yearly', 'annual'
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_plan');
  end if;

  v_plan_amount := (case v_submission.plan_type
    when 'starter_monthly' then c_starter_monthly_bdt
    when 'starter_quarterly' then c_starter_quarterly_bdt
    when 'starter_half_yearly' then c_starter_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'starter_annual' then c_starter_annual_bdt
    when 'pro_monthly' then c_pro_monthly_bdt
    when 'pro_quarterly' then c_pro_quarterly_bdt
    when 'pro_half_yearly' then c_pro_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'pro_annual' then c_pro_annual_bdt
    when 'firm_monthly' then c_firm_monthly_bdt
    when 'firm_quarterly' then c_firm_quarterly_bdt
    when 'firm_half_yearly' then c_firm_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'firm_annual' then c_firm_annual_bdt
    when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then c_firm_plus_quarterly_bdt
    when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then c_firm_plus_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'firm_plus_annual' then c_firm_plus_annual_bdt
    when 'enterprise_quarterly' then c_enterprise_quarterly_bdt
    when 'enterprise_half_yearly' then c_enterprise_half_yearly_bdt
    when 'enterprise_annual' then c_enterprise_annual_bdt
    when 'monthly' then c_legacy_monthly_bdt
    when 'quarterly' then c_legacy_quarterly_bdt
    when 'half_yearly' then c_legacy_half_yearly_bdt
    else c_legacy_annual_bdt
  end);

  if v_submission.amount <> v_plan_amount then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_amount');
  end if;

  v_plan_months := (case v_submission.plan_type
    when 'starter_monthly' then 1
    when 'starter_quarterly' then 3
    when 'starter_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'starter_annual' then 12
    when 'pro_monthly' then 1
    when 'pro_quarterly' then 3
    when 'pro_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'pro_annual' then 12
    when 'firm_monthly' then 1
    when 'firm_quarterly' then 3
    when 'firm_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'firm_annual' then 12
    when 'firm_plus_quarterly' then 3
    when 'firm_plus_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'firm_plus_annual' then 12
    when 'enterprise_quarterly' then 3
    when 'enterprise_half_yearly' then 6
    when 'enterprise_annual' then 12
    when 'monthly' then 1
    when 'quarterly' then 3
    when 'half_yearly' then 6
    else 12
  end);

  -- Which tier the purchase bought, from the key alone. The four legacy keys are
  -- Starter now, matching the rename in `20261019100000`.
  v_tier := (case
    when v_submission.plan_type in (
      'starter_monthly', 'starter_quarterly', 'starter_half_yearly', 'starter_annual',
      'monthly', 'quarterly', 'half_yearly', 'annual'
    ) then 'starter'
    when v_submission.plan_type in (
      'pro_monthly', 'pro_quarterly', 'pro_half_yearly', 'pro_annual'
    ) then 'pro'
    when v_submission.plan_type in (
      'firm_monthly', 'firm_quarterly', 'firm_half_yearly', 'firm_annual'
    ) then 'firm'
    when v_submission.plan_type in (
      'firm_plus_quarterly', 'firm_plus_half_yearly', 'firm_plus_annual'
    ) then 'firm_plus'
    else 'enterprise'
  end);

  select * into v_profile
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_submission.user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- A chamber owner cannot buy a plan with no seats. It would either sign out
  -- every associate later or leave the owner with one reserved device while the
  -- card promises two, and the chamber would be permanently useless. Dissolve
  -- first, then buy an individual plan.
  if public.tier_seat_cap(v_tier) = 0
     and exists (
       select 1
         from public.firms f
        where f.owner_id = v_submission.user_id
     ) then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'chamber_requires_firm_plan');
  end if;

  -- Server time decides the base; a lapsed-but-not-expired window is not lost.
  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;
  v_new_expiry := greatest(coalesce(v_previous_expiry, v_now), v_now)
    + make_interval(months => v_plan_months);

  -- The instant the newly bought tier's capacity may start. A lower tier waits
  -- for the grace that guards the period it replaces; a purchase made after the
  -- grace, or after a lapsed period, starts at once.
  v_capacity_start := case
    when v_previous_expiry is null then v_now
    when v_previous_expiry + interval '48 hours' > v_now
      then v_previous_expiry + interval '48 hours'
    else v_now
  end;

  -- The tier in force, as it stands *before* this approval: a waiting change
  -- that has already started counts, so buying during it does not resurrect the
  -- older tier.
  v_effective := public.effective_tier(
    v_profile.tier, v_profile.tier_pending, v_profile.tier_pending_from
  );

  -- A plan is "running" while its paid period has not ended. At or after that
  -- instant the account is free or lapsed, and a purchase starts at once.
  v_active := v_previous_expiry is not null and v_previous_expiry > v_now;

  -- A queued change only counts while its start is still in the future.
  v_pending_live :=
    v_profile.tier_pending is not null
    and v_profile.tier_pending_from is not null
    and v_profile.tier_pending_from > v_now;

  if not v_active then
    -- Nothing is running. A lower tier bought **inside the grace** waits for the
    -- grace to end, so the expired plan keeps its capacity for the full 48h; a
    -- purchase after the grace replaces the tier at once.
    if public.tier_rank(v_tier) < public.tier_rank(v_effective)
       and v_capacity_start > v_now then
      update public.profiles p
         set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
             subscription_status = 'premium',
             tier_pending = v_tier,
             tier_pending_from = v_capacity_start
       where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
      v_queue_start := v_capacity_start;
      v_queued := true;
    else
      update public.profiles p
         set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
             subscription_status = 'premium',
             tier = v_tier,
             tier_pending = null,
             tier_pending_from = null
       where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
    end if;
  elsif v_tier = v_effective then
    -- A renewal of the plan in force. A waiting change is pushed back by the
    -- same term, because it starts when the *paid* period now ends.
    update public.profiles p
       set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
           subscription_status = 'premium',
           tier_pending_from = case
             when v_pending_live then p.tier_pending_from + make_interval(months => v_plan_months)
             else p.tier_pending_from
           end
     where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
  elsif v_pending_live and v_tier = v_profile.tier_pending then
    -- A renewal of the plan already waiting: its own start moves later by the
    -- term just bought, and the running plan's period grows with it.
    update public.profiles p
       set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
           subscription_status = 'premium',
           tier_pending_from = p.tier_pending_from + make_interval(months => v_plan_months)
     where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
  elsif v_pending_live then
    -- Only one change may wait. A third plan cannot be queued behind a second
    -- without deciding what the user actually wants; the server refuses.
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'change_pending',
      'pending_tier', v_profile.tier_pending,
      'pending_from', v_profile.tier_pending_from
    );
  else
    -- No unstarted change is waiting (a started one may still be in force). An
    -- upgrade now takes effect at once and clears the pending pair; a lower tier
    -- is queued to start when the paid period + grace ends.
    if public.tier_rank(v_tier) > public.tier_rank(v_effective) then
      update public.profiles p
         set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
             subscription_status = 'premium',
             tier = v_tier,
             tier_pending = null,
             tier_pending_from = null
       where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
    else
      v_queue_start := v_capacity_start;
      -- The paid term still starts at the old period's end; the grace delays
      -- only the tier's start, never the paid time.
      v_new_expiry := greatest(coalesce(v_previous_expiry, v_now), v_now)
        + make_interval(months => v_plan_months);
      update public.profiles p
         set subscription_expiry = v_new_expiry,
             subscription_status = 'premium',
             tier_pending = v_tier,
             tier_pending_from = v_queue_start
       where p.id = v_submission.user_id;
      v_queued := true;
    end if;
  end if;

  update public.payment_submissions s
     set status = 'approved',
         approved_at = now(),
         approved_by = auth.uid(),
         updated_at = (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint
   where s.id = payment_submission_id;

  -- Exactly one immutable event per submission (UNIQUE on the FK).
  insert into public.payment_approval_events (
    payment_submission_id, user_id, approved_by, plan_type, amount,
    previous_expiry, new_expiry
  )
  values (
    payment_submission_id, v_submission.user_id, auth.uid(),
    v_submission.plan_type, v_submission.amount,
    v_previous_expiry, v_new_expiry
  );

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'approved',
    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
    'new_expiry', v_new_expiry,
    'tier', v_tier,
    'queued', v_queued,
    'starts_at', case when v_queued then v_queue_start else null end
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.approve_payment(uuid) is
  'Approves one pending payment and grants the plan it names. A lower tier starts 48 hours after the paid period it replaces ends; an upgrade or same-tier renewal starts at once. Refuses a Starter/Pro purchase by a chamber owner. Idempotent; validates the key, amount and duration on the server ladder.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Existing queued downgrades get the same grace.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- `tier_pending_from` is the OLD expiry in the live code, so the predicate is
-- "the start is still inside the 48h window", not equality with the new expiry.
-- A start older than 48h is left alone (its grace has long passed); a recently
-- started one gets the remainder. Only `profiles` is written: the mirror trigger
-- copies the value to `firms`, and writing both would add 48h twice.
do $$
declare
  v_count integer;
begin
  update public.profiles p
     set tier_pending_from = p.tier_pending_from + interval '48 hours'
   where p.tier_pending is not null
     and p.tier_pending_from is not null
     and p.tier_pending_from + interval '48 hours' > now()
     and public.tier_rank(p.tier_pending) < public.tier_rank(p.tier);
  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  raise notice 'downgrade grace backfill: % profile(s) shifted by 48h (mirrored to firms)', v_count;
end;
$$;
```

### 0.0.635 · `20261026110000_firm_shared_capacity.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-26.** Chamber capacity is shared: associates plus the owner's own devices must fit the tier's slots (Firm 5, Firm Plus 10, Enterprise 20, owner included). Adds joined_at and capacity_signed_out_at to firm_members, closes its direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE bypass, adds the capacity helpers, makes device_cap dynamic for an owner and 0 for a signed-out associate, rebuilds join_firm/register_device/remove_firm_member under one firm lock order, adds owner sign-out/admit RPCs, and rebalances a chamber only after a started lower-tier shrink (owner devices first, then the newest associates), every 15 minutes by pg_cron.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- 2026-10-26 — Chamber capacity is shared between associates and the owner's
-- own devices.
--
-- **Why.** The tier's slots (Firm 5, Firm Plus 10, Enterprise 20, owner
-- included) only bound new joins, and every chamber account was held to one
-- device. An owner could therefore never use more than one device of the
-- capacity they paid for, and a downgrade never signed anybody out. The user's
-- ruling: a chamber has `S` slots; each associate uses one, and the owner's
-- active devices use the rest. `associates + owner devices <= S`, with the
-- owner's first device always reserved.
--
-- **The model, in one place:**
--
--   a = non-owner firm_members rows (seated and signed-out)
--   d = the owner's active user_devices
--   join:   a + max(d, 1) + 1 <= S
--   admit:  seated + max(d, 1) + 1 <= S
--   trim:   d -> max(1, S - a);  seated -> min(a, S - 1)
--   owner device cap = max(1, S - a)
--
-- Signed-out members keep their membership and their seats; only an owner
-- removal frees a slot. A member signed out for capacity can sign in again only
-- after being admitted by the owner.
--
-- **When capacity shrinks.** Only after a queued downgrade has started. The
-- payment migration (`20261026100000`) starts a lower tier 48h after the period
-- it replaces ends. `rebalance_firm_capacity` then trims the owner's extra
-- devices first (least recently seen) and the newest associates next. A legacy
-- over-roster chamber with no pending downgrade is never mass-signed-out; the
-- owner trims it from the roster card.
--
-- **Lock order (documented once):** `firm_capacity:<firm id>` first, then the
-- invite row / the per-user device lock / the membership row. `join_firm` reads
-- the invite once to learn the firm, takes the capacity lock, then re-reads the
-- invite `for update`; locking the invite first would deadlock against
-- `dissolve_firm`, which holds the capacity lock while it updates invites.
--
-- **Revocation reasons.** `capacity` (a signed-out associate or a trimmed owner
-- device) and `removed` (the owner removed the account). `lapse` is not reused:
-- its client copy is built around a device-cap number.
--
-- **No deploy-time sweep.** The cron only acts on firms whose lower-tier pending
-- change has started; a legacy over-roster is the owner's to trim. A device that
-- registers also rebalances lazily, so a shrink is enforced on first contact
-- even if the cron is late.
--
-- Requires `20261026100000_payment_downgrade_after_grace.sql` (it defines
-- `tier_seat_cap` and the grace-aware pending start).
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Schema: join order, the signed-out marker, and the orphan cleanup.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.firm_members
  add column if not exists joined_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  add column if not exists capacity_signed_out_at timestamptz;

comment on column public.firm_members.joined_at is
  'When this membership began, used to choose the newest associates when a shrink has to sign people out. Backfilled approximately from the permission stamps for rows that predate it.';
comment on column public.firm_members.capacity_signed_out_at is
  'Null while the associate is seated. Set when the owner or the capacity trim signs their devices out; the membership and its seat remain until the owner removes them.';

-- Existing rows: the oldest permission stamp is the best join time the cache
-- has. The order is approximate, and the trim breaks ties on id.
update public.firm_members m
   set joined_at = case
     when coalesce(m.synced_at, 0) > 0 and coalesce(m.permissions_synced_at, 0) > 0
       then to_timestamp(
         (least(m.synced_at, m.permissions_synced_at) / 1000.0)::double precision
       )
     when coalesce(m.synced_at, 0) > 0
       then to_timestamp((m.synced_at / 1000.0)::double precision)
     when coalesce(m.permissions_synced_at, 0) > 0
       then to_timestamp((m.permissions_synced_at / 1000.0)::double precision)
     else m.joined_at
   end;

-- The old join path did not check `profiles.firm_id`, so a member of one
-- chamber could redeem another chamber's code and leave a row behind in the
-- first. That row grants nothing (every read is scoped by the profile) but it
-- would hold a seat forever. Delete those rows; never the owner's own row.
do $$
declare
  v_count integer;
begin
  delete from public.firm_members m
   using public.firms f
   where f.id = m.firm_id
     and m.user_id <> f.owner_id
     and not exists (
       select 1
         from public.profiles p
        where p.id = m.user_id
          and p.firm_id = m.firm_id
     );
  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  raise notice 'orphaned firm_members rows removed: %', v_count;
end;
$$;

-- Two reasons the client words differently: a member signed out for capacity
-- stays in the firm, while a removed account is gone.
alter table public.user_devices
  drop constraint if exists user_devices_reason_check;
alter table public.user_devices
  add constraint user_devices_reason_check
  check (
    revoked_reason is null
    or revoked_reason in (
      'replaced', 'user', 'cap', 'lapse', 'signed_out', 'capacity', 'removed'
    )
  );

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Close the direct-write bypass on `firm_members`.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- Supabase's default privileges give `authenticated` table-level INSERT/UPDATE/
-- DELETE on every public table, and the owner policies then accept any row of
-- the caller's firm. That let an owner insert a seat without `join_firm`, delete
-- one without the RPC, and — after this migration — write the signed-out marker.
-- The app only ever updates the four permission columns, so the grant is
-- narrowed to exactly those and every write path is the RPC.
revoke insert, delete, update on public.firm_members from authenticated, anon;
grant update (role, can_add, can_edit, can_delete) on public.firm_members to authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Capacity helpers. All internal: no client role may execute them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select coalesce(
    (
      select public.tier_seat_cap(
        public.effective_tier(f.tier, f.tier_pending, f.tier_pending_from)
      )
        from public.firms f
       where f.id = p_firm_id
    ),
    0
  );
$$;

comment on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) is
  'Slots a chamber may hold, owner included: firm 5, firm_plus 10, enterprise 20, 0 for every other tier. Never null.';

create or replace function public.firm_associate_count(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select count(*)::integer
    from public.firm_members m
    join public.firms f
      on f.id = m.firm_id
    join public.profiles p
      on p.id = m.user_id
     and p.firm_id = m.firm_id
   where m.firm_id = p_firm_id
     and m.user_id <> f.owner_id;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_associate_count(uuid) is
  'Non-owner members of the chamber whose profile still points at it. An orphaned row (its profile moved to another chamber) never consumes a seat. Signed-out members count.';

create or replace function public.firm_seated_count(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select count(*)::integer
    from public.firm_members m
    join public.firms f
      on f.id = m.firm_id
    join public.profiles p
      on p.id = m.user_id
     and p.firm_id = m.firm_id
   where m.firm_id = p_firm_id
     and m.user_id <> f.owner_id
     and m.capacity_signed_out_at is null;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_seated_count(uuid) is
  'Associates of the chamber who are currently allowed a device (capacity_signed_out_at is null).';

create or replace function public.firm_owner_device_count(p_firm_id uuid)
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select count(*)::integer
    from public.user_devices d
    join public.firms f
      on f.id = p_firm_id
   where d.user_id = f.owner_id
     and d.revoked_at is null;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_owner_device_count(uuid) is
  'The owner''s active devices, which share the chamber''s slots with its associates.';

create or replace function public.firm_capacity_frozen(p_firm_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select coalesce(
    (
      select f.subscription_expiry is null
          or f.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' <= now()
        from public.firms f
       where f.id = p_firm_id
    ),
    true
  );
$$;

comment on function public.firm_capacity_frozen(uuid) is
  'True once the chamber''s 48h grace has ended (or it never had a plan): no new associate may join.';

create or replace function public.firm_capacity_usage(p_firm_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  with c as (
    select
      public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id) as slots,
      public.firm_associate_count(p_firm_id) as associates,
      public.firm_seated_count(p_firm_id) as seated,
      public.firm_owner_device_count(p_firm_id) as owner_devices
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'slots', c.slots,
    'associates', c.associates,
    'seated', c.seated,
    'signed_out', c.associates - c.seated,
    'owner_devices', c.owner_devices,
    'owner_device_cap', greatest(1, c.slots - c.associates),
    'used', c.associates + c.owner_devices,
    'active', c.seated + c.owner_devices,
    'over', c.associates > c.slots - 1
            or c.associates + c.owner_devices > c.slots,
    'frozen', public.firm_capacity_frozen(p_firm_id)
  )
  from c;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_capacity_usage(uuid) is
  'One chamber''s capacity picture: slots, associates, seated/signed-out counts, owner devices, the owner device cap, committed and active usage, and whether it is over or frozen.';

create or replace function public.firm_capacity_needs_trim(p_firm_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.firm_owner_device_count(p_firm_id)
           > greatest(
               1,
               public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id) - public.firm_associate_count(p_firm_id)
             )
      or public.firm_seated_count(p_firm_id)
           > least(
               public.firm_associate_count(p_firm_id),
               greatest(public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id) - 1, 0)
             );
$$;

comment on function public.firm_capacity_needs_trim(uuid) is
  'True when there are more active devices than the plan allows. Unlike "over", it becomes false once the trim has signed the excess out, even though signed-out members still hold seats.';

create or replace function public.firm_capacity_trim_due(p_firm_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select coalesce(
    (
      select f.tier_pending is not null
          and f.tier_pending_from is not null
          and f.tier_pending_from <= now()
          /* a legacy pending upgrade is not a shrink */
          and public.tier_seat_cap(f.tier_pending) < public.tier_seat_cap(f.tier)
          and public.firm_capacity_needs_trim(p_firm_id)
        from public.firms f
       where f.id = p_firm_id
    ),
    false
  );
$$;

comment on function public.firm_capacity_trim_due(uuid) is
  'The only automatic-trim gate: a lower-tier pending change has started and the active usage is above it. A legacy over-roster with no pending shrink never trims automatically.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. The caller's device cap: dynamic for the owner, zero for a signed-out
--    associate, one for a seated associate.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.device_cap(p_user_id uuid default auth.uid())
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select case
           -- A chamber owner's devices share the chamber's remaining slots.
           when p.firm_id is not null
                and exists (
                  select 1
                    from public.firms f
                   where f.id = p.firm_id
                     and f.owner_id = p.id
                )
             then greatest(
               1,
               public.firm_seat_cap(p.firm_id) - public.firm_associate_count(p.firm_id)
             )
           -- A member signed out for capacity has no device until admitted.
           when p.firm_id is not null
                and exists (
                  select 1
                    from public.firm_members m
                   where m.firm_id = p.firm_id
                     and m.user_id = p.id
                     and m.capacity_signed_out_at is not null
                )
             then 0
           -- Every other chamber account: one device.
           when p.firm_id is not null then 1
           -- An individual reads their own effective tier.
           else public.tier_device_cap(
             public.effective_tier(p.tier, p.tier_pending, p.tier_pending_from)
           )
         end
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = p_user_id;
$$;

comment on function public.device_cap(uuid) is
  'The caller''s concurrent-device allowance: a chamber owner gets the slots left after associates (at least 1), a seated associate 1, a capacity-signed-out associate 0, an individual their effective tier''s cap.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. Joining a chamber: shared slots, the freeze, and one chamber per account.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.join_firm(code text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  c_max_failures constant integer := 5;
  c_window constant interval := interval '15 minutes';
  c_retention constant interval := interval '1 day';
  c_role_associate constant text := 'associate';

  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_code_hash text;
  v_invite public.firm_invites%rowtype;
  v_failures integer;
  v_used_at bigint;
  v_diary_cases integer;
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_current_firm uuid;
  v_seat_cap integer;
  v_associates integer;
  v_owner_devices integer;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  delete from public.invite_attempts a
   where a.attempted_at < now() - c_retention;

  select pg_catalog.count(*) into v_failures
    from public.invite_attempts a
   where a.user_id = v_user_id
     and a.attempted_at > now() - c_window;

  if v_failures >= c_max_failures then
    raise exception 'Too many attempts — try again later'
      using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;

  v_code_hash := public.sha256_hex(upper(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(code, ''))));

  -- Learn the chamber without a row lock, take the capacity lock first, then
  -- re-read the invite. Locking the invite first would deadlock against
  -- dissolve_firm, which holds the capacity lock while it retires invites.
  select i.firm_id into v_firm_id
    from public.firm_invites i
   where i.code_hash = v_code_hash
     and i.used_by is null
     and i.revoked = false;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    insert into public.invite_attempts (user_id) values (v_user_id);
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_code');
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));

  select * into v_invite
    from public.firm_invites i
   where i.code_hash = v_code_hash
     and i.used_by is null
     and i.revoked = false
   for update;

  if not found then
    -- Another redemption won the race while this call waited for the lock.
    insert into public.invite_attempts (user_id) values (v_user_id);
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_code');
  end if;

  v_used_at := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;

  -- Retry by someone already in the firm. The code is retired as revoked.
  if exists (
    select 1
      from public.firm_members m
     where m.firm_id = v_invite.firm_id
       and m.user_id = v_user_id
  ) then
    update public.firm_invites i
       set revoked = true
     where i.id = v_invite.id;

    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'already_member',
      'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
    );
  end if;

  -- One chamber per account. The old path did not check this, so a member of
  -- chamber A could join B and leave an orphaned seat in A. The code is left
  -- unused for someone who can actually redeem it.
  select p.firm_id into v_current_firm
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  if v_current_firm is not null and v_current_firm is distinct from v_invite.firm_id then
    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'already_in_firm',
      'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
    );
  end if;

  -- A seat starts empty (§2.1).
  v_diary_cases := public.individual_diary_cases(v_user_id);

  if public.holds_own_diary(v_user_id) then
    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'has_own_diary',
      'cases', v_diary_cases
    );
  end if;

  -- A lapsed chamber is frozen: no new associate may join until the owner
  -- renews. Existing members keep working locally; nothing syncs.
  if public.firm_capacity_frozen(v_invite.firm_id) then
    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'firm_lapsed',
      'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
    );
  end if;

  -- The shared capacity: a new associate uses one slot, and the owner's first
  -- device is always reserved. Signed-out members still count, which is what
  -- forces an owner to remove them before inviting anyone else.
  v_seat_cap := public.firm_seat_cap(v_invite.firm_id);
  v_associates := public.firm_associate_count(v_invite.firm_id);
  v_owner_devices := public.firm_owner_device_count(v_invite.firm_id);

  if v_associates + greatest(v_owner_devices, 1) + 1 > v_seat_cap then
    delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'seats_full',
      'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id,
      'seats', v_seat_cap,
      'used', v_associates + v_owner_devices
    );
  end if;

  insert into public.firm_members (
    firm_id, user_id, role, can_add, can_edit, can_delete,
    synced_at, permissions_synced_at, joined_at
  )
  values (
    v_invite.firm_id, v_user_id, c_role_associate, true, true, false,
    v_used_at, v_used_at, now()
  )
  on conflict (firm_id, user_id) do update
    set role = 'associate',
        can_add = true,
        can_edit = true,
        can_delete = false,
        synced_at = excluded.synced_at,
        permissions_synced_at = excluded.permissions_synced_at;

  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = v_invite.firm_id,
         role = 'associate'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  update public.firm_invites i
     set used_by = v_user_id, used_at = v_used_at
   where i.id = v_invite.id;

  delete from public.invite_attempts a where a.user_id = v_user_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'joined',
    'firm_id', v_invite.firm_id
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.join_firm(text) is
  'Single-use invite redemption: rate limit, hash, chamber freeze, own-diary and shared-capacity gates (associates + owner devices), one-chamber-per-account, membership, profile relink, invite consumed — one transaction.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. Registering a device: the firm lock first, then the user lock.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.register_device(
  p_device_key text,
  p_platform text default 'unknown',
  p_label text default '',
  p_install_secret text default null
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  c_evict_after constant interval := interval '7 days';

  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_session uuid := public.current_session_id();
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_cap integer;
  v_key text := pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_device_key, ''));
  v_platform text := case
                       when p_platform in ('android', 'ios', 'windows') then p_platform
                       else 'unknown'
                     end;
  v_label text := left(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_label, '')), 120);
  v_secret text := coalesce(
    nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(coalesce(p_install_secret, '')), ''),
    public.current_install_secret()
  );
  v_hash text := case
                   when v_secret is null then null
                   else public.sha256_hex(v_secret)
                 end;
  v_row public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_evicted public.user_devices%rowtype;
  v_active integer;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  if v_session is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unmanaged');
  end if;

  if v_key = '' then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_device_key');
  end if;

  if v_hash is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_install_secret');
  end if;

  -- Lock order: the capacity lock first, then the per-user device lock. A
  -- chamber whose lower tier has started is rebalanced before this device is
  -- allowed to claim a slot.
  select p.firm_id into v_firm_id
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_user;

  if v_firm_id is not null then
    perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));
    if public.firm_capacity_trim_due(v_firm_id) then
      perform public.rebalance_firm_capacity(v_firm_id, v_session);
    end if;
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('user_devices:' || v_user::text));

  -- A member signed out for capacity cannot claim a slot until the owner
  -- admits them again.
  if v_firm_id is not null and exists (
    select 1
      from public.firm_members m
     where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
       and m.user_id = v_user
       and m.capacity_signed_out_at is not null
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'revoked',
      'cap', 0,
      'reason', 'capacity'
    );
  end if;

  v_cap := coalesce(public.device_cap(v_user), 1);

  -- The ceiling may have fallen since these rows were written. A revoked caller
  -- is skipped: it cannot take a slot, so trimming for it would be unfair.
  if not exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.session_id = v_session
       and d.revoked_at is not null
  ) then
    perform public.device_trim_surplus(v_user, v_session, v_cap);
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- This session is already known.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.session_id = v_session
     and d.user_id = v_user;

  if found then
    if v_row.revoked_at is not null then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'revoked',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', v_row.revoked_reason
      );
    end if;

    if v_row.install_secret_hash is not null
       and v_row.install_secret_hash is distinct from v_hash then
      return jsonb_build_object(
        'status', 'session_in_use',
        'cap', v_cap,
        'reason', 'session_in_use'
      );
    end if;

    update public.user_devices d
       set device_key = case
             when exists (
               select 1
                 from public.user_devices x
                where x.user_id = v_user
                  and x.device_key = v_key
                  and x.revoked_at is null
                  and x.id <> v_row.id
             ) then d.device_key
             else v_key
           end,
           platform = v_platform,
           label = v_label,
           install_secret_hash = coalesce(d.install_secret_hash, v_hash)
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The same phone, a different session: it replaces its own row.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select * into v_row
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.device_key = v_key
     and d.revoked_at is null
     and (d.install_secret_hash is null or d.install_secret_hash = v_hash)
     for update;

  if found then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = v_now,
           revoked_reason = 'replaced',
           flushed_at = v_now
     where d.id = v_row.id;

    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- The key is held by another active device.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  if exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.user_id = v_user
       and d.device_key = v_key
       and d.revoked_at is null
  ) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- A new device: a free slot, the idle-spare eviction, or a refusal.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  select count(*) into v_active
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  if v_active < v_cap then
    insert into public.user_devices (
      user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
    )
    values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
    returning * into v_row;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'ok',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'evicted', null,
      'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_label),
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  select * into v_evicted
    from public.user_devices d
   where d.user_id = v_user
     and d.revoked_at is null
   order by d.last_seen_at asc, d.created_at asc
   limit 1
   for update;

  -- Rule 2: with no live plan the evicted device has nowhere to hand its work,
  -- so nothing is evicted and the new device is refused instead.
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(v_user) then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  -- Rule 3: only a device idle for a week may be evicted automatically.
  if v_evicted.id is null
     or v_evicted.last_seen_at > v_now - c_evict_after then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'device_limit_reached',
      'cap', v_cap,
      'devices', public.device_list(v_user)
    );
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = v_now,
         revoked_reason = 'cap'
   where d.id = v_evicted.id;

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = v_user
     and t.device_key = v_evicted.device_key;

  insert into public.user_devices (
    user_id, session_id, device_key, platform, label, install_secret_hash
  )
  values (v_user, v_session, v_key, v_platform, v_label, v_hash)
  returning * into v_row;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'cap', v_cap,
    'device', jsonb_build_object('id', v_row.id, 'label', v_row.label),
    'devices', public.device_list(v_user),
    'evicted', jsonb_build_object(
      'id', v_evicted.id,
      'label', v_evicted.label,
      'platform', v_evicted.platform,
      'last_seen_at', v_evicted.last_seen_at
    )
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text) is
  'Claims a device slot for the caller''s session under the firm capacity lock and the per-user lock. A capacity-signed-out associate is refused; a chamber owner''s cap is the slots left after associates; every other device rule (install secret, same-phone replacement, key collision, 7-day eviction) is unchanged.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 7. Removing an associate: only their own chamber's access, never another's.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.remove_firm_member(p_user_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path to 'pg_catalog', 'public'
as $function$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_target_firm uuid;
  v_locked boolean;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_request');
  end if;

  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  if p_user_id = v_actor then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'cannot_remove_self');
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));

  select true into v_locked
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- An orphaned row (the person now belongs to another chamber) is only a
  -- stale seat. Do not relink their profile or revoke their devices: both
  -- belong to the other chamber.
  select p.firm_id into v_target_firm
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = p_user_id;

  if v_target_firm = v_firm_id then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = now(),
           revoked_reason = 'removed'
     where d.user_id = p_user_id
       and d.revoked_at is null;

    delete from public.device_tokens t
     where t.user_id = p_user_id;
  end if;

  delete from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id;

  if v_target_firm = v_firm_id then
    update public.profiles p
       set firm_id = null,
           role = 'individual'
     where p.id = p_user_id;
  end if;

  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'user:' || p_user_id::text,
    true
  );
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'firm:' || v_firm_id::text,
    true
  );

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'removed',
    'user_id', p_user_id,
    'firm_id', v_firm_id
  );
end;
$function$;

comment on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) is
  'Owner-only removal: locks the membership, revokes the member''s devices as removed (only when their profile still points at this chamber), clears push registrations, deletes the membership, relinks the profile to individual, and announces on both topics. An orphaned row is deleted without touching the other chamber. Authored rows stay with the chamber.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 8. Owner actions: sign a member out for capacity, or admit them again.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.sign_out_firm_member(p_user_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_target_firm uuid;
  v_signed_out_at timestamptz;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_request');
  end if;

  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  if p_user_id = v_actor then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'cannot_sign_out_self');
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));

  select m.capacity_signed_out_at into v_signed_out_at
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  if v_signed_out_at is not null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_signed_out');
  end if;

  select p.firm_id into v_target_firm
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = p_user_id;

  if v_target_firm is distinct from v_firm_id then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  update public.firm_members m
     set capacity_signed_out_at = now()
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_reason = 'capacity'
   where d.user_id = p_user_id
     and d.revoked_at is null;

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = p_user_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'signed_out',
    'user_id', p_user_id,
    'firm_id', v_firm_id
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sign_out_firm_member(uuid) is
  'Owner-only: keeps the membership but marks it capacity-signed-out, revokes all its devices as capacity and clears their push registrations. Used to choose who loses access before or after a shrink.';

create or replace function public.admit_firm_member(p_user_id uuid)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_target_firm uuid;
  v_signed_out_at timestamptz;
  v_seated integer;
  v_owner_devices integer;
  v_seat_cap integer;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_request');
  end if;

  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  if p_user_id = v_actor then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'cannot_admit_self');
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));

  select m.capacity_signed_out_at into v_signed_out_at
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  if v_signed_out_at is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_signed_out');
  end if;

  select p.firm_id into v_target_firm
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = p_user_id;

  if v_target_firm is distinct from v_firm_id then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  v_seat_cap := public.firm_seat_cap(v_firm_id);
  v_seated := public.firm_seated_count(v_firm_id);
  v_owner_devices := public.firm_owner_device_count(v_firm_id);

  if v_seated + greatest(v_owner_devices, 1) + 1 > v_seat_cap then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'seats_full',
      'firm_id', v_firm_id,
      'seats', v_seat_cap
    );
  end if;

  update public.firm_members m
     set capacity_signed_out_at = null
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'admitted',
    'user_id', p_user_id,
    'firm_id', v_firm_id
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.admit_firm_member(uuid) is
  'Owner-only: clears a capacity-signed-out marker when the chamber has room for the member''s device and the owner''s reserved one. The member signs in again normally.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 9. Dissolving a chamber takes the capacity lock too.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.dissolve_firm()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_members integer;
  v_table text;
  c_ledger constant text[] := array[
    'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references', 'delete_requests',
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  ];
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- Resolve without a lock, take the capacity lock (same key and order as a
  -- join), then lock the row. A join cannot add a member between the roster
  -- count and the delete.
  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor
   order by f.created_at
   limit 1;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || v_firm_id::text));

  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.id = v_firm_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  select count(*) into v_members
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id <> v_actor;

  if v_members > 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'status', 'members_remaining',
      'members', v_members
    );
  end if;

  update public.firm_invites i
     set revoked = true
   where i.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and i.revoked = false;

  foreach v_table in array c_ledger loop
    execute format(
```
