```sql
      'update public.%1$I set firm_id = null, scope_owner_id = $1 where firm_id = $2',
      v_table
    ) using v_actor, v_firm_id;
  end loop;

  update public.conflict_log c
     set firm_id = null
   where c.firm_id = v_firm_id;

  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = null,
         role = 'individual'
   where p.id = v_actor;

  delete from public.firms f where f.id = v_firm_id;

  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', v_actor),
    'row_change',
    'user:' || v_actor::text,
    true
  );

  return jsonb_build_object('status', 'dissolved', 'firm_id', v_firm_id);
end;
$$;

comment on function public.dissolve_firm() is
  'Owner-only: dissolves the caller''s chamber once its roster holds nobody else, under the same capacity lock a join takes. Every ledger row loses firm_id and gains the owner as scope_owner_id, open invites are retired, the firms row is removed and the account returns to individual.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 10. The trim: owner's extra devices first, then the newest associates.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.rebalance_firm_capacity(
  p_firm_id uuid,
  p_keep_session uuid default null
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_owner uuid;
  v_slots integer;
  v_associates integer;
  v_seated integer;
  v_devices integer;
  v_owner_cap integer;
  v_seat_target integer;
  v_keep_id uuid;
  v_ids uuid[];
  v_keys text[];
  v_flag uuid[];
  v_trimmed_owner integer := 0;
  v_flagged integer := 0;
begin
  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('firm_capacity:' || p_firm_id::text));

  select f.owner_id into v_owner
    from public.firms f
   where f.id = p_firm_id;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  v_slots := public.firm_seat_cap(p_firm_id);
  v_associates := public.firm_associate_count(p_firm_id);
  v_seated := public.firm_seated_count(p_firm_id);
  v_devices := public.firm_owner_device_count(p_firm_id);
  v_owner_cap := greatest(1, v_slots - v_associates);
  v_seat_target := least(v_associates, greatest(v_slots - 1, 0));

  -- Never revoke the device that is making this call.
  if p_keep_session is not null then
    select d.id into v_keep_id
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.user_id = v_owner
       and d.session_id = p_keep_session
       and d.revoked_at is null;
  end if;

  select array_agg(s.id), array_agg(s.device_key)
    into v_ids, v_keys
    from (
      select d.id, d.device_key
        from public.user_devices d
       where d.user_id = v_owner
         and d.revoked_at is null
         and (v_keep_id is null or d.id <> v_keep_id)
       order by d.last_seen_at asc, d.created_at asc
       limit greatest(v_devices - v_owner_cap, 0)
    ) s;

  if v_ids is not null then
    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = now(),
           revoked_reason = 'capacity'
     where d.id = any(v_ids);

    delete from public.device_tokens t
     where t.user_id = v_owner
       and t.device_key = any(v_keys);

    v_trimmed_owner := cardinality(v_ids);
  end if;

  select array_agg(s.user_id)
    into v_flag
    from (
      select m.user_id
        from public.firm_members m
        join public.profiles p
          on p.id = m.user_id
         and p.firm_id = m.firm_id
       where m.firm_id = p_firm_id
         and m.user_id <> v_owner
         and m.capacity_signed_out_at is null
       order by m.joined_at desc, m.id desc
       limit greatest(v_seated - v_seat_target, 0)
    ) s;

  if v_flag is not null then
    update public.firm_members m
       set capacity_signed_out_at = now()
     where m.firm_id = p_firm_id
       and m.user_id = any(v_flag);

    update public.user_devices d
       set revoked_at = now(),
           revoked_reason = 'capacity'
     where d.user_id = any(v_flag)
       and d.revoked_at is null;

    delete from public.device_tokens t
     where t.user_id = any(v_flag);

    v_flagged := cardinality(v_flag);
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'slots', v_slots,
    'associates', v_associates,
    'seated', v_seated,
    'owner_devices', v_devices,
    'owner_devices_trimmed', v_trimmed_owner,
    'associates_signed_out', v_flagged
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.rebalance_firm_capacity(uuid, uuid) is
  'Enforces a chamber''s shared slots: revokes the owner''s devices beyond max(1, slots - associates), least recently seen first (never p_keep_session), then signs out the newest seated associates beyond min(associates, slots - 1), revoking their devices. Never clears a marker.';

create or replace function public.rebalance_all_firm_capacities()
returns integer
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_firm record;
  v_count integer := 0;
begin
  for v_firm in
    select f.id
      from public.firms f
     where public.firm_capacity_trim_due(f.id)
  loop
    perform public.rebalance_firm_capacity(v_firm.id);
    v_count := v_count + 1;
  end loop;

  return v_count;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.rebalance_all_firm_capacities() is
  'The cron target: rebalances only chambers whose lower-tier pending change has started and whose active usage is over. Returns how many chambers were processed.';

-- Schedule every 15 minutes so a shrink is enforced shortly after its deadline.
-- The same guarded pattern as the other pg_cron jobs; if the extension is not
-- available, the lazy rebalance in register_device still enforces it on contact.
do $$
begin
  begin
    create extension if not exists pg_cron;
  exception
    when others then
      raise notice
        'pg_cron could not be created (%); schedule public.rebalance_all_firm_capacities() '
        'from the dashboard.', sqlerrm;
  end;

  if exists (select 1 from pg_extension where extname = 'pg_cron') then
    perform cron.unschedule('rebalance-firm-capacity')
     where exists (select 1 from cron.job where jobname = 'rebalance-firm-capacity');

    perform cron.schedule(
      'rebalance-firm-capacity',
      '*/15 * * * *',
      'select public.rebalance_all_firm_capacities()'
    );

    raise notice 'pg_cron: rebalance-firm-capacity scheduled every 15 minutes.';
  else
    raise notice
      'pg_cron is not installed; public.rebalance_firm_capacity exists but is '
      'only invoked by register_device.';
  end if;
end;
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 11. Grants: every new helper is internal; the RPCs keep their client shape.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

revoke all on function public.tier_seat_cap(text) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_seat_cap(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_associate_count(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_seated_count(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_owner_device_count(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_capacity_frozen(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_capacity_usage(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_capacity_needs_trim(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.firm_capacity_trim_due(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.device_cap(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;

revoke all on function public.join_firm(text) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.join_firm(text) to authenticated;

revoke all on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.register_device(text, text, text, text) to authenticated;

revoke all on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.remove_firm_member(uuid) to authenticated;

revoke all on function public.sign_out_firm_member(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.sign_out_firm_member(uuid) to authenticated;

revoke all on function public.admit_firm_member(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.admit_firm_member(uuid) to authenticated;

revoke all on function public.rebalance_firm_capacity(uuid, uuid)
  from public, anon, authenticated;
revoke all on function public.rebalance_all_firm_capacities()
  from public, anon, authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.645 — Owner-Designate Seats — A Chamber-Tier Buyer Keeps The Slots Before The Firm Exists

### 0.0.645 · `20261026130000_owner_designate_device_slots.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-26.** A chamber-tier account with no chamber — a Firm, Firm Plus or Enterprise owner-designate — now keeps the tier's full seat cap for its own devices (5 / 10 / 20) instead of falling to the one-per-member cap. A chamber owner still reads the slots left after associates; a seated associate 1; a capacity-signed-out associate 0; a non-chamber tier its own cap.

```sql
-- 2026-10-26 — A chamber-tier buyer keeps the seats they paid for before the
-- firm exists.
--
-- The paywall sells Firm / Firm Plus / Enterprise as "up to N devices
-- simultaneously or up to N-1 associates". A buyer who has not created the
-- chamber yet is still on their personal account, and `device_cap` fell through
-- to `tier_device_cap`, which answers 1 for every chamber tier (the per-member
-- rule). The buyer therefore saw "Devices 1 of 1" after paying for five.
--
-- An account with a chamber-tier plan and no firm is an **owner-designate**: it
-- reads the tier's full seat cap (Firm 5, Firm Plus 10, Enterprise 20) for its
-- own devices. Once it owns a firm the existing owner branch applies — the
-- slots left after associates; a seated associate still reads 1, a
-- capacity-signed-out associate 0, and non-chamber tiers keep their own caps.
--
-- Table class: `profiles`/`firms`/`firm_members` remain pull-only caches; this
-- is a server-side cap function only. No table, column or grant changes.

create or replace function public.device_cap(p_user_id uuid default auth.uid())
returns integer
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select case
           -- A chamber owner's devices share the chamber's remaining slots.
           when p.firm_id is not null
                and exists (
                  select 1
                    from public.firms f
                   where f.id = p.firm_id
                     and f.owner_id = p.id
                )
             then greatest(
               1,
               public.firm_seat_cap(p.firm_id) - public.firm_associate_count(p.firm_id)
             )
           -- A member signed out for capacity has no device until admitted.
           when p.firm_id is not null
                and exists (
                  select 1
                    from public.firm_members m
                   where m.firm_id = p.firm_id
                     and m.user_id = p.id
                     and m.capacity_signed_out_at is not null
                )
             then 0
           -- Every other chamber account: one device.
           when p.firm_id is not null then 1
           -- A chamber tier with no chamber yet is an owner-designate: it keeps
           -- the seats it paid for until an associate takes one. A non-chamber
           -- tier reads its own device cap.
           else coalesce(
             nullif(
               public.tier_seat_cap(
                 public.effective_tier(p.tier, p.tier_pending, p.tier_pending_from)
               ),
               0
             ),
             public.tier_device_cap(
               public.effective_tier(p.tier, p.tier_pending, p.tier_pending_from)
             )
           )
         end
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = p_user_id;
$$;

comment on function public.device_cap(uuid) is
  'The caller''s concurrent-device allowance: a chamber owner gets the slots left after associates (at least 1); a chamber-tier account with no chamber keeps the tier''s full seat cap (Firm 5, Firm Plus 10, Enterprise 20); a seated associate 1; a capacity-signed-out associate 0; a non-chamber tier its own cap.';
```

## App Version 0.0.675 — Delete Requests — The Requester's Name Travels With The Request

### 0.0.675 · `20261026140000_delete_requests_requester_name.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-26.** A delete request now carries the requester's name inside the row, so a reviewer reads who asked offline and from the first review instead of falling back to a neutral label when that colleague's profile is not in the reviewer's pull-only cache. The value is server-derived: a trigger fills requester_name from the profile of the row's own requested_by on both write paths, keeps the client's value only while that profile still holds no name, and the column is granted exactly like the rest of the row.

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The requester's name travels inside the request itself
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- A delete request exists to protect a chamber's owner from a member deleting
-- the chamber's data, and a request nobody can put a face to does not protect
-- anyone. Until now the reviewer's screen had to look the name up out of the
-- `profiles` cache on their own device, which is a pull-only cache and holds the
-- reader's own row — so the line read *A Firm Member* exactly when it mattered
-- most.
--
-- The name therefore becomes part of the request row: one nullable column,
-- written once by the requester and carried to every reviewer's device by the
-- ordinary pull, so it is readable offline from the first review.
--
-- It is **server-derived, not client-trusted**: the trigger below fills it from
-- `public.profiles` for the row's own `requested_by`, whatever the client sent,
-- because a request that names somebody is an attribution inside an audit trail
-- and the app must not be the authority on a colleague's name. A client value is
-- kept only when the profile still holds no name (a brand-new account), which is
-- strictly better than a blank.
--
-- Firm-shared and display-only, so it rides the ordinary push/pull row: nothing
-- in `sync_can_write` or the `delete_requests` policies changes.

alter table public.delete_requests
  add column if not exists requester_name text;

comment on column public.delete_requests.requester_name is
  'Display name of requested_by as the server recorded it when the request was '
  'written; server-derived from profiles by trigger, snapshot of the name at '
  'write time.';

-- Backfill the requests already in the queue: the profile is the only source for
-- a row that predates the column, and a request whose requester has since been
-- hard-deleted keeps the blank it has rather than a made-up name.
update public.delete_requests r
   set requester_name = nullif(btrim(p.full_name), '')
  from public.profiles p
 where p.id = r.requested_by
   and coalesce(r.requester_name, '') = ''
   and nullif(btrim(p.full_name), '') is not null;

-- The value is the server's to decide, on both write paths: `push_changes` writes
-- the row directly and a SECURITY DEFINER function would otherwise be the only
-- writer of a column that is also granted to clients.
create or replace function public.delete_requests_set_requester_name()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_name text;
begin
  select nullif(btrim(p.full_name), '')
    into v_name
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = new.requested_by;

  -- Definer rights, so this reads the profile regardless of the caller's own
  -- read scope. A missing or still-empty profile leaves whatever arrived in
  -- place, which is the requester's own best guess and never an invention.
  if v_name is not null then
    new.requester_name := v_name;
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

-- Trigger functions can only run as triggers, and the EXECUTE is closed anyway so
-- no signed-in account can reach it through PostgREST's RPC surface.
revoke all on function public.delete_requests_set_requester_name()
  from public, anon, authenticated;

drop trigger if exists delete_requests_set_requester_name
  on public.delete_requests;

create trigger delete_requests_set_requester_name
  before insert or update on public.delete_requests
  for each row
  execute function public.delete_requests_set_requester_name();

-- Column-level parity with the rest of the row: `20261015100000` revoked the
-- table-level write grants and granted back the columns that existed then, so a
-- column added afterwards is writable by name only if it says so here.
grant insert (requester_name), update (requester_name)
  on public.delete_requests
  to authenticated;
```

## App Version 0.0.684 — Delete Requests — A Rejection, A Refresh And A Withdrawal That Land

### 0.0.684 · `20261027100000_delete_request_review_firm_scope.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-27.** The delete-request rule reads the firm the row actually has. `push_changes` subtracts the scope columns from the row it hands `sync_can_write`, which is harmless for every other table (a trigger gates can_edit on the ten gated tables, and `enforce_delete_transition()` reads `old.firm_id`), but `delete_requests` has no permission trigger, so a reviewer's rejection, a requester's snapshot refresh and a withdrawal were all judged against a null firm and refused with `permission_denied` — the client rolled each one back and claimed the user's permissions had changed. The rule now reads the stored request's own firm_id when the row names none; nothing else in the function changes.

```sql
-- The delete-request rule reads the firm the row actually has.
--
-- `push_changes` subtracts the scope columns from the row it hands
-- `sync_can_write` (§3.3's "an existing row keeps the firm it has"). For every
-- other table that is harmless: `enforce_member_permission()` gates `can_edit`
-- on the ten gated tables, and `enforce_delete_transition()` reads `old.firm_id`
-- for the tombstone gate, so neither rule needs the firm in the row.
--
-- `delete_requests` has no permission trigger — raising a request must stay open
-- to every member, so `20261016100000` deliberately left the table out — which
-- made its update/delete branch the one rule the subtracted firm decided. Read
-- against a null firm, `can_delete_firm(null)` is false and the requester's own
-- `firm_id is not distinct from current_firm_id()` comparison is false too, so
-- **a reviewer's rejection, a requester's snapshot refresh and a withdrawal were
-- all refused with `permission_denied`** — the client rolls such a mutation back
-- from its pre-mutation snapshot, so the request returned to the review queue
-- and the app raised its "Your firm permissions changed" notice even though no
-- permission had changed. An approval was unaffected: that branch validates
-- `v_existing -> firm_id` and builds its own `v_final` with the firm intact.
--
-- The fix is one lookup: when the row names no firm, read the stored request's
-- own `firm_id` before answering. The comparison is by `id::text` against the
-- lower-cased id, so a malformed value cannot raise a cast error and the lookup
-- cannot become the thing that refuses a valid write. Everything else in the
-- function is the shipped body verbatim (`20261016100000`, which is the newest
-- of its three definitions), still SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/delete_request_review_test.sql`, which drives all
-- four decisions through `push_changes` as the roles the app uses.

create or replace function public.sync_can_write(
  p_table text,
  p_row jsonb,
  p_operation text
)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_is_reference boolean := p_table in (
    'court_categories', 'case_categories', 'courts', 'steps', 'case_types',
    'on_behalfs'
  );
  -- The firm a delete-request rule weighs: the row's own when it carries one,
  -- otherwise the stored request's.
  v_request_firm uuid;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    return false;
  end if;

  if p_operation = 'insert' then
    if p_table = 'delete_requests' then
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'requested_by')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
             is not distinct from public.current_firm_id();
    elsif v_is_reference then
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'is_custom')::boolean, false)
         and coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
                is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
         )
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or public.can_add_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
         );
    else
      return coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
                is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
         )
         and (
           p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
           or public.can_add_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
         );
    end if;
  end if;

  -- update / delete
  if p_table = 'delete_requests' then
    -- The requester may edit or withdraw their own request while it is pending,
    -- but only while the request's firm is still theirs: a removed requester must
    -- not be able to touch it. A member with delete permission may still review.
    --
    -- A review reaches this function without the firm in the row (see the file
    -- header), so the firm is taken from the request the payload names when the
    -- row itself has none. An update that names no such request — an id this
    -- table does not hold — stays unfirm and is refused, which is the safe
    -- direction: no caller may delete in a firm that cannot be read.
    v_request_firm := nullif(p_row ->> 'firm_id', '')::uuid;
    if v_request_firm is null then
      select d.firm_id into v_request_firm
        from public.delete_requests d
       where d.id::text = lower(nullif(p_row ->> 'id', ''));
    end if;

    return (
      coalesce((p_row ->> 'requested_by')::uuid, null) = v_actor
      and (p_row ->> 'status') = 'pending'
      and v_request_firm is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
    ) or public.can_delete_firm(v_request_firm);
  elsif v_is_reference then
    -- A built-in row has no creator and no firm; only a custom row is writable.
    if not coalesce((p_row ->> 'is_custom')::boolean, false) then
      return false;
    end if;
    return (
        coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
        and (
          p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
          or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
               is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
        )
      )
      or public.can_edit_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null));
  elsif p_table = 'conflict_log' then
    return coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor;
  else
    -- Authorship only counts while the row's firm is still the caller's firm: a
    -- removed member keeps their own personal rows but not the firm's.
    if not (
      (
        coalesce((p_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid, null) = v_actor
        and (
          p_row ->> 'firm_id' is null
          or coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null)
               is not distinct from public.current_firm_id()
        )
      )
      or public.can_edit_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null))
    ) then
      return false;
    end if;
    -- The delete transition additionally needs can_delete, mirroring
    -- enforce_delete_transition().
    if p_operation = 'delete' and (p_row ->> 'firm_id') is not null then
      return public.can_delete_firm(coalesce((p_row ->> 'firm_id')::uuid, null));
    end if;
    return true;
  end if;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.sync_can_write(text, jsonb, text) is
  'Explicit write re-check for push_changes: same rules as the Phase 4 RLS policies, evaluated on the row that would be written, plus the Phase 5 can_add gate on a create. A firm comparison uses `is not distinct from`, because `=` against a NULL current_firm_id would yield NULL and slip past an `if not`. Authorship of a firm-scoped row is honoured only while the row''s firm is still the caller''s firm, so a removed member cannot merge a queued write. An update is not gated here: enforce_member_permission() is the enforcement for can_edit, and it can be, because push_changes subtracts firm_id from the row it passes here — a rule that cannot see the firm cannot weigh can_edit. The one update rule that needs the firm anyway — delete_requests, whose table carries no permission trigger — reads the stored request''s firm_id when the row itself names none, so a review and a withdrawal are judged against the firm the request belongs to.';

-- The RPC's helper stays reachable by no client role directly: push_changes is
-- the only entry point, and it calls this as owner. `create or replace` keeps
-- the existing ACL; the revoke is restated so this file records the posture.
revoke all on function public.sync_can_write(text, jsonb, text)
  from public, anon, authenticated;
```

### 0.0.684 · `20261027110000_delete_request_withdrawal_exit.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-27.** A requester may withdraw their own pending delete request. The ordinary tombstone gate demands can_delete in the row's firm, and the member who raises a delete request is exactly the member without it, so the app's **Withdraw** action could never be applied once the request had reached the server. `enforce_delete_transition()` now excepts one carrying row — a delete request whose status is still pending and whose requested_by is the caller — which is the rule `delete_requests_update_scoped` already states; a decided request still cannot be withdrawn.

```sql
-- A requester may withdraw their own pending delete request.
--
-- `delete_requests` carries the ordinary tombstone gate from
-- `20260929102100`: a firm-scoped row may only be soft-deleted by the owner or a
-- member holding `can_delete`. That rule is right for chamber data and wrong for
-- this one row — a member with no `can_delete` is exactly the member who raises a
-- delete request, and the **Withdraw** action the app offers them is that row
-- toggled to `is_deleted`. So the button could never work once the request had
-- reached the server: the trigger refused it with `delete_not_permitted`, the
-- client rolled the withdrawal back, and the requester was told their firm
-- permissions had changed.
--
-- The exception below is the rule the shipped policy already states —
-- `delete_requests_update_scoped` grants the requester their own **still-pending**
-- row ("The requester edits their own still-pending request; a reviewer with
-- can_delete acts on it. Anything else is refused") — and the same rule
-- `sync_can_write`'s delete-request branch spells out for the RPC door. It is
-- keyed on `old.requested_by`, so a decided request cannot be withdrawn after the
-- fact, and on `old.status = 'pending'`, so a review that has already been
-- answered is never erased by the requester. Nothing else changes: every other
-- table, and every decided request, keeps the gate it had.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/delete_request_review_test.sql`.

create or replace function public.enforce_delete_transition()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  if old.is_deleted = false and new.is_deleted = true then
    -- Individual rows (no firm) are the creator's own; a firm row needs either
    -- the owner or a member holding can_delete. An associate without it must go
    -- through the delete-request workflow instead — and withdrawing their own
    -- request is that workflow's own exit, so it is allowed by the caller's own
    -- row rather than by a permission they do not have.
    if tg_table_name = 'delete_requests'
       and old.status = 'pending'
       and old.requested_by = auth.uid() then
      return new;
    end if;

    if not public.can_delete_firm(old.firm_id)
       and old.firm_id is not null then
      raise exception 'delete_not_permitted'
        using errcode = '42501',
              hint = 'Requires can_delete in this firm; raise a delete request instead.';
    end if;
  end if;
  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.enforce_delete_transition() is
  'BEFORE UPDATE on the twelve domain tables: refuses is_deleted true unless the caller may delete in the row''s firm (owner or can_delete), with one carrying row excepted — a requester''s own still-pending delete request, which the delete-request workflow lets them withdraw.';

-- The grants are untouched: `create or replace` keeps the function's ACL, and a
-- trigger function needs no EXECUTE privilege of its own.
```

### 0.0.684 · `20261027120000_delete_request_withdrawal_field_guard.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-27.** The withdrawal exit reads its two fields only on the table that has them. `20261027110000` wrote the exception as one condition, and `old.status` is resolved at run time on a generic record — so the other eleven tables the trigger guards, which have no `status` column, raised on every tombstone and could not delete at all. The rule is unchanged; the two `delete_requests` fields are read inside the table test, where nothing else can reach them. Caught by the two proofs that tombstone a case and a reference row.

```sql
-- The withdrawal exit reads its two fields only on the table that has them.
--
-- `20261027110000` added the requester's own-pending-request exit to
-- `enforce_delete_transition()`, but wrote it as one condition:

--     if tg_table_name = 'delete_requests'
--        and old.status = 'pending'
--        and old.requested_by = auth.uid() then

-- `old` is a generic record, so `old.status` is resolved at run time — and on
-- the other **eleven** tables the trigger guards there is no `status` column to
-- resolve, so the trigger raised `record "old" has no field "status"` on every
-- tombstone: a case, note, reference, history row or custom court could no
-- longer be deleted at all. Caught by the proofs, not by reading — the case
-- delete in `supabase/tests/push_changes_smoke_test.sql` and the reference
-- tombstones in `supabase/tests/firm_mode_reference_in_use_guard_test.sql` both
-- failed within a minute of the apply, which is exactly what those files exist
-- for.
--
-- The rule is unchanged and stays exactly as `20261027110000` states it; only
-- the way it reads the row changes: the two `delete_requests` fields are read
-- inside the table test, where nothing else can reach them.

create or replace function public.enforce_delete_transition()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
begin
  if old.is_deleted = false and new.is_deleted = true then
    -- Individual rows (no firm) are the creator's own; a firm row needs either
    -- the owner or a member holding can_delete. An associate without it must go
    -- through the delete-request workflow instead — and withdrawing their own
    -- request is that workflow's own exit, so it is allowed by the caller's own
    -- row rather than by a permission they do not have. `status` and
    -- `requested_by` exist on this one table only, which is why they are read
    -- inside the test rather than in the condition above it.
    if tg_table_name = 'delete_requests' then
      if old.status = 'pending' and old.requested_by = auth.uid() then
        return new;
      end if;
    end if;

    if not public.can_delete_firm(old.firm_id)
       and old.firm_id is not null then
      raise exception 'delete_not_permitted'
        using errcode = '42501',
              hint = 'Requires can_delete in this firm; raise a delete request instead.';
    end if;
  end if;
  return new;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.enforce_delete_transition() is
  'BEFORE UPDATE on the twelve domain tables: refuses is_deleted true unless the caller may delete in the row''s firm (owner or can_delete), with one carrying row excepted — a requester''s own still-pending delete request, which the delete-request workflow lets them withdraw. The exception reads status/requested_by inside the delete_requests test, because those columns exist on no other table this trigger guards.';
```
