### 0.0.684 · `20261027130000_push_changes_check_row_firm.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-27.** The permission verdict is weighed on the row as it exists. `push_changes_core` subtracts the scope columns before the write, and handed that same stripped row to `sync_can_write`, so every rule that needs the firm was weighed against a row with no firm: `can_edit_firm(null)` is false and the authorship clause decided alone — a chamber member could not edit a case, note or reference a colleague had authored, including the firm's owner, while `enforce_member_permission()` allows it because it reads `new.firm_id`. The check now receives `v_final` with the stored firm restored; the write still omits `firm_id`, so no payload can move a row between scopes. The body is the newest shipped one with that one statement changed.

```sql
-- The permission verdict is weighed on the row as it exists.
--
-- `push_changes_core` subtracts the scope columns from the row it is about to
-- write (§3.3's "an existing row keeps the firm it has"), and handed that same
-- stripped row to `sync_can_write`. Every rule that needs the firm was therefore
-- weighed against a row with no firm: `can_edit_firm(null)` is false, and the
-- authorship clause decided alone — so **a chamber member could not edit a case,
-- note or reference a colleague had authored, including the firm's owner**,
-- while `enforce_member_permission()` allows exactly that, because it reads
-- `new.firm_id` from the stored row. The delete-request rules were the same
-- defect in the other branch (`20261027100000`).
--
-- The fix is that one row: the check is handed the row as it exists, which means
-- the firm the write deliberately omits. The write itself still omits `firm_id`,
-- so no payload can move an existing row between scopes; the tombstone and
-- `can_delete` rules can now weigh the firm too, which is what
-- `enforce_delete_transition()` enforces at the trigger and what this function's
-- own comment claims. This is the newest shipped body (`20261015110000`) with no
-- other change.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/push_changes_smoke_test.sql` (the colleague-edit and
-- removed-member sections pin both directions) and by
-- `supabase/tests/delete_request_review_test.sql`.

create or replace function public.push_changes_core(rows jsonb)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  -- Read once: every insert in this batch is scoped to the caller's own firm,
  -- and a profile change mid-batch must not be able to split the batch's scope.
  v_firm_id uuid := public.current_firm_id();
  v_entitled boolean;
  v_n integer;
  v_results jsonb[];
  v_order integer[];
  v_idx integer;
  v_row jsonb;
  v_mutation_id text;
  v_entity_type text;
  v_entity_id text;
  v_operation text;
  v_table text;
  v_payload jsonb;
  v_base_version integer;
  v_existing jsonb;
  v_final jsonb;
  v_new_row jsonb;
  v_old_version integer;
  v_ms bigint;
  v_hash text;
  v_receipt public.mutation_receipts%rowtype;
  v_status text;
  v_error_code text;
  v_message text;
  v_result jsonb;
  v_cols text;
  v_vals text;
  v_bad integer;
  v_has_created_at boolean;
  v_prov jsonb;
  v_hist jsonb;
  v_hist_row jsonb;
  v_child jsonb;
  v_children jsonb;
  v_state text;
  v_msg text;
  -- Delete-review accumulators (Task 20 Phase 4).
  v_target jsonb;
  v_target_type text;
  v_target_table text;
  v_expected integer;
  v_req_status text;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- Batch invariant: the Flutter client always sends one JSON array.
  if rows is null or jsonb_typeof(rows) <> 'array' then
    raise exception 'push_changes: rows must be a JSON array'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  v_n := jsonb_array_length(rows);
  if v_n = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('results', '[]'::jsonb);
  end if;

  v_entitled := public.has_sync_entitlement(v_actor);
  v_ms := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;

  -- One slot per submitted row, so the response is exactly one result per
  -- mutation_id in input order even though processing follows dependency order.
  v_results := array_fill(null::jsonb, array[v_n]);

  select array_agg(i order by r, i)
    into v_order
    from (
      select i,
             public.sync_dependency_rank(
               coalesce(rows -> (i - 1) ->> 'entity_type', '')
             ) as r
        from generate_series(1, v_n) as i
    ) s;

  foreach v_idx in array v_order loop
    v_row := rows -> (v_idx - 1);

    -- Reset every per-mutation accumulator so nothing from the previous
    -- iteration can leak into this one's result.
    v_status := null;
    v_error_code := null;
    v_message := null;
    v_existing := null;
    v_final := null;
    v_new_row := null;
    v_children := null;
    v_hist_row := null;
    v_target := null;
    v_target_type := null;
    v_target_table := null;
    v_expected := null;
    v_req_status := null;

    v_mutation_id := nullif(v_row ->> 'mutation_id', '');
    v_entity_type := nullif(v_row ->> 'entity_type', '');
    v_entity_id := nullif(v_row ->> 'entity_id', '');
    v_operation := nullif(v_row ->> 'operation', '');

    if v_mutation_id is null or v_entity_type is null
       or v_entity_id is null or v_operation is null then
      raise exception
        'push_changes: every row needs mutation_id, entity_type, entity_id and operation'
        using errcode = '22023';
    end if;

    v_table := public.sync_entity_table(v_entity_type);
    v_hash := public.sha256_hex(v_row::text);

    -- Idempotency: a known mutation_id with the same canonical hash returns the
    -- original result and applies nothing; a different hash is refused.
    select * into v_receipt
      from public.mutation_receipts r
     where r.mutation_id = v_mutation_id;
    if found then
      if v_receipt.request_hash = v_hash then
        v_results[v_idx] := v_receipt.result_payload;
      else
        v_results[v_idx] := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', 'mutation_id_reused',
          'message', 'This mutation id was already used with a different payload.'
        );
      end if;
      continue;
    end if;

    -- The implicit savepoint for this logical mutation: a permanent failure
    -- rolls back only this block, while a receipt (written after the block) and
    -- every other mutation survive.
    begin
      if not v_entitled then
        v_status := 'rejected';
        v_error_code := 'entitlement_required';
        v_message := 'Online sync requires an active subscription.';
      elsif v_table is null then
        v_status := 'rejected';
        v_error_code := 'unknown_entity';
        v_message := format('Unknown entity type %s.', v_entity_type);
      else
        -- The scope columns are never taken from a payload (§3.3): `scope_owner_id`
        -- belongs to the dissolve, and `firm_id` is derived below on insert and
        -- preserved on an existing row. Stripping here is what makes both true
        -- for every path at once — insert, update, delete and the delete-review
        -- branch all read this one variable.
        v_payload := coalesce(v_row -> 'payload', '{}'::jsonb)
          - 'scope_owner_id' - 'firm_id';

        -- A payload key that is not a real column is a client validation error,
        -- never a silent no-op.
        select count(*) into v_bad
          from jsonb_object_keys(v_payload) k
         where not exists (
           select 1
             from pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
             join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = a.attrelid
             join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
            where n.nspname = 'public'
              and c.relname = v_table
              and a.attname = k
              and a.attnum > 0
              and a.attisdropped = false
         );
        if v_bad > 0 then
          raise exception 'unknown_column'
            using errcode = '42703',
                  hint = 'The payload names a column that does not exist on the server table.';
        end if;

        v_base_version := nullif(v_row ->> 'base_version', '')::int;

        if v_operation = 'insert' then
          -- Inserts require no existing row.
          execute format(
            'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
            v_table
          ) into v_existing using v_entity_id;

          if v_existing is not null then
            v_status := 'conflict';
            v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
            v_message := 'A row with this id already exists.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          else
            -- Server-owned columns are never taken from the client; the
            -- server_updated_at trigger stamps its own column.
            v_final := v_payload
              - 'server_updated_at' - 'version' - 'last_modified_by';
            if v_table = 'conflict_log' then
              -- The server column is a timestamptz defaulted to server now();
              -- the client's epoch-ms value must not be cast into it.
              v_final := v_final - 'created_at';
            end if;
            v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object(
              'version', 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text,
              -- §1: a chamber account holds chamber rows and nothing else, so a
              -- new row's firm is the caller's own — null for an individual, the
              -- chamber for a member. This is what makes firm mode work at all:
              -- the client's whole-row payload carries its local `firm_id`
              -- (null), and without this derivation a member's case landed as a
              -- personal row inside the chamber, invisible to everybody else.
              'firm_id', v_firm_id
            );
            -- Only a table whose `created_at` is an epoch-ms *integer* column may
            -- receive the fallback: the six reference tables have none, and
            -- `conflict_log.created_at` is a server-owned timestamptz that must
            -- take its own default rather than the client's milliseconds.
            select exists (
              select 1
                from pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
                join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = a.attrelid
                join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
               where n.nspname = 'public'
                 and c.relname = v_table
                 and a.attname = 'created_at'
                 and a.attnum > 0
                 and a.atttypid in ('int8'::regtype, 'int4'::regtype)
            ) into v_has_created_at;
            if v_has_created_at and v_final ->> 'created_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('created_at', v_ms);
            end if;
            if v_final ->> 'updated_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('updated_at', v_ms);
            end if;
            -- `insert ... select *` reads NULL for an absent key rather than
            -- the column default, so a soft-delete flag must be explicit.
            if v_final ->> 'is_deleted' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('is_deleted', false);
            end if;

            if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'insert') then
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message := 'The caller may not create this row.';
            else
              -- Only the columns the snapshot carries are named, so a column
              -- the payload omitted still gets its own default rather than
              -- NULL (jsonb_populate_record does not apply defaults).
              select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                     string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                into v_cols, v_vals
                from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k;

              execute format(
                'insert into public.%I (%s) select %s from '
                'jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v',
                v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
              ) using v_final;
              execute format(
                'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                v_table
              ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
              v_status := 'accepted';
            end if;
          end if;
        else
          -- Lock the target row first, then decide.
          execute format(
            'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1 for update',
            v_table
          ) into v_existing using v_entity_id;

          if v_existing is null then
            v_status := 'rejected';
            v_error_code := 'not_found';
            v_message := 'The row no longer exists on the server.';
          elsif (v_existing ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean = true
                and v_operation = 'update' then
            v_status := 'tombstone';
            v_error_code := 'tombstone';
            v_message := 'The row was deleted on the server.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          elsif (v_existing ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean = true
                and v_operation = 'delete' then
            v_status := 'already_resolved';
            v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
            v_message := 'The row was already deleted.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;

          -- -----------------------------------------------------------------
          -- Delete-review approval (Task 20 Phase 4). The request row is the
          -- one locked above; the target is locked next.
          -- -----------------------------------------------------------------
          elsif v_table = 'delete_requests'
                and (v_payload ->> 'status') = 'approved' then
            v_req_status := coalesce(v_existing ->> 'status', '');

            if v_req_status in ('approved', 'rejected') then
              -- Already decided: nothing to do, and no second tombstone.
              v_status := 'already_resolved';
              v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
              v_message := 'This request was already reviewed.';
              v_new_row := v_existing;
            elsif not public.can_delete_firm(
                    nullif(v_existing ->> 'firm_id', '')::uuid) then
              -- The requester cannot approve their own request: only a member
              -- with delete permission may review one.
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message :=
                'Only a member with delete permission may review this request.';
            elsif v_base_version is null
                  or v_base_version <> (v_existing ->> 'version')::int then
              v_status := 'conflict';
              v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
              v_message := 'The request changed since this decision was made.';
              v_new_row := v_existing;
            else
              v_target_type := nullif(v_existing ->> 'entity_type', '');
              v_target_table := public.sync_entity_table(v_target_type);
              v_expected := nullif(v_existing ->> 'target_base_version', '')::int;

              if v_target_table is null or v_target_table not in (
                'cases', 'case_history', 'notes', 'case_references'
              ) then
                v_status := 'rejected';
                v_error_code := 'unsupported_target';
                v_message :=
                  'This request names a record that cannot be deleted here.';
              else
                execute format(
                  'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1 for update',
                  v_target_table
                ) into v_target using (v_existing ->> 'entity_id');

                if v_target is null
                   or coalesce((v_target ->> 'is_deleted')::boolean, false) then
                  -- Nothing left to approve. The request is untouched audit
                  -- history; the tombstone rides back for the reviewer.
                  v_status := 'already_resolved';
                  v_error_code := 'already_resolved';
                  v_message := 'The record was already deleted.';
                  v_new_row := v_existing;
                elsif coalesce(v_target ->> 'firm_id', '')
                      is distinct from coalesce(v_existing ->> 'firm_id', '') then
                  v_status := 'rejected';
                  v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                  v_message := 'The record is not in this request''s firm.';
                elsif v_expected is null
                      or v_expected <> (v_target ->> 'version')::int then
                  -- The record moved under the request: park the request as
                  -- stale and adopt the version the reviewer just saw, so a
                  -- reconfirm re-decides against the row that exists now.
                  v_final := (v_existing || jsonb_build_object(
                      'status', 'stale_review_required',
                      'target_base_version', (v_target ->> 'version')::int,
                      'updated_at', v_ms,
                      'version', (v_existing ->> 'version')::int + 1,
                      'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
                    )) - 'server_updated_at';

                  if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'update') then
                    v_status := 'rejected';
                    v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                    v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
                  else
                    select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                           string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                      into v_cols, v_vals
                      from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
                     where k <> 'server_updated_at';

                    execute format(
                      'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                      'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                      'where t.id = $2',
                      v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
                    ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

                    execute format(
                      'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                      v_table
                    ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
                    v_status := 'target_conflict';
                    v_error_code := 'target_conflict';
                    v_message :=
                      'The record changed since this request was made.';
                  end if;
                else
                  -- Reconfirmed against the row that exists now: tombstone the
                  -- target in this same savepoint.
                  execute format(
                    'update public.%I t set is_deleted = true, '
                    '  version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
                    '  last_modified_by = $1, updated_at = $2 '
                    'where t.id = $3 returning to_jsonb(t)',
                    v_target_table
                  ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, (v_existing ->> 'entity_id')
                  into v_target;

                  -- The same cascade an ordinary case delete performs, so an
                  -- approved request cannot leave live children behind. The
                  -- request stores the singular `entity_type` ('case'), so the
                  -- test is against the resolved *table* ('cases').
                  if v_target_table = 'cases' then
                    v_children := '[]'::jsonb;
                    for v_child in execute format(
                      'update public.case_history t '
                      'set is_deleted = true, '
                      '    version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
                      '    last_modified_by = $1, '
                      '    updated_at = $2 '
                      'where t.case_id = $3 and t.is_deleted = false '
                      'returning to_jsonb(t)'
                    ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, (v_existing ->> 'entity_id')
                    loop
                      v_children := v_children || jsonb_build_array(v_child);
                    end loop;
                  end if;

                  -- Resolve the request beside the tombstone.
                  v_final := (v_existing || jsonb_build_object(
                      'status', 'approved',
                      'reviewed_by', v_actor::text,
                      'review_note', coalesce(
                        v_payload ->> 'review_note',
                        v_existing ->> 'review_note'),
                      'updated_at', v_ms,
                      'version', (v_existing ->> 'version')::int + 1,
                      'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
                    )) - 'server_updated_at';

                  if not public.sync_can_write(v_table, v_final, 'update') then
                    v_status := 'rejected';
                    v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
                    v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
                  else
                    select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                           string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                      into v_cols, v_vals
                      from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
                     where k <> 'server_updated_at';

                    execute format(
                      'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                      'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                      'where t.id = $2',
                      v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
                    ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

                    execute format(
                      'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                      v_table
                    ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
                    v_status := 'accepted';
                  end if;
                end if;
              end if;
            end if;
          elsif v_base_version is null
                or v_base_version <> (v_existing ->> 'version')::int then
            v_status := 'conflict';
            v_error_code := 'version_conflict';
            v_message := 'The server version changed since this edit was made.';
            v_new_row := v_existing;
          else
            v_old_version := (v_existing ->> 'version')::int;
            -- `firm_id` is subtracted as well: an existing row keeps the firm it
            -- has, whatever the payload named, so no update can move a case out
            -- of the chamber it belongs to (§3.3).
            v_final := (v_existing || v_payload)
              - 'server_updated_at' - 'version' - 'last_modified_by' - 'firm_id';
            if v_table = 'conflict_log' then
              v_final := v_final - 'created_at';
            end if;
            v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object(
              'version', v_old_version + 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text
            );
            if v_operation = 'delete' then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('is_deleted', true);
            end if;
            if v_final ->> 'updated_at' is null then
              v_final := v_final || jsonb_build_object('updated_at', v_ms);
            end if;

            -- The verdict is weighed on the row as it exists: `v_final`
            -- has had its firm subtracted for the write below, and a rule
            -- that cannot see the firm cannot weigh `can_edit` — this is
            -- the same row `enforce_member_permission()` sees. A null firm
            -- here is an individual's own row, exactly as before.
            if not public.sync_can_write(
                 v_table,
                 v_final || jsonb_build_object('firm_id', v_existing -> 'firm_id'),
                 v_operation
               ) then
              v_status := 'rejected';
              v_error_code := 'permission_denied';
              v_message := 'The caller may not write this row.';
            else
              -- Update every column the final snapshot carries, except
              -- server_updated_at, which the trigger owns.
              -- Both lists are ordered by the same key, so the columns and
              -- their values can never fall out of step.
              select string_agg(quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k),
                     string_agg('v.' || quote_ident(k), ', ' order by k)
                into v_cols, v_vals
                from jsonb_object_keys(v_final) k
               where k <> 'server_updated_at';

              execute format(
                'update public.%I t set (%s) = (%s) '
                'from jsonb_populate_record(null::public.%I, $1) v '
                'where t.id = $2',
                v_table, v_cols, v_vals, v_table
              ) using v_final, v_entity_id;

              execute format(
                'select to_jsonb(t) from public.%I t where t.id = $1',
                v_table
              ) into v_new_row using v_entity_id;
              v_status := 'accepted';
            end if;
          end if;
        end if;

        -- Atomic history and cascade soft-delete, only on an accepted case
        -- mutation. A delete-request approval whose target is a case performs
        -- its own cascade inside the branch above, so this stays case-only.
        if v_status = 'accepted' and v_table = 'cases' then
          if v_operation = 'delete' then
            -- One accepted case delete soft-deletes its children in this same
            -- savepoint; the changed children ride back to the caller.
            v_children := '[]'::jsonb;
            for v_child in execute format(
              'update public.case_history t '
              'set is_deleted = true, '
              '    version = coalesce(t.version, 1) + 1, '
              '    last_modified_by = $1, '
              '    updated_at = $2 '
              'where t.case_id = $3 and t.is_deleted = false '
              'returning to_jsonb(t)'
            ) using v_actor::text, v_ms, v_entity_id
            loop
              v_children := v_children || jsonb_build_array(v_child);
            end loop;
          elsif v_operation = 'update'
                and (v_final ->> 'next_date') is distinct from
                    (v_existing ->> 'next_date') then
            -- The client's provisional preview supplies its identity so the
            -- authoritative event replaces it one-for-one.
            v_prov := v_row -> 'provisional_history';
            if v_prov is null or jsonb_typeof(v_prov) <> 'object' then
              v_prov := '{}'::jsonb;
            end if;

            v_hist := v_prov || jsonb_build_object(
              'id', coalesce(v_prov ->> 'id', gen_random_uuid()::text),
              'case_id', v_entity_id,
              'user_id', v_new_row -> 'user_id',
              'firm_id', v_new_row -> 'firm_id',
              'source_mutation_id',
                coalesce(v_prov ->> 'source_mutation_id', v_mutation_id),
              'created_by', v_actor,
              'base_case_version',
                coalesce(nullif(v_prov ->> 'base_case_version', '')::int,
                         v_old_version),
              'result_case_version', (v_new_row ->> 'version')::int,
              'version', 1,
              'last_modified_by', v_actor::text,
              'is_deleted', false,
              'updated_at', v_ms
            );
            -- Nothing the client omitted is invented: the previous values come
            -- from the authoritative base row.
            if v_hist ->> 'hearing_date' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'hearing_date',
                coalesce(nullif(v_existing ->> 'next_date', '')::bigint, v_ms)
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'last_step' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'last_step', v_existing -> 'last_step'
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'note_result' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'note_result', v_existing -> 'notes_results'
              );
            end if;
            if v_hist ->> 'result' is null then
              v_hist := v_hist || jsonb_build_object(
                'result', v_existing -> 'result'
              );
            end if;

            execute format(
              'insert into public.case_history select * from '
              'jsonb_populate_record(null::public.case_history, $1)'
            ) using v_hist;

            -- Hand the authoritative row back so the client can reconcile its
            -- provisional preview (same id) in one write.
            execute format(
              'select to_jsonb(t) from public.case_history t where t.id = $1'
            ) into v_hist_row using v_hist ->> 'id';
          end if;
        end if;
      end if;

      -- Terminal result for this mutation.
      if v_status = 'accepted' then
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'accepted',
          'version', (v_new_row ->> 'version')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'children', coalesce(v_children, '[]'::jsonb),
          'history', v_hist_row,
          -- A delete-request approval carries the target it tombstoned, so the
          -- reviewer's client can apply the record's disappearance in one pass.
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type
        );
      elsif v_status = 'target_conflict' then
        -- The request was parked as stale_review_required; hand back both rows
        -- so the reviewer can inspect the record that exists now.
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'target_conflict',
          'version', nullif(v_new_row ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type,
          'target_version', nullif(v_target ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'error_code', v_error_code,
          'message', v_message
        );
      elsif v_status in ('conflict', 'tombstone', 'already_resolved') then
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', v_status,
          'version', nullif(v_new_row ->> 'version', '')::int,
          'row', v_new_row,
          'target', v_target,
          'target_entity_type', v_target_type,
          'error_code', v_error_code,
          'message', v_message
        );
      else
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', coalesce(v_error_code, 'validation_failed'),
          'message', coalesce(v_message, 'The mutation was refused.')
        );
      end if;
    exception
      when others then
        get stacked diagnostics
          v_state = returned_sqlstate,
          v_msg = message_text;
        -- A permanent, per-mutation failure is caught and reported; anything
        -- else is infrastructure and aborts the whole RPC.
        if v_state not in (
          '42501', 'P0001', '23502', '23503', '23505', '23514',
          '22P02', '22007', '22003', '42804', '42703'
        ) then
          raise;
        end if;
        v_result := jsonb_build_object(
          'mutation_id', v_mutation_id,
          'entity_type', v_entity_type,
          'entity_id', v_entity_id,
          'operation', v_operation,
          'status', 'rejected',
          'error_code', case v_state
            when '42501' then 'permission_denied'
            when 'P0001' then 'entitlement_required'
            else 'validation_failed'
          end,
          'message', v_msg
        );
    end;

    -- Receipt for every terminal result, in the same transaction. It is written
    -- after the savepoint block so a per-mutation rejection still records one.
    insert into public.mutation_receipts (
      mutation_id, actor_id, entity_type, entity_id, request_hash,
      terminal_status, result_payload
    ) values (
      v_mutation_id, v_actor, v_entity_type, v_entity_id, v_hash,
      v_result ->> 'status', v_result
    )
    on conflict (mutation_id) do nothing;

    v_results[v_idx] := v_result;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object('results', (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(v_results[k] order by k), '[]'::jsonb)
      from generate_subscripts(v_results, 1) as k
  ));
end;
$$;

comment on function public.push_changes_core(jsonb) is
  'Single atomic push pipeline: optimistic concurrency, per-mutation savepoints, idempotent receipts, authoritative case history and cascade soft-deletes, and the delete-review approval branch (locking, target_conflict/stale_review_required, already_resolved, atomic tombstone). The scope columns belong to the server: an insert takes its firm_id from current_firm_id(), an existing row keeps the firm it has, and scope_owner_id is never taken from a payload. The permission check beside each write is handed the row as it exists — including the firm the write itself omits — so can_edit and can_delete are weighed against the chamber the row is actually in.';

comment on function public.sync_can_write(text, jsonb, text) is
  'Explicit write re-check for push_changes: same rules as the Phase 4 RLS policies, evaluated on the row that would be written, plus the Phase 5 can_add gate on a create. A firm comparison uses `is not distinct from`, because `=` against a NULL current_firm_id would yield NULL and slip past an `if not`. Authorship of a firm-scoped row is honoured only while the row''s firm is still the caller''s firm, so a removed member cannot merge a queued write. The verdict is weighed on the row as it exists — push_changes hands this function the stored firm for an update or a delete — because a rule that cannot see the firm cannot weigh can_edit or can_delete; and a delete_requests row resolves its firm from the stored request when the row names none, so the rule holds even for a caller that stripped it.';
```

## App Version 0.0.685 — Delete Requests — A Request No Longer Outlives Its Record

### 0.0.685 · `20261028100000_delete_request_target_closure.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-28.** A delete request whose record someone else deleted closes itself. Nothing watched the record: a member with `can_delete` could delete the case a colleague had already asked about, and the request stayed pending for ever — in every reviewer's queue as work that could never succeed, in the requester's list as "waiting", clearable only by rejecting it, which records a decision that never happened. A trigger function on the four tables a request may name (`cases`, `case_history`, `notes`, `case_references`) now closes every still-open request for a tombstoned row as `already_deleted`, in the same transaction as the deletion, stamped by the deleter; an approval still ends approved because it writes after the tombstone it causes. The same migration backfills requests already left hanging and adds a partial unique index for at most one open request per record, so two colleagues can no longer queue two rows that end in one deletion and one pointless approval.

```sql
-- A delete request whose record someone else deleted closes itself.
--
-- The gap this closes: a request is a request to delete *a record*, but nothing
-- watched the record. A member holding `can_delete` could delete the case a
-- colleague had already asked about, and the request stayed `pending` for ever.
-- It then sat in every reviewer's queue as something that could never succeed:
-- an approval found the target already tombstoned and answered
-- `already_resolved` while leaving the request exactly as it was, so the row
-- came straight back to the queue, and the requester's own list still said
-- "waiting". The only way out was to **reject** it, which recorded a decision
-- that never happened.
--
-- The rule below is the honest one: when a record a request names is tombstoned,
-- the request is answered by that fact. It becomes `already_deleted`, which is a
-- terminal state (the client reads it as a decided request, so it leaves the
-- queue and the requester is told), and the write happens in the same
-- transaction as the deletion, so every device learns it through the ordinary
-- pull whether or not anyone opens the review screen.
--
-- It is a trigger rather than another branch inside `push_changes_core` because
-- that function is regenerated whole by each migration that touches it, and this
-- rule belongs to the table, not to one RPC: a deletion made by any path — the
-- app's push, a direct admin edit, a future RPC — closes the request the same
-- way. The approval path keeps working untouched: an approval tombstones the
-- target *before* it writes `status = 'approved'`, so the approval's own write is
-- the last one and the request ends approved, not already_deleted.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/delete_request_closure_test.sql`.

create or replace function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_entity_type text;
  v_ms bigint;
begin
  -- An AFTER trigger that only cares about a tombstone being created.
  if not (old.is_deleted = false and new.is_deleted = true) then
    return null;
  end if;

  -- The singular entity type a request stores for the table that changed. The
  -- four tables are the only ones `delete_requests` may name.
  v_entity_type := case tg_table_name
    when 'cases' then 'case'
    when 'case_history' then 'case_history'
    when 'notes' then 'note'
    when 'case_references' then 'reference'
  end;

  if v_entity_type is null then
    return null;
  end if;

  v_ms := (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint;

  -- Only requests still open are closed; a decided one is audit history and is
  -- never rewritten. The firm comparison keeps the rule inside the chamber that
  -- owns the record, exactly as the approval branch does.
  update public.delete_requests r
     set status = 'already_deleted',
         version = r.version + 1,
         updated_at = v_ms,
         last_modified_by = coalesce(new.last_modified_by, r.last_modified_by)
   where r.entity_type = v_entity_type
     and r.entity_id = new.id
     and r.is_deleted = false
     and r.status in ('pending', 'stale_review_required')
     and r.firm_id is not distinct from new.firm_id;

  return null;
end;
$$;

comment on function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target() is
  'AFTER UPDATE OF is_deleted on the four records a delete request may name: closes every still-open request for that row as already_deleted, in the same transaction as the tombstone, so a request never outlives its record. A decided request is never rewritten, and an approved request still ends approved because the approval writes last.';

revoke all on function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target()
  from public, anon, authenticated;

drop trigger if exists cases_close_delete_requests on public.cases;
create trigger cases_close_delete_requests
  after update of is_deleted on public.cases
  for each row
  execute function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target();

drop trigger if exists case_history_close_delete_requests
  on public.case_history;
create trigger case_history_close_delete_requests
  after update of is_deleted on public.case_history
  for each row
  execute function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target();

drop trigger if exists notes_close_delete_requests on public.notes;
create trigger notes_close_delete_requests
  after update of is_deleted on public.notes
  for each row
  execute function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target();

drop trigger if exists case_references_close_delete_requests
  on public.case_references;
create trigger case_references_close_delete_requests
  after update of is_deleted on public.case_references
  for each row
  execute function public.close_delete_requests_for_deleted_target();

-- Requests already left hanging by the old behaviour: the record it names is
-- tombstoned, so close them now rather than waiting for a reviewer to press a
-- button that cannot work.
--
-- A tombstoned row is required rather than a merely absent one. A request can be
-- pushed before the record it names (two queue entries, no ordering between
-- them), so "the row is not here" is not proof that it was deleted — only
-- `is_deleted = true` is.
update public.delete_requests r
   set status = 'already_deleted',
       version = r.version + 1,
       updated_at = (extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000)::bigint
 where r.is_deleted = false
   and r.status in ('pending', 'stale_review_required')
   and (
     (r.entity_type = 'case'
       and exists (
         select 1 from public.cases t
          where t.id = r.entity_id and t.is_deleted = true
       ))
     or (r.entity_type = 'case_history'
       and exists (
         select 1 from public.case_history t
          where t.id = r.entity_id and t.is_deleted = true
       ))
     or (r.entity_type = 'note'
       and exists (
         select 1 from public.notes t
          where t.id = r.entity_id and t.is_deleted = true
       ))
     or (r.entity_type = 'reference'
       and exists (
         select 1 from public.case_references t
          where t.id = r.entity_id and t.is_deleted = true
       ))
   );

-- One open request per record. Two colleagues asking about the same case used to
-- create two rows for one deletion: the first approval removed the record and the
-- second became permanently pointless. Partial (not a table constraint) because
-- decided and withdrawn rows are history and may repeat.
create unique index if not exists delete_requests_one_open_per_target
  on public.delete_requests (entity_type, entity_id)
  where is_deleted = false
    and status in ('pending', 'stale_review_required');

comment on index public.delete_requests_one_open_per_target is
  'At most one open (pending or stale) delete request per record; decided and withdrawn rows are audit history and are not constrained.';
```

## App Version 0.0.713 — Firm Devices — The Owner Sees Every Slot In Use

### 0.0.713 · `20261029100000_firm_device_list.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-29.** The chamber owner can see every device sharing the firm's slots. `device_state()` answers for the caller's own session, so the owner's Devices screen could only list the owner's phones while the other holders of the shared slots stayed invisible to the one person who manages them — and `user_devices` grants no read to any client role. `firm_device_list()` returns the chamber's slots, its associate count and every active device whose profile still points at that chamber, each with the member's current profile name, the registration snapshot as the fallback, `is_owner` and `is_current`. Owner-only: an associate or an individual reads `not_owner`, and nothing here writes.

```sql
-- The chamber owner can see every device sharing the firm's slots.
--
-- The gap this closes: `device_state()` answers for the caller's own session,
-- so an owner's Devices screen could only ever list the owner's own phones. The
-- chamber's slots are shared (`associates + owner devices <= slots`), and the
-- other holders of those slots were invisible to the one person who manages
-- them. `user_devices` is server-managed and grants no read to any client role,
-- so this function is the only way the owner's screen can name who holds a
-- slot — the same reason `device_state()` exists for a single device.
--
-- Owner-only and read-only: an associate keeps `device_state()` (their own
-- sign-in), an individual gets `not_owner`, and nothing here writes. The names
-- come from `profiles` (the account's current name) with the registration
-- snapshot on the device row as the fallback, so a renamed account does not
-- read stale on the owner's screen; only a row whose profile still points at
-- this chamber is listed, which is what keeps a removed member's devices out.
--
-- Proven by `supabase/tests/firm_device_list_test.sql`.

create or replace function public.firm_device_list()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm uuid := public.current_firm_id();
  v_owner uuid;
begin
  if v_user is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select f.owner_id into v_owner
    from public.firms f
   where f.id = v_firm;

  if v_owner is distinct from v_user then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'ok',
    'slots', public.firm_seat_cap(v_firm),
    -- The seat count the screen's shared-slots note reads, so it does not need
    -- the roster as well.
    'associates', (
      select count(*)::integer
        from public.firm_members m
       where m.firm_id = v_firm
         and m.user_id <> v_owner
    ),
    'devices', coalesce(
      (
        select jsonb_agg(
                 jsonb_build_object(
                   'id', d.id,
                   'label', d.label,
                   'platform', d.platform,
                   'last_seen_at', d.last_seen_at,
                   'is_current', d.session_id = public.current_session_id(),
                   'is_owner', d.user_id = v_owner,
                   'member_name', coalesce(
                     nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(p.full_name), ''),
                     nullif(pg_catalog.btrim(d.full_name), ''),
                     ''
                   )
                 )
                 -- The owner's own devices first, then the associates', each
                 -- group newest contact first: the order the two sections draw.
                 order by (d.user_id = v_owner) desc, d.last_seen_at desc
               )
          from public.user_devices d
          join public.profiles p
            on p.id = d.user_id
           and p.firm_id = v_firm
         where d.revoked_at is null
      ),
      '[]'::jsonb
    )
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.firm_device_list() is
  'The chamber owner''s whole device picture: active devices of the owner and of every associate whose profile still points at the chamber, each with its member name and is_owner, plus the chamber''s slots and associate count. Owner-only; a member or an individual reads not_owner.';

revoke all on function public.firm_device_list() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.firm_device_list() to authenticated;
```

## Manual SQL — Applied Outside The Migration Tool

> **These statements are not applied by the migration tool.** `storage.objects` is owned by `supabase_storage_admin`, which the migration role (`postgres`) is not a member of, so a storage policy cannot be created by a migration or through the MCP. They are created once in Supabase's Storage policy editor, and recorded here because this ledger is the whole record of the SQL this project runs.

### Manual · `storage_policies.sql`

> **Created 2026-10-25.** The eight storage policies for the profile-picture and chamber-logo buckets. `storage.objects` is owned by `supabase_storage_admin`, which the migration role is not a member of, so these are created once in the Supabase Storage policy editor instead.

```sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- Storage policies — applied through the Supabase Storage policy editor.
--
-- **Why this file is not a migration.** `storage.objects` is owned by
-- `supabase_storage_admin`. The migration role (`postgres`) is neither its owner
-- nor a member of that role, so `create policy` fails in the migrations, in the
-- psql applier and through the MCP's SQL. Supabase's Storage policy editor does
-- run with the required rights, so these eight policies are created there once.
--
-- **When.** After both migrations are applied:
--   20261025120000_firm_logo_storage.sql
--   20261025180000_profile_avatar_storage.sql
-- The migrations create the buckets, the helper functions and the version
-- triggers; these policies are what let the app read and write the objects.
--
-- **How.** Supabase Dashboard → Storage → Policies. For each block below create
-- a policy on `storage.objects` with:
--   * the given name and operation,
--   * role `authenticated`,
--   * the USING and/or WITH CHECK expression shown.
-- A SQL editor that runs with the storage admin's rights can execute the
-- `create policy` statement directly. Each block drops its own name first, so a
-- re-run is safe.
--
-- This file is included in `supabase/AllSupabaseSql.md` as a labelled manual
-- section. It is not applied by `tool/apply_supabase_migrations.dart`.
--
-- **The editor adds a SELECT policy beside each UPDATE and DELETE policy.** The
-- Storage API reads a row before it updates or removes it, so the editor creates
-- a matching SELECT policy (e.g. `... _1`) automatically. Those are permissive
-- and therefore redundant with the bucket's SELECT policy, not a restriction;
-- leave them in place. The live policy names also carry a random suffix, which
-- is cosmetic. Both proofs were run against the live project on 2026-10-25 and
-- printed FIRM LOGO OK and PROFILE AVATAR OK.
-- ===========================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Chamber logos — bucket `firm-avatars`, object `{firm_id}.jpg`
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- 1. firm_logo_select_member — SELECT
--    Any member of the chamber may read its logo; a lapsed chamber keeps it.
drop policy if exists firm_logo_select_member on storage.objects;
create policy firm_logo_select_member on storage.objects
  for select to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'firm-avatars'
    and name = public.current_firm_id()::text || '.jpg'
  );

-- 2. firm_logo_insert_owner — INSERT
--    Only the owner of a chamber whose plan is live may add its logo.
drop policy if exists firm_logo_insert_owner on storage.objects;
create policy firm_logo_insert_owner on storage.objects
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'firm-avatars'
    and name = public.current_firm_id()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_firm_logo()
  );

-- 3. firm_logo_update_owner — UPDATE
--    A replace is an UPDATE, so the old and the new row must both satisfy it.
drop policy if exists firm_logo_update_owner on storage.objects;
create policy firm_logo_update_owner on storage.objects
  for update to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'firm-avatars'
    and name = public.current_firm_id()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_firm_logo()
  )
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'firm-avatars'
    and name = public.current_firm_id()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_firm_logo()
  );

-- 4. firm_logo_delete_owner — DELETE
--    Removing the logo stays possible after a lapse, so the owner can clean up.
drop policy if exists firm_logo_delete_owner on storage.objects;
create policy firm_logo_delete_owner on storage.objects
  for delete to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'firm-avatars'
    and name = public.current_firm_id()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.is_firm_owner(public.current_firm_id())
  );

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Individual profile pictures — bucket `individual-avatars`, object
-- `{user_id}.jpg`
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- 5. profile_avatar_select_owner — SELECT
--    The holder reads their own picture, including after a lapse.
drop policy if exists profile_avatar_select_owner on storage.objects;
create policy profile_avatar_select_owner on storage.objects
  for select to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'individual-avatars'
    and name = auth.uid()::text || '.jpg'
  );

-- 6. profile_avatar_insert_owner — INSERT
--    Only a premium individual or a premium chamber owner may add one.
drop policy if exists profile_avatar_insert_owner on storage.objects;
create policy profile_avatar_insert_owner on storage.objects
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'individual-avatars'
    and name = auth.uid()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_profile_avatar()
  );

-- 7. profile_avatar_update_owner — UPDATE
--    A replace is an UPDATE; both the old and the new row satisfy the rule.
drop policy if exists profile_avatar_update_owner on storage.objects;
create policy profile_avatar_update_owner on storage.objects
  for update to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'individual-avatars'
    and name = auth.uid()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_profile_avatar()
  )
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'individual-avatars'
    and name = auth.uid()::text || '.jpg'
    and public.can_write_profile_avatar()
  );

-- 8. profile_avatar_delete_owner — DELETE
--    The holder can always remove their own picture, including after a lapse.
drop policy if exists profile_avatar_delete_owner on storage.objects;
create policy profile_avatar_delete_owner on storage.objects
  for delete to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'individual-avatars'
    and name = auth.uid()::text || '.jpg'
  );
```
